    /**
     * A self-signed certificate with its key, packed as a `.pfx` with a password:
     * what an A1 file looks like. Only for tests. The CNPJ goes in the name, as
     * ICP-Brasil writes it (`RAZAO SOCIAL:CNPJ`).
     */
    export function testPfx({
      name = "ACADEMIA TESTE LTDA:48240052000161",
      password = "senha-de-teste",
      from = new Date("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
      until = new Date("2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
      withKey = true,
      bits = 1024,
    }: { name?: string; password?: string; from?: Date; until?: Date; withKey?: boolean; bits?: number } = {}): Uint8Array {
      // 1024 keeps the tests fast; a TLS handshake needs 2048.
      const keys = forge.pki.rsa.generateKeyPair({ bits, e: 0x10001 });
      const certificate = forge.pki.createCertificate();
      certificate.publicKey = keys.publicKey;
      certificate.serialNumber = "01";
      certificate.validity.notBefore = from;
      certificate.validity.notAfter = until;
      const subject = [{ name: "commonName", value: name }];
      certificate.setSubject(subject);
      certificate.setIssuer(subject);
      certificate.sign(keys.privateKey, forge.md.sha256.create());
      const asn1 = forge.pkcs12.toPkcs12Asn1(withKey ? keys.privateKey : null, [certificate], password, { algorithm: "3des" });
      return new Uint8Array(Buffer.from(forge.asn1.toDer(asn1).getBytes(), "binary"));
    }
    
    /** A certificate for `localhost`, with its key in PEM: the stand-in for a server the system talks to over TLS. */
    export function serverIdentity(): { key: string; cert: string } {
      const keys = forge.pki.rsa.generateKeyPair({ bits: 2048, e: 0x10001 });
      const certificate = forge.pki.createCertificate();
      certificate.publicKey = keys.publicKey;
      certificate.serialNumber = "03";
      certificate.validity.notBefore = new Date(Date.now() - 86_400_000);
      certificate.validity.notAfter = new Date(Date.now() + 86_400_000);
      const name = [{ name: "commonName", value: "localhost" }];
      certificate.setSubject(name);
      certificate.setIssuer(name);
      certificate.setExtensions([{ name: "subjectAltName", altNames: [{ type: 2, value: "localhost" }] }, { name: "basicConstraints", cA: true }]);
      certificate.sign(keys.privateKey, forge.md.sha256.create());
      return { key: forge.pki.privateKeyToPem(keys.privateKey), cert: forge.pki.certificateToPem(certificate) };
    }

    export function fixed(value: string, scale: number, wholeDigits: number): string {
      const match = /^(\d+)(?:[.,](\d+))?$/.exec(value.trim())
      if (!match || (match[2]?.length ?? 0) > scale) throw new Error(`Informe um decimal positivo com até ${scale} casas`)
      const whole = BigInt(match[1]).toString()
      if (whole.length > wholeDigits) throw new Error("Valor acima do limite fiscal")
      return `${whole}.${(match[2] || "").padEnd(scale, "0")}`
    }

    ---
    title: Server and Client Components
    description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.
    related:
      title: Next Steps
      description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.
      links:
        - app/api-reference/directives/use-client
        - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary
    ---
    
    By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.
    
    This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.
    
    > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).

    impl DraftItem {
        pub fn commercial_total(&self) -> Result<i128, DomainError> {
            let gross = exact_decimal(&self.gross_total, 13, 2)?;
            let freight = exact_decimal(self.freight_amount.as_deref().unwrap_or("0.00"), 13, 2)?;
            let discount = exact_decimal(self.discount_amount.as_deref().unwrap_or("0.00"), 13, 2)?;
            let net = gross + freight - discount;

    /** Sum item-rounded figures, preserving gross products, freight and discount separately. */
    export function nfeTotals(input: NfeInput): NfeTotals {
      const sum = (pick: (figures: ItemFigures) => number) => roundCents(input.items.reduce((total, item) => total + pick(figuresOf(item, input)), 0));
      const products = sum((figures) => figures.product);
      const ipi = sum((figures) => figures.ipi);
      const freight = roundCents(input.items.reduce((total, item) => total + (item.freightAmount ?? 0), 0));
      const discount = roundCents(input.items.reduce((total, item) => total + (item.discountAmount ?? 0), 0));
      return {
        freight,
        discount,
        products,
        ipi,
        icmsBase: sum((figures) => figures.icmsBase),
        icms: sum((figures) => figures.icms),
        pis: sum((figures) => figures.pis),
        cofins: sum((figures) => figures.cofins),
        difal: sum((figures) => figures.difal),
        fcp: sum((figures) => figures.fcp),
        // In 2026 IBS and CBS are informed and do not add to the total of the invoice.
        invoice: roundCents(products + freight - discount + ipi),
        reformBase: sum((figures) => figures.reformBase),
        ibsState: sum((figures) => figures.ibsState),
        ibsCity: sum((figures) => figures.ibsCity),
        cbs: sum((figures) => figures.cbs),
      };
    }

    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use utoipa::ToSchema;
    use crate::{domains::DomainError, platform::valid_document};
    use super::model::{DraftInput, exact_decimal, state_code};
    
    #[derive(Clone, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, ToSchema)]
    #[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct Transport {
        pub carrier_tax_id: Option<String>, pub carrier_name: Option<String>,
        pub state_registration: Option<String>, pub address: Option<String>,
        pub city: Option<String>, pub state: Option<String>,
        pub plate: Option<String>, pub vehicle_state: Option<String>, pub rntc: Option<String>,
        pub volumes: Option<u32>, pub volume_kind: Option<String>,
        pub volume_number: Option<String>, pub brand: Option<String>,
        pub net_weight: Option<String>, pub gross_weight: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, ToSchema)]
    #[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct Retentions {
        pub pis: Option<String>, pub cofins: Option<String>, pub csll: Option<String>,
        pub income_tax_base: Option<String>, pub income_tax: Option<String>,
        pub social_security_base: Option<String>, pub social_security: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, ToSchema)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct XmlAccess { pub tax_id: String, pub name: Option<String> }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, ToSchema)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct Intermediary { pub tax_id: String, pub registration: String }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Deserialize, Serialize, ToSchema)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "camelCase")]
    pub struct Installment { pub number: String, pub due_date: String, pub amount: String }
    
    fn valid_text(value: &str, max: usize) -> bool {
        !value.trim().is_empty() && value.chars().count() <= max && !value.chars().any(char::is_control)
    }
    fn document(value: &str) -> bool { valid_document(value, if value.len() == 11 { "fisica" } else { "juridica" }) }
    
    pub fn validate(draft: &DraftInput) -> Result<(), DomainError> {
        if let Some(transport) = &draft.transport {
            if draft.freight_mode.as_deref().unwrap_or("9") == "9" {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Dados de transporte exigem modalidade de frete diferente de 9"));
            }
            if transport.carrier_tax_id.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !document(value))
                || transport.carrier_tax_id.is_some() != transport.carrier_name.is_some()
                || [&transport.carrier_name, &transport.address, &transport.city, &transport.volume_kind, &transport.volume_number, &transport.brand].into_iter().any(|value| value.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !valid_text(value, 60)))
                || [&transport.state, &transport.vehicle_state].into_iter().any(|value| value.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| state_code(value).is_none()))
                || transport.state_registration.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !valid_text(value, 14) || transport.state.is_none())
                || transport.plate.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| value.len() != 7 || !value.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_uppercase() || byte.is_ascii_digit()))
                || transport.vehicle_state.is_some() && transport.plate.is_none()
                || transport.rntc.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !valid_text(value, 20) || transport.plate.is_none())
            { return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Confira documento, nome, UF, veiculo e volumes da transportadora")); }
            let net = transport.net_weight.as_deref().map(|value| exact_decimal(value, 12, 3)).transpose()?;
            let gross = transport.gross_weight.as_deref().map(|value| exact_decimal(value, 12, 3)).transpose()?;
            if net.zip(gross).is_some_and(|(net, gross)| net > gross) { return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Peso liquido nao pode superar o peso bruto")); }
        }
        if let Some(retentions) = &draft.retentions {
            for value in [&retentions.pis, &retentions.cofins, &retentions.csll, &retentions.income_tax_base, &retentions.income_tax, &retentions.social_security_base, &retentions.social_security].into_iter().flatten() {
                exact_decimal(value, 13, 2)?;
            }
        }
        let mut documents = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        if draft.authorized_xml.len() > 10 || draft.authorized_xml.iter().any(|entry| !document(&entry.tax_id) || !documents.insert(&entry.tax_id) || entry.name.as_ref().is_some_and(|name| !valid_text(name, 200))) {
            return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Informe ate 10 CPF/CNPJ distintos para acesso ao XML"));
        }
        if let Some(intermediary) = &draft.intermediary {
            if !valid_document(&intermediary.tax_id, "juridica") || !valid_text(&intermediary.registration, 60) || ![2, 3, 4, 9].contains(&draft.presence_indicator.unwrap_or(9)) {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Intermediador exige CNPJ, cadastro e operacao nao presencial"));
            }
        }
        if draft.tax_authority_information.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !valid_text(value, 2000))
            || draft.payment_terms.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !valid_text(value, 200)) {
            return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Confira informacoes fiscais e condicao de pagamento"));
        }
        if draft.installments.len() > 120 || draft.model == 65 && !draft.installments.is_empty() { return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Parcelas exigem NF-e modelo 55 e limite de 120 parcelas")); }
        let mut numbers = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for installment in &draft.installments {
            if installment.number.len() != 3 || !installment.number.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) || !numbers.insert(&installment.number)
                || time::Date::parse(&installment.due_date, &time::format_description::well_known::Iso8601::DATE).is_err()
                || exact_decimal(&installment.amount, 13, 2)? <= 0 {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Confira numero, vencimento e valor positivo de cada parcela"));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    export type Transport = {
      carrierTaxId?: string | null; carrierName?: string | null; stateRegistration?: string | null;
      address?: string | null; city?: string | null; state?: string | null;
      plate?: string | null; vehicleState?: string | null; rntc?: string | null;
      volumes?: number | null; volumeKind?: string | null; volumeNumber?: string | null; brand?: string | null;
      netWeight?: string | null; grossWeight?: string | null;
    }
    export type Retentions = Partial<Record<"pis" | "cofins" | "csll" | "incomeTaxBase" | "incomeTax" | "socialSecurityBase" | "socialSecurity", string | null>>
    export type Installment = { number: string; dueDate: string; amount: string }
    export type FiscalExtras = {
      transport?: Transport | null; retentions?: Retentions | null;
      authorizedXml?: { taxId: string; name?: string | null }[];
      intermediary?: { taxId: string; registration: string } | null;
      taxAuthorityInformation?: string | null; paymentTerms?: string | null;
      financialCategoryId?: string | null; installments?: Installment[];
    }
    
    export function generateInstallments(total: string, count: number, firstDueDate: string, interval: number): Installment[] {
      if (!/^\d+\.\d{2}$/.test(total) || !Number.isInteger(count) || count < 1 || count > 120 || !Number.isInteger(interval) || interval < 1 || interval > 365) throw new Error("Confira quantidade de parcelas e intervalo.")
      const first = new Date(`${firstDueDate}T12:00:00Z`)
      if (!Number.isFinite(first.valueOf()) || first.toISOString().slice(0, 10) !== firstDueDate) throw new Error("Informe o primeiro vencimento.")
      const cents = BigInt(total.replace(".", "")), divisor = BigInt(count)
      if (cents < divisor) throw new Error("O valor da nota deve permitir parcelas de pelo menos um centavo.")
      return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => {
        const value = cents / divisor + (BigInt(index) < cents % divisor ? 1n : 0n)
        const due = new Date(first); due.setUTCDate(due.getUTCDate() + index * interval)
        return { number: String(index + 1).padStart(3, "0"), dueDate: due.toISOString().slice(0, 10), amount: `${value / 100n}.${String(value % 100n).padStart(2, "0")}` }
      })
    }

    async fn prepare(
        tx: &mut Transaction<'_, Postgres>,
        tenant: Uuid,
        value: &DraftInput,
    ) -> Result<(IssuerSnapshot, i64), DomainError> {
        let row = load_profile(tx, tenant)
            .await?
            .ok_or(DomainError::Conflict(
                "Configure a preparação fiscal antes de criar o rascunho",
            ))?;
        let profile = profile_data(&row)?;
        let total = value.validate(&profile)?;
        let (company_revision, company) = issuer(tx, tenant, &profile).await?;
        Ok((
            IssuerSnapshot {
                tax_id: company.tax_id.clone(),
                legal_name: company.legal_name.clone(),
                company_revision,
                company,
                profile_revision: row.revision,
                profile,
            },
            total,
        ))
    }
    
    fn draft_ibpt_snapshot(
        state: &AppState,
        tenant: Uuid,
        value: &DraftInput,
    ) -> Result<Option<ibpt_document::IbptDocumentSnapshot>, FiscalError> {
        ibpt_document::snapshot(&state.ibpt, tenant, value).map_err(|error| match error {
            DomainError::Conflict(title) => FiscalError::IbptUnavailable(title),
            other => FiscalError::Domain(other),
        })
    }

    function commercialItemCents(item: DraftItem): bigint {
      const gross = scaled(itemTotal(item.quantity, item.unitPrice))
      const freight = scaled(fixed(item.freightAmount || "0", 2, 13))
      const discount = scaled(fixed(item.discountAmount || "0", 2, 13))
      const net = gross + freight - discount
      if (discount > gross || net <= BigInt(0)) throw new Error("Confira o desconto e o total do item com frete")
      return net

    use std::{env, net::SocketAddr};
    
    use anyhow::{Context, ensure};
    use uuid::Uuid;
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct Config {
        pub bind_address: SocketAddr,
        pub auth_userinfo_url: String,
        pub database_url: String,
        pub database_max_connections: u32,
        pub nfe_production_enabled: bool,
        pub nfe_production_tenant_id: Option<Uuid>,
        pub invitations: Option<crate::platform::invitations::ProvisioningClient>,
        pub mail: Option<crate::platform::mail::SmtpMailer>,
        pub danfe: Option<crate::domains::fiscal::danfe_client::DanfeClient>,
        pub contracts: Option<crate::domains::contracts::provider::Docuseal>,
    }
    
    impl Config {
        pub fn from_env() -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
            let nfe_production_enabled = parse_legacy_fiscal_flag(
                &env::var("NFE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED").unwrap_or_else(|_| "false".to_owned()),
            )?;
            let nfe_production_tenant_id = env::var("NFE_PRODUCTION_TENANT_ID")
                .ok()
                .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
                .map(|value| {
                    Uuid::parse_str(value.trim()).context("NFE_PRODUCTION_TENANT_ID must be a UUID")
                })
                .transpose()?;
            ensure!(
                !nfe_production_enabled || nfe_production_tenant_id.is_some(),
                "NFE_PRODUCTION_TENANT_ID is required when NFE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED=true"
            );
            let bind_address = env::var("API_BIND_ADDRESS")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "0.0.0.0:8080".to_owned())
                .parse()
                .context("API_BIND_ADDRESS must be a valid socket address")?;
            let auth_issuer = env::var("AUTH_ISSUER")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "https://auth.avilaops.com".to_owned())
                .trim_end_matches('/')
                .to_owned();
            let auth_userinfo_url = env::var("AUTH_USERINFO_URL")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| format!("{auth_issuer}/oauth/userinfo"));
            reqwest::Url::parse(&auth_userinfo_url)
                .context("AUTH_USERINFO_URL must be a valid absolute URL")?;
            let database_url = env::var("DATABASE_URL").context("DATABASE_URL is required")?;
            let database_max_connections = env::var("DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS")
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "10".to_owned())
                .parse()
                .context("DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS must be an integer")?;
    
            ensure!(
                database_max_connections > 0,
                "DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS must be greater than zero"
            );
    
            Ok(Self {
                bind_address,
                auth_userinfo_url,
                database_url,
                database_max_connections,
                nfe_production_enabled,
                nfe_production_tenant_id,
                invitations: crate::platform::invitations::ProvisioningClient::from_env(&auth_issuer)?,
                mail: crate::platform::mail::SmtpMailer::from_env()?,
                danfe: danfe_configuration()?,
                contracts: crate::domains::contracts::provider::Docuseal::from_env()?,
            })
        }
    }
    
    fn danfe_configuration() -> anyhow::Result<Option<crate::domains::fiscal::danfe_client::DanfeClient>>
    {
        let endpoint = env::var("DANFE_MCP_URL")
            .ok()
            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty());
        let token = env::var("DANFE_MCP_TOKEN")
            .ok()
            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty());
        let ca_path = env::var("DANFE_CA_BUNDLE_FILE")
            .ok()
            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty());
        if endpoint.is_none() && token.is_none() && ca_path.is_none() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let endpoint = endpoint.context("DANFE_MCP_URL is required when enabling DANFE")?;
        let token = token.context("DANFE_MCP_TOKEN is required when enabling DANFE")?;
        let bundle = ca_path
            .map(|path| std::fs::read_to_string(path).context("Failed to read DANFE_CA_BUNDLE_FILE"))
            .transpose()?;
        crate::domains::fiscal::danfe_client::DanfeClient::new(&endpoint, &token, bundle).map(Some)
    }
    
    // This is an explicit deployment gate. It never selects a tenant environment,
    // provisions credentials or proves fiscal homologation by itself.
    fn parse_legacy_fiscal_flag(value: &str) -> anyhow::Result<bool> {
        ensure!(
            ["false", "true"].contains(&value),
            "NFE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED must be a boolean; select the fiscal environment in the company profile"
        );
        Ok(value == "true")
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::parse_legacy_fiscal_flag;
        #[test]
        fn legacy_flag_accepts_booleans_without_selecting_a_company_environment() {
            assert!(!parse_legacy_fiscal_flag("false").unwrap());
            assert!(parse_legacy_fiscal_flag("true").unwrap());
            for value in ["1", "", "False", "production"] {
                assert!(parse_legacy_fiscal_flag(value).is_err());
            }
        }
    }

    /// Hourly reconciliation of the current month. Unique origin and tenant lock make replicas safe.
    pub fn start_worker(state: AppState) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3600));
            interval.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Skip);
            loop {
                interval.tick().await;
                if let Err(error) = worker_tick(&state).await {
                    tracing::error!(
                        ?error,
                        "staff payroll recurrence failed; next reconciliation will retry"
                    );
                }
            }
        })
    }
    async fn worker_tick(state: &AppState) -> Result<(), DomainError> {
        let tenants: Vec<Uuid> = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT * FROM erp_staff_payroll_due_tenants()")
            .fetch_all(&state.database)
            .await
            .map_err(db)?;

        pub fn from_env() -> anyhow::Result<Option<Arc<Self>>> {
            let keyring = std::env::var("FISCAL_A1_KEYRING")
                .ok()
                .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
                .map(Zeroizing::new);
            let roots = std::env::var("FISCAL_A1_CA_BUNDLE_FILE")
                .ok()
                .filter(|value| !value.is_empty());
            if keyring.is_none() && roots.is_none() {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            let keyring = keyring.ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("FISCAL_A1_KEYRING is required"))?;
            let roots = if let Some(path) = roots {
                std::fs::read(path)?
            } else {
                include_bytes!("../../../../../deploy/fiscal/icp-brasil-roots.pem").to_vec()
            };
            Ok(Some(Arc::new(Self::new(&keyring, &roots)?)))
        }

    /** Local development can run the fiscal API without changing the other ERP services. */
    export function fiscalApiOrigin(resource: string, defaultOrigin: string, override: string | undefined, environment: string | undefined): string {
      if (environment !== "development" || !override || !/^\/fiscal\/(?:nfe(?:\/|$)|issued-nfes$|readiness$|config$|certificate$|order-preparations\/|ibpt(?:\/|$))/.test(resource)) return defaultOrigin
      const url = new URL(override)
      if (!["http:", "https:"].includes(url.protocol) || !["127.0.0.1", "[::1]"].includes(url.hostname) || url.username || url.password || url.pathname !== "/" || url.search || url.hash) throw new Error("Destino fiscal local inválido")
      return url.origin
    }
    Add: C:\Users\nicol\source\erp-next-main\apps\web\tests\local-fiscal-api.node.test.mjs

      for (const route of ["/products", "/fiscal/danfe", "/fiscal/incoming", "/fiscal/nfe-other"]) assert.equal(fiscalApiOrigin(route, original, "http://127.0.0.1:8081", "development"), original)
      assert.equal(fiscalApiOrigin("/fiscal/nfe", original, "http://127.0.0.1:8081", "production"), original)

    # Brainstorming
    
    You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
    partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
    skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
    anything gets built.
    
    People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
    help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
    hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.
    
    ## First: What Do You Actually Know?
    
    Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
    why?
    
    - **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
      blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
    - **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.
    
    Before you start implementing, you must, in order:
    
    1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
       human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
    2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
    3. Get their approval of that doc.
    4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.
    
    Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
    feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
    the questions.
    
    ## Look Before You Ask
    
    In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
    a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
    first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
    connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
    parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
    project or their context already answers.
    
    ## Your First Message
    
    Move the work forward, with one of these:
    
    - **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
      request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
      request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
      shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
      Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
      and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
      have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
      has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
      so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
      want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
      corrections, then one question about what they want: the thing their
      request leaves open whose answer would most change what gets built.
      Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
    - **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
      biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
      what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
      my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
      I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
      different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"
    
    How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
    brainstorming:
    
    - **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
      design discussion): end with your question. They want this
      conversation.
    - **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. After your
      question, add a light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
      "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
      it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
      (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
      asked through the normal workflow.
    
    That's the whole message.
    
    ## The Conversation
    
    Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
    example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
    above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
    process jargon. You never need to quote this skill to your human
    partner.
    
    Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
    report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
    the rest.
    
    **Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
    intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
    stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
    something concrete.
    
    **How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
    materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
    libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
    of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
    they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
    want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
    said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
    uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
    something they agreed to.
    
    **Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
    out as questions:
    
    - what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
    - why now, and what success looks like to them
    - goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
      if it technically works)
    - prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
    - current state: what exists now, what they've tried
    - the details they care about
    
    **Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
    you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
    question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
    them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
    ("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
    Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
    already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
    change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
    beats a question.
    
    **Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
    would help, offer to go look: deeper into their codebase or project,
    their own files and data, or the web. Say what you'd look for. They
    decide whether you go.
    
    **Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
    before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
    of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
    ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
    existing work rules out. Present the two or three that remain, grounding
    each in what the project actually does and saying what it trades off.
    Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want to go. When
    there's genuinely one sensible way, say so and explain why the others
    don't fit. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
    describing first.
    
    **Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
    would help more than reading:
    
    - something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
    - a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
    - a flow or a sequence of steps
    - options that would look different from each other
    - a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map
    
    Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
    options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.
    
    **Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
    fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
    they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
    When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
    or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
    and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
    conversation.
    
    ## Play It Back
    
    Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
    describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
    behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
    questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
    the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.
    
    Only what they said goes in as theirs. Anything you filled in goes in
    as your proposal, with your reason. End each chunk by asking what's wrong
    or missing.
    
    Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
    look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
    they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
    (its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
    they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.
    
    ## Size the Work
    
    Once you understand what they want and they've picked an approach, say
    how big the work is in plain words. They can override it.
    
    | Size | The design doc |
    |------|----------------|
    | A small change | a short one: what you already covered together, written down |
    | A project | the full written design (below) |
    
    Short or full, the design doc has an **Approaches** part: the two or
    three ways you considered building it, what each trades off, which one
    they picked, and why. They pick in the conversation, before you write
    the doc.
    
    If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.
    
    If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
    order, and brainstorm them one at a time.
    
    ## The Written Design
    
    Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan
    from without going back to your human partner. Cover:
    
    - intent and the why
    - goals, non-goals, anti-goals
    - constraints
    - approaches (above)
    - the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
    - what's left to the builder
    
    For a small change, the short design covers the same points in a line
    or two each and goes straight to your human partner, without the
    builder check.
    
    **Where it goes:** in a software repo,
    `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
    Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.
    
    **Builder check** (for a project): dispatch a fresh subagent with
    `builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
    partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
    may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
    until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:
    
    - **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
      in the document.
    - **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
      built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
    - **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
      what gets built.
    
    Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
    document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
    calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
    round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
    document as that builder yourself.
    
    <HARD-GATE>
    Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the design doc:
    the short one for a small change, the full one for a project.
    Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
    dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
    Reading and exploring are fine.
    
    Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
    and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
    stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
    that comes back through this gate.
    
    After the design doc is approved, the next step is the plan: invoke
    superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
    </HARD-GATE>
    
    ## Red Flags
    
    | Thought | Reality |
    |---------|---------|
    | "I'll offer a menu of what they might want" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
    | "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
    | "I've answered their questions, so I'll write the doc" | Lay out the approaches first, in a message of their own. |
    | "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
    | "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A design doc you haven't written isn't approved. |
    | "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |
    
    ## Visual Companion
    
    A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
    tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
    browser.
    
    **Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
    above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
    else in it:
    
    > "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"
    
    If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.
    
    **Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
    Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
    Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
    question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.
    
    If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
    starting the server.

    # Orientacoes para agentes
    
    Leia os manifestos e a documentacao do projeto antes de alterar codigo.
    Preserve trabalho existente, proteja segredos e valide as mudancas pertinentes.
    
    ## Controle da equipe
    
    Para coordenar demandas deste projeto, leia [.agents/equipe/README.md](.agents/equipe/README.md).
    O registro de responsaveis, tarefas, decisoes e integracoes fica em `.agents/equipe/controle.json`.
    A skill de coordenacao esta em `.agents/skills/avila-mcp-avilaops-com-equipe/SKILL.md`.
    Mantenha evidencias e estado atualizados; as regras especificas deste repositorio continuam valendo.
    # mcp.avilaops.com
    
    Porta de entrada do MCP da Ávila Ops. **O MCP é um só**, da empresa inteira, e
    vive no n8n (workflow `MCP - Avila Ops`, `https://n8n.avilaops.com/mcp/avilaops`):
    lá ficam as ferramentas de todos os sistemas (WhatsApp e posts, catálogos da
    Meta, Search Console, cofre de segredos, fiscal, notas, CMS). Este serviço só cuida
    do login das pessoas e repassa o pedido.
    
    | Endereço | O que é | Acesso |
    |---|---|---|
    | `https://mcp.avilaops.com/mcp` | O MCP da Ávila Ops (repassa ao n8n) | login |
    | `https://mcp.avilaops.com/gsc` | Backend dedicado opcional: 21 ferramentas GSC e oito workflows SEO | OAuth Ávila Ops |
    | `https://mcp.avilaops.com/hindsight` | Hindsight self-hosted, atrás do OAuth Ávila Ops | OAuth Ávila Ops |
    | `https://mcp.avilaops.com/ml` | Laboratório MLOps: suítes, execuções, evidências e comparações | OAuth Ávila Ops |
    
    Desde 13/10/2026, `/gsc` é uma exceção opcional à unificação descrita abaixo:
    com `GSC_UPSTREAM_URL` configurado, atende o backend dedicado com OAuth;
    sem essa variável, mantém a resposta 410. Novos sistemas continuam entrando
    no MCP principal. Consulte [o procedimento de reconstrução do GSC](backends/gsc/README.md)
    e [a revalidação operacional](backends/gsc/DEPLOY-AVILA.md).
    
    Decisão do Nicolas em 12/10/2026: não ter um MCP por sistema. **Sistema novo
    entra como ferramenta no workflow do n8n, não como endereço novo aqui.** Os
    endereços que existiram por dois dias (`/infisical`, `/gsc`, `/fiscal`)
    respondem 410 dizendo qual é o endereço único.
    
    O que está dentro em 12/10/2026 (115 ferramentas): WhatsApp e posts, planejador,
    catálogos da Meta, Search Console, Infisical, fiscal, notas e CMS.
    
    ## Como o acesso funciona
    
    - **Pessoas (Claude no computador, no celular ou no navegador):** OAuth 2.1 no
      formato da especificação de autorização do MCP. O Claude descobre os
      metadados, registra-se sozinho (registro dinâmico), abre o login do
      `auth.avilaops.com` e a pessoa confirma numa tela nossa. Quem pode entrar é
      decidido no painel do `auth` (aplicação `mcp`).
      O `userinfo` precisa devolver também `papel` e `apps`; esses valores seguem
      no token opaco deste gateway. Ferramentas cujo nome contém `admin_` só são
      executadas quando o papel autenticado é `ADMIN`.
    - **Máquinas (Claude Code em servidor, n8n):** token de serviço no cabeçalho
      `Authorization: Bearer`. O serviço guarda só o SHA-256 de cada token aceito
      (`SERVICO_SHA256`).
    - **Sistemas da casa (TMS, ERP):** token de serviço com escopo. Em
      `SERVICO_SHA256`, `hash:fiscal_` aceita só as ferramentas que começam com
      `fiscal_` (vários prefixos com `|`); chamada de outra ferramenta responde 403.
      A lista de ferramentas (`tools/list`) continua vindo inteira.
    - **Servidor aberto:** passa sem credencial.
    
    O servidor de destino nunca recebe a credencial de quem chamou: recebe a
    credencial técnica dele, lida do `.env`. Essa credencial autentica somente o
    salto servidor→servidor. A autorização da operação continua sendo o papel da
    pessoa no OAuth, conferido pelo gateway antes do repasse.
    
    Tokens emitidos aqui: acesso de 1 hora e renovação de 30 dias, trocada a cada
    uso. Código de autorização ou token de renovação apresentado duas vezes derruba
    todos os tokens daquela conexão. Nada disso é guardado em claro: o banco
    (`/dados/mcp.sqlite`) tem só os hashes.
    
    ## Rotas
    
    | Rota | Para quê |
    |---|---|
    | `GET /` | Página com os endereços e o passo a passo |
    | `GET /health` | Verificação de saúde |
    | `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Metadados do servidor de autorização (RFC 8414) |
    | `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<id>` | Metadados do recurso (RFC 9728) |
    | `POST /oauth/register` | Registro dinâmico de cliente (RFC 7591) |
    | `GET /oauth/authorize` | Início do login |
    | `GET /oauth/retorno` | Volta do `auth.avilaops.com`; mostra a tela de confirmação |
    | `POST /oauth/confirmar` | Resposta da tela de confirmação |
    | `POST /oauth/token` | Troca de código e renovação |
    | `POST /oauth/revoke` | Encerrar uma conexão (RFC 7009) |
    | `GET /conexoes` | Tela "Minhas conexões": aplicativos autorizados pela pessoa, com último uso e o botão de desconectar (pede login) |
    | `GET/POST/DELETE /mcp` | O MCP (HTTP streamable), repassado ao n8n |
    
    ## Acrescentar um sistema
    
    No n8n, no workflow `MCP - Avila Ops`: um nó de ferramenta (HTTP Request Tool,
    Data Table Tool) ou, quando o sistema já tem servidor MCP, um nó **MCP Client
    Tool** apontando para ele (é assim que o fiscal e as notas entram; as
    ferramentas ganham o nome do nó como prefixo: `fiscal_...`, `notas_...`). Nada
    muda neste repositório.
    
    ## Desenvolver
    
    Sem dependências de npm: só o que vem no Node 22 (`http`, `crypto`, `sqlite`,
    `fetch`).
    
    ```bash
    npm test
    ```
    
    ## Publicar
    
    O GitHub Actions testa, constrói a imagem no GHCR e publica no `apps-noclient`
    (aplicação `mcp.avilaops.com`). O compose versionado fica em
    `infra/apps-noclient/mcp-avilaops-com/`.
    
    ## Operar

    # Controle da equipe
    
    Este diretorio e o registro compartilhado de trabalho de `avila-mcp-avilaops-com`.
    
    ## Rotina
    
    1. Leia o AGENTS.md da raiz, o contexto e o registro de controle.
    2. Cadastre as pessoas reais da equipe antes de atribuir tarefas.
    3. Registre cada demanda com objetivo, responsavel e criterios de aceite.
    4. Atualize o estado ao iniciar, bloquear, enviar para revisao ou concluir.
    5. Para concluir, registre a evidencia da verificacao e a revisao pertinente.
    6. Registre decisoes e integracoes verificadas; indique ambiente e identidade sem segredos.
    
    ## Arquivos
    
    - [Contexto](CONTEXTO.md): fontes de informacao e comandos encontrados no projeto.
    - [Registro](controle.json): pessoas, tarefas, decisoes e integracoes.
    - [Modelo de demanda](MODELO-DE-DEMANDA.md): contrato de entrega e passagem entre pessoas.
    
    O arquivo inicia vazio porque nao foram informados membros nem demandas concretas.
    Esta estrutura coordena pessoas e agentes; nao delega trabalho ou envia mensagens automaticamente.
    Versione os registros junto ao projeto. Em conflitos, preserve os IDs e reconcilie as evidencias.
    
    ## Atualizar com a ferramenta central
    
    A partir de `D:/Projetos/central-integracoes/desenvolvimento`:
    
    ```powershell
    python scripts/equipe.py membro avila-mcp-avilaops-com --id pessoa --nome 'Nome real' --papel 'Desenvolvimento'
    python scripts/equipe.py tarefa avila-mcp-avilaops-com --titulo 'Demanda concreta' --responsavel pessoa --aceite 'Resultado verificavel'
    python scripts/equipe.py estado avila-mcp-avilaops-com --id T-0001 --status em-andamento
    python scripts/equipe.py painel
    ```
    
    Os comandos sao exemplos de uso e nao representam cadastros realizados.
    O CLI roda na maquina com o catalogo; os JSONs e instrucoes podem ser usados em outros checkouts.
    As alteracoes sao locais ate serem commitadas e compartilhadas pelo fluxo normal do repositorio.
    ---
    name: avila-mcp-avilaops-com-equipe
    description: Coordene a equipe desta aplicacao quando o usuario pedir distribuicao de tarefas, acompanhamento, impedimentos, revisao ou passagem de trabalho.
    ---
    
    # Coordenar a equipe da aplicacao
    
    1. Confirme que a raiz do checkout corresponde a `avila-mcp-avilaops-com`; leia AGENTS.md e `.agents/equipe/README.md`.
    2. Leia `.agents/equipe/CONTEXTO.md` e `.agents/equipe/controle.json`. Consulte o codigo e os manifestos quando o pedido depender de fatos tecnicos.
    3. Use apenas membros cadastrados. Se faltar a identidade de quem deve receber uma demanda, mantenha-a sem atribuicao no relato e solicite o dado antes de cadastrar a tarefa.
    4. Registre tarefas reais com objetivo, responsavel, prioridade e criterios de aceite. Preserve IDs, historico e alteracoes de outros colaboradores.
    5. Ao atualizar status, registre motivo de bloqueio ou evidencia de conclusao. Uma implementacao local nao comprova publicacao em producao.
    6. Registre decisoes com justificativa e evidencia. Integrações precisam de ambiente, identidade nao secreta e verificacao real de acesso.
    7. Apresente tarefas por estado, responsaveis, bloqueios e proxima acao. Diga quando o registro esta vazio ou desatualizado.
    
    Use o CLI `scripts/equipe.py` da central quando estiver acessivel; em outro host, atualize o mesmo JSON preservando seu formato.
    Nao inicie outros agentes nem envie mensagens em nome da equipe sem autorizacao do usuario.
    Este workflow organiza registros; nao instala conectores, nao concede acesso e nao comprova conclusao por conta propria.

        "mcp>=1.30.0,<3.0",
        "click>=8.3.3",
    ]
    
    [project.optional-dependencies]
    dev = [
        "pytest>=9.1.1",
        "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
        "ruff>=0.17.0",
        "mypy>=1.10",
        "pre-commit>=3.7",
    ]
    
    [project.scripts]
    mcp-fiscal-brasil = "mcp_fiscal_brasil.server:main"
    mcp-fiscal = "mcp_fiscal_brasil.cli:main"
    mcp-fiscal-api = "mcp_fiscal_brasil.api:run"
    
    [project.urls]
    Homepage = "https://github.com/DeHor-Labs/mcp-fiscal-brasil"
    Repository = "https://github.com/DeHor-Labs/mcp-fiscal-brasil"
    Issues = "https://github.com/DeHor-Labs/mcp-fiscal-brasil/issues"
    Changelog = "https://github.com/DeHor-Labs/mcp-fiscal-brasil/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"
    Examples = "https://github.com/DeHor-Labs/mcp-fiscal-brasil/tree/main/examples"
    
    [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
    packages = ["src/mcp_fiscal_brasil"]
    include = ["src/mcp_fiscal_brasil/tabelas/data/*.db"]
    
    [tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
    exclude = ["landing"]
    
    [tool.ruff]
    target-version = "py311"
    line-length = 100
    src = ["src", "tests"]
    
    [tool.ruff.lint]
    select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "B", "C4", "RUF"]
    ignore = ["E501"]
    
    [tool.ruff.lint.isort]
    known-first-party = ["mcp_fiscal_brasil"]
    
    [tool.mypy]
    python_version = "3.11"
    strict = true
    ignore_missing_imports = true
    plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
    
    [[tool.mypy.overrides]]
    module = [
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.server",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.bcb._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.cep._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.cnae._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.empresa._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.ibge._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.mei._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.tabelas._tools",
        "mcp_fiscal_brasil.importacao._tools",
    ]
    # Decoradores @app.tool() do FastMCP nao sao tipados; o override por modulo
    # e mais cirurgico do que rebaixar o strict global.
    # warn_unused_ignores = false: server.py usa hasattr guard antes de .model_dump()
    # em dados_completos (tipado como object no dataclass de distribuicao); o mypy
    # strict reporta o type: ignore como unused mesmo com a guarda em vigor.
    disallow_untyped_decorators = false
    warn_unused_ignores = false
    
    [tool.pytest.ini_options]
    asyncio_mode = "auto"
    testpaths = ["tests"]
    
    [dependency-groups]
    dev = [
        "httpx>=0.28.1",
        "mkdocs-gen-files>=0.6.1",
        "mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin>=1.6.0",
        "mkdocs-literate-nav>=0.6.3",
        "mkdocs-material>=9.7.7",
        "mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin>=1.2.3",
        "mkdocstrings[python]>=1.0.6",
        "pymdown-extensions>=10.21.3",
        "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
        "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
        "types-cachetools>=7.0.0.20260713",
    ]
    # Compose para desenvolvimento e demos do mcp-fiscal-brasil.
    #
    # Servicos:
    # - api: FastAPI REST + Web UI demo em http://localhost:8000
    # - mcp-http: servidor MCP via HTTP transport (alternativa ao stdio)
    #
    # Uso:
    #   docker compose up api
    #   docker compose up mcp-http
    
    services:
      api:
        build: .
        image: mcp-fiscal-brasil:dev
        command: ["mcp-fiscal-api"]
        ports:
          - "8000:8000"
        environment:
          HOST: 0.0.0.0
          PORT: "8000"
          MCP_FISCAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "30"
          MCP_FISCAL_CACHE_TTL: "300"
          MCP_FISCAL_RATE_LIMIT: "10"
        restart: unless-stopped
        healthcheck:
          test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health')"]
          interval: 30s
          timeout: 5s
          retries: 3
    
      mcp-http:
        build: .
        image: mcp-fiscal-brasil:dev
        command: ["mcp-fiscal-brasil", "--transport", "http"]
        ports:
          - "8001:8000"
        environment:
          HOST: 0.0.0.0
          PORT: "8000"
          MCP_FISCAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "30"
          MCP_FISCAL_CACHE_TTL: "300"
        restart: unless-stopped
        profiles: ["mcp"]
    # Imagem Docker do mcp-fiscal-brasil
    # Multi-stage para imagem final enxuta com uv.
    #
    # Build:
    #   docker build -t mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0 .
    #
    # Run (servidor MCP stdio):
    #   docker run --rm -i mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0
    #
    # Run (REST API + Web UI):
    #   docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0 mcp-fiscal-api
    #
    # Run (MCP HTTP transport):
    #   docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0 mcp-fiscal-brasil --transport http
    #
    # Variaveis de ambiente uteis:
    #   MCP_FISCAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT=30
    #   MCP_FISCAL_CACHE_TTL=300
    #   MCP_FISCAL_RATE_LIMIT=10
    #   HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=8000
    
    # ---- Build stage ----
    FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
    
    ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
        PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    
    WORKDIR /build
    
    COPY pyproject.toml README.md LICENSE ./
    COPY src/ ./src/
    
    RUN pip install --no-cache-dir hatchling build && \
        python -m build --wheel
    
    # ---- Runtime stage ----
    FROM python:3.12-slim AS runtime
    
    ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
        PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
        PORT=8000 \
        HOST=0.0.0.0
    
    WORKDIR /app
    
    COPY --from=builder /build/dist/*.whl ./
    COPY scripts/docker_healthcheck.py ./docker_healthcheck.py
    
    RUN pip install --no-cache-dir *.whl && \
        rm -f *.whl && \
        groupadd -r app && useradd -r -g app -d /app -s /usr/sbin/nologin app && \
        chown -R app:app /app
    
    USER app
    
    EXPOSE 8000
    
    # O CMD padrao (mcp-fiscal-brasil, stdio) nao abre porta HTTP. O healthcheck
    # detecta automaticamente qual modo esta rodando: se a porta estiver
    # escutando, valida via GET /health; caso contrario, confirma so que o
    # pacote importa (modo stdio). Ver scripts/docker_healthcheck.py.
    HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
        CMD python docker_healthcheck.py || exit 1
    
    # Comando padrao: servidor MCP via stdio (uso por clientes MCP nativos).
    # Sobrescreva para REST API: docker run ... mcp-fiscal-api
    CMD ["mcp-fiscal-brasil"]

Ops\",\"webhookId\":\"558ce129-6cdb-4c96-8c38-7403831baf27\",\"type\":\"@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.mcpTrigger\",\"typeVersion\":2.1,\"position\":[832,0],\"parameters\":{\"authentication\":\"bearerAuth\",\"path\":\"avilaops\",\"instructions\":\"Ferramentas da operação da Avila Ops. Posts: post_agendar aceita os canais whatsapp (conversa do próprio número), status (Status do WhatsApp para a lista de público), canal (canal público do WhatsApp), instagram, facebook e tiktok; use whatsapp_estado antes de agendar para WhatsApp. Planejador de posts: planejador_rascunhos lista as peças com texto de modelo e planejador_redigir grava o texto redigido; nenhuma das duas publica, quem aprova é o Nicolas na tela. Catálogos da Meta: produtos, assessoria (o que está ligado ao WhatsApp) e apps; catalogo_incluir cria, catalogo_alterar muda só os campos informados, catalogo_excluir não tem volta. Search Console (somente leitura): comece por gsc_list_properties para obter o site_url exato e use esse valor em gsc_search_analytics, gsc_list_sitemaps e gsc_inspect_url. Horários sempre em ISO 8601 UTC (Brasília + 3 h). Cofre de segredos (Infisical, somente leitura): infisical_list_secrets lista os nomes e infisical_get_secret lê um valor; só leia um valor quando a tarefa precisar. Fiscal: consultas e validações fiscais brasileiras (CNPJ, CEP, NCM, CFOP, ICMS, NF-e, CT-e, MDF-e, IBS/CBS); validar_xml_fiscal confere XML contra os esquemas oficiais. Notas (Outline): documentos e coleções da casa, leitura e escrita; apagar só com pedido explícito. CMS: sites e conteúdo da casa e dos clientes (cms_*). cms_publicar põe conteúdo no ar em site de cliente e cms_despublicar, cms_apagar_midia e cms_remover_redirecionamento desfazem coisas: só com pedido explícito. Credenciais do n8n: credencial_listar, credencial_criar, credencial_alterar e credencial_apagar. Nenhuma devolve valor. Segredo entra por do_cofre (nome de um segredo cadastrado no Cofre), não por valores; credencial_alterar troca os valores por inteiro e vale na hora para os workflows que a usam; credencial_apagar não tem volta e só com pedido explícito.\\nLojas: não é exposto por este MCP central, porque operações de loja exigem o OAuth do usuário e a seleção explícita do tenant. Use lojas_conectar para consultar o endereço e depois adicione o conector dedicado https://lojas.avilaops.com/api/mcp; ele abre o login, solicita a loja e limita as ferramentas aos escopos autorizados.\"},\"credentials\":{\"httpBearerAuth\":{\"id\":\"20bmZRTP30B7wgqo\",\"name\":\"MCP Avila Ops (token de acesso)\"}}},{\"id\":\"1ee781a7-4cec-4667-aa45-249e0073ee36\",\"name\":\"whatsapp_estado\",\"type\":\"n8n-nodes-base.httpRequestTool\",\"typeVersion\":4.5,\"position\":[96,400],\"parameters\":{\"toolDescription\":\"Lista os números de WhatsApp do serviço de envio e o estado de cada um (aberta = conectado, aguardando_pareamento, conectando).     logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    MAX_CNPJS_POR_LOTE = 50
    
    
    def _validar_cnpj_ou_erro(cnpj: str) -> None:
        """Rejeita CNPJ com dígito verificador inválido antes de qualquer consulta externa.
    
        Evita que as tools agenticas disparem consultas (Receita, Simples, MEI) para
        um valor que nunca poderia existir.
        """
        if not validate_cnpj_qualquer(cnpj):
            raise ValueError(
                f"CNPJ inválido: {cnpj}. Verifique o formato e o dígito verificador "
                "(numérico ou alfanumérico, com ou sem máscara)."
            )
    
    
    def _normalizar_e_validar_cnpjs(cnpjs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        if len(cnpjs) > MAX_CNPJS_POR_LOTE:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Tamanho do lote inválido: recebeu {len(cnpjs)} CNPJs, máximo permitido é "
                f"{MAX_CNPJS_POR_LOTE}."
            )
    
        invalidos: list[str] = []
        normalizados: list[str] = []
    
        for cnpj in cnpjs:
            if not validate_cnpj_qualquer(cnpj):
                invalidos.append(cnpj)
                continue
            normalizados.append(normalizar_cnpj(cnpj))
    
        if invalidos:
            raise ValueError(
                "CNPJ(s) inválido(s) no lote. "
                f"Verifique o formato e o dígito verificador: {', '.join(invalidos)}"
            )
    
        return normalizados
    
    
    app = FastMCP(
        name="MCP Fiscal Brasil",
        version=__version__,
        instructions=(
            "Servidor MCP para integrar IAs com o sistema fiscal brasileiro. "
            "Consulte CNPJ, NFe, NFSe, SPED, eSocial e certidões via linguagem natural. "
            "Dados obtidos de fontes públicas: BrasilAPI, ReceitaWS, SEFAZ."
        ),
    )

    def main() -> None:
        """Inicia o servidor MCP.
    
        Modo de transporte configurável via argumento --transport ou variável de ambiente
        FASTMCP_TRANSPORT. Valores aceitos: stdio (padrão), sse, http, streamable-http.
    
        Para HTTP/SSE, a porta é configurada via variável PORT (padrão: 8000).
        """
        import argparse
        import os
    
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="MCP Fiscal Brasil")
        parser.add_argument(
            "--transport",
            choices=["stdio", "sse", "http", "streamable-http"],
            default=os.environ.get("FASTMCP_TRANSPORT", "stdio"),
            help="Protocolo de transporte (padrão: stdio)",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--port",
            type=int,
            default=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000")),
            help="Porta HTTP/SSE (padrão: 8000, ou valor da variável PORT)",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--host",
            default=os.environ.get("HOST", "0.0.0.0"),
            help="Host para HTTP/SSE (padrão: 0.0.0.0)",
        )
        args = parser.parse_args()
    
        logger.info("Iniciando MCP Fiscal Brasil v%s (transport=%s)", __version__, args.transport)
    
        if args.transport == "stdio":
            app.run(transport="stdio")
        else:
            app.run(transport=args.transport, host=args.host, port=args.port)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    name: writing-plans
    description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
    ---
    
    # Writing Plans
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.
    
    **Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."
    
    **Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.
    
    **Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
    - (User preferences for plan location override this default)
    
    ## Scope Check
    
    If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.
    
    ## File Structure
    
    Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.
    
    - Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
    - You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
    - Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.
    
    This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.
    
    ## Task Right-Sizing
    
    A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
    fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
    configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
    deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
    reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
    independently testable deliverable.
    
    ## Step Granularity
    
    **Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
    - "Write the failing test" - step
    - "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
    - "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
    - "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
    - "Commit" - step
    
    ## Plan Document Header
    
    **Every plan MUST start with this header:**
    
    ```markdown
    # [Feature Name] Implementation Plan
    
    > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
    
    **Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]
    
    **Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]
    
    **Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]
    
    **Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
    argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]
    
    ## Global Constraints
    
    [The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
    naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
    values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
    include this section.]
    
    ## Review Focus
    
    [The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
    tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
    — one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
    reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
    document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
    meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
    break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
    you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
    owns the code, in that task's own step style.]
    
    ---
    ```
