        /// Structural and arithmetic validation only; not an XSD or tax determination.
        pub fn validate(&self, profile: &ProfileInput) -> Result<i64, DomainError> {
            super::simplified::validate(self, profile)?;
            super::draft_extras::validate(self)?;
            use time::{OffsetDateTime, format_description::well_known::Rfc3339};
            let parse_date = |value: &str| OffsetDateTime::parse(value, &Rfc3339)
                .map_err(|_| DomainError::Invalid("Data fiscal deve incluir data, hora e fuso horario"));
            let issued_at = self.issued_at.as_deref().map(parse_date).transpose()?;
            let departure_at = self.departure_at.as_deref().map(parse_date).transpose()?;
            if departure_at.is_some() && issued_at.is_none()
                || issued_at.zip(departure_at).is_some_and(|(issued, departure)| departure < issued)
            {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Data de saida exige emissao informada e nao pode antecede-la"));
            }
            if self.presence_indicator.is_some_and(|value| ![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9].contains(&value)) {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Indicador de presenca invalido"));
            }
            if self.print_type.is_some_and(|value| if self.model == 65 { value != 4 } else { ![1, 2, 6].contains(&value) }) {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Apresentacao do DANFE incompativel com o modelo"));
            }
            if self.model == 65 && (departure_at.is_some() || self.final_consumer == Some(false) || self.presence_indicator.is_some_and(|value| ![1, 4, 5].contains(&value))) {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("NFC-e exige consumidor final e nao permite data de saida"));
            }
            if self.salesperson.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !text(value, 200)) {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Nome do vendedor exige ate 200 caracteres"));
            }
            if self.tax_declaration.as_ref().zip(self.final_consumer).is_some_and(|(taxes, final_consumer)| taxes.final_consumer != final_consumer) {
                return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Consumidor final diverge da declaracao tributaria"));
            }
    
            if self.environment != profile.environment {
                return Err(DomainError::Conflict(
                    "O ambiente do rascunho deve corresponder à configuração fiscal",
                ));
            }
    }

      if (!selection.uf || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(selection.asOf) || selection.items.length !== count) throw new Error("Informe UF, data e uma escolha IBPT para cada item")
      return {
        uf: selection.uf,
        asOf: selection.asOf,
        items: selection.items.map((item, index) => {
          if (!/^\d{1,3}$/.test(item.ex) || item.origin !== "national" && item.origin !== "imported") throw new Error(`Informe EX e origem IBPT no item ${index + 1}`)

          if (version && !/^\d{2}\.\d\.[A-Z]$/.test(version)) throw new Error(`Informe a versão IBPT no formato 26.2.A no item ${index + 1}`)
          return { ex: item.ex, origin: item.origin, version }
        }),
      }
    }

    async fn issuer(
        tx: &mut Transaction<'_, Postgres>,
        tenant: Uuid,
        profile: &ProfileInput,
    ) -> Result<(i64, CompanyData), DomainError> {
        let row = sqlx::query_as::<_, (String, String, i64, serde_json::Value)>(
            "SELECT t.tax_id,t.legal_name,p.revision,p.details FROM tenants t JOIN company_profiles p ON p.tenant_id=t.id WHERE t.id=$1"
        ).bind(tenant).fetch_optional(&mut **tx).await.map_err(db)?.ok_or(DomainError::Conflict("Preencha os dados da empresa antes da preparação fiscal"))?;
        let mut company: CompanyData =
            serde_json::from_value(row.3).map_err(|_| access::AccessError::Internal)?;
        company.tax_id = row.0;
        company.legal_name = row.1;
        company
            .validate()
            .map_err(|_| DomainError::Conflict("Cadastro da empresa incompleto ou inválido"))?;
        if company.person_type != "juridica"
            || company.tax_id.len() != 14
            || !profile.matches_company(
                &company.state,
                &company.tax_regime,
                &company.state_registration,
            )
        {
            return Err(DomainError::Conflict(
                "Emitente exige CNPJ e UF, IE e CRT coerentes com o cadastro da empresa",
            ));
        }
        Ok((row.2, company))
    }

    ---
    title: use client
    description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.
    ---
    
    The `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature.
    
    > **Good to know:**
    >
    > You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client.
    
    ## Usage
    
    To declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function:
    
    ```tsx filename="app/components/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
    'use client'
    
    import { useState } from 'react'
    
    export default function Counter() {
      const [count, setCount] = useState(0)

                "CSC NFC-e não pertence à empresa ou ao ambiente atual",
            ));
        }
        let vault = state.certificates.as_ref().ok_or(DomainError::Conflict(
            "Armazenamento seguro de CSC indisponível",
        ))?;
        let secret = vault
            .open_settings_secret(

    async function bounded(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, maximum: number) {
      const reader = stream?.getReader()
      const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []
      let size = 0
      if (reader) for (;;) {
        const { done, value } = await reader.read()
        if (done) break
        size += value.byteLength
        if (size > maximum) { await reader.cancel(); throw new RangeError("Document exceeds limit") }
        chunks.push(value)
      }
      return Buffer.concat(chunks)
    }

    pub async fn get_profile(
        State(state): State<AppState>,
        Extension(identity): Extension<AuthenticatedIdentity>,
        headers: HeaderMap,
    ) -> Result<Response, FiscalError> {
        let (tenant, mut tx, can_edit) = authorized(
            &state,
            &headers,
            &identity,
            "fiscal.config.read",
            "fiscal.config.manage",
            false,
        )
        .await?;
        let row = load_profile(&mut tx, tenant).await?;
        let current = row.as_ref().map_or(0, |row| row.revision);
        let mut data = row.as_ref().map(profile_data).transpose()?;
        if let Some(profile) = data.as_mut()
            && let Some(number) = sqlx::query_scalar::<_, i64>("SELECT next_number FROM fiscal_number_sequences WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND environment=$2 AND model=55 AND series=$3")
                .bind(tenant).bind(profile.environment.as_str()).bind(i32::from(profile.series)).fetch_optional(&mut *tx).await.map_err(db)? {
            profile.next_number = Some(number.try_into().map_err(|_| access::AccessError::Internal)?);
        }
        let certificate_verified = certificates::verified(&state, &mut tx, tenant).await?;
        tx.commit().await.map_err(db)?;
        Ok(response(
            StatusCode::OK,
            Some(current),
            ProfileSnapshot {
                tenant_id: tenant,
                revision: current,
                can_edit,
                certificate_verified,
                data,
            },
        ))

      const [busy, setBusy] = useState("")
      const [blocked, setBlocked] = useState(false)

          if (controller.signal.aborted) return
          setErrorStatus(response.ok ? undefined : response.status)
          if (!response.ok) throw new Error(value.title || "Não foi possível consultar o certificado")
          const revision = response.headers.get("etag")
          if (!revision) throw new Error("Não foi possível confirmar a revisão do certificado")
          if (controller.signal.aborted) return

          tenant.current = value.tenantId

    ---
    
    # Brainstorming
    
    You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
    partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
    skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
    anything gets built.
    
    People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
    help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
    hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.
    
    ## First: What Do You Actually Know?
    
    Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
    why?
    
    - **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
      blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
    - **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.
    
    Before you start implementing, you must, in order:
    
    1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
       human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
    2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
    3. Get their approval of that doc.
    4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

                Self::BrasilCep | Self::BrasilCnpj => "BrasilAPI",
                Self::CnpjWs => "CNPJ.ws",
            }
        }
    }
    
    fn now_string(time: OffsetDateTime) -> String {
        time.format(&Rfc3339).expect("RFC3339 timestamp")
    }
    
    fn reserve(queue: &mut VecDeque<Instant>, maximum: usize, now: Instant) -> bool {
        while queue
            .front()
            .is_some_and(|old| now.duration_since(*old) >= Duration::from_secs(60))
        {
            queue.pop_front();
        }
        if queue.len() >= maximum {
            return false;
        }
        queue.push_back(now);
        true
    }
    
    impl RegistryClient {
        pub fn new(cnpj_ws_enabled: bool) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
            Ok(Self {
                http: reqwest::Client::builder()
                    .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
                    .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(1))
                    .timeout(PROVIDER_TIMEOUT)

    # ERP
    
    ERP modular da Ávila Ops, mantido em `avilaops/erp-next`. O sistema nasce separado do ERP legado e usa um monólito modular para preservar transações, contratos entre domínios e rastreabilidade.
    
    O [mapa de organização](architecture/README.md) explica cada pasta, os limites
    entre web/BFF/API/motor fiscal e onde colocar novas funcionalidades. As regras
    estão vinculadas ao Ávila Experiments e são verificadas no CI.
    
    ## Fundação
    
    - API: Rust, Axum e SQLx.
    - Banco: PostgreSQL 18.
    - Web: Next.js, React e TypeScript.
    - Multiempresa: `tenant_id`, políticas RLS e contexto transacional.
    - Segurança: Auth Ávila Ops será integrado por OIDC; permissões pertencem ao ERP.
    - Integração: outbox transacional; n8n consome eventos e não contém regras centrais.
    - Auditoria: registro append-only de ações relevantes.
    
    ## Desenvolvimento local
    
    1. Copie `.env.example` para `.env`.
    2. Execute `docker compose up -d postgres`.
    3. Com a conta de migração em `DATABASE_URL`, execute `cargo run -p erp-next-api -- migrate`.
    4. Com a conta de aplicação em `DATABASE_URL`, execute `cargo run -p erp-next-api`.
    5. Em outro terminal, execute `pnpm --filter web dev` (ou `pnpm dev:web` na raiz). O ERP Next abre em `http://localhost:3002`, sua porta padrão de desenvolvimento.
    
    A API não executa DDL ao iniciar o servidor HTTP. Em produção, a conta da
    aplicação deve ter `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS` e permissões apenas sobre as
    operações necessárias. Use outra conta para aplicar migrações.
    
    Endpoints iniciais:
    
    - `GET /health/live`: processo ativo.
    - `GET /health/ready`: API conectada ao PostgreSQL.
    
    Recursos empresariais implementados exigem Bearer válido e `X-Tenant-Id`:
    `/api/v1/me`, `/api/v1/users`, `/api/v1/roles`, `/api/v1/permissions`
    e `/api/v1/company`. O último oferece GET e PUT com ETag/If-Match.
    O contrato gerado está em `/openapi.json`.
    
    O primeiro ciclo comercial conecta produtos, clientes e fornecedores, estoque,
    pedidos e contas a receber. Confirmar um pedido reserva saldo; concluí-lo registra
    a saída e origina o título na mesma transação. Recebimentos integrais e estornos
    são declarações manuais, sem integração bancária. Os contratos estão em
    [pessoas](docs/PESSOAS-PERSISTENTES.md),
    [estoque](docs/ESTOQUE-PERSISTENTE.md) e
    [pedidos e financeiro](docs/PEDIDOS-FINANCEIRO.md).
    
    Usuários existentes podem ter a associação e os papéis alterados com controle
    de revisão. Papéis oferecem criação idempotente, alteração e exclusão autorizadas.
    Os [contratos e limites de acessos](docs/API-ACESSOS.md) detalham as operações,
    a proteção do último administrador e a pendência de convites no Auth.
    
    Para a web, use as variáveis de `apps/web/.env.example` no ambiente do Next.js
    (ou em `apps/web/.env.local` no desenvolvimento). A API Rust lê variáveis do
    processo: copiar um arquivo `.env` não as exporta automaticamente para o Cargo.
    Nunca publique os segredos como variáveis `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
    
    O [estado atual e as pendências](docs/STATUS-ERP.md) distinguem frontend
    demonstrativo, persistência testada e integração com serviços reais.
    
    A [continuidade fiscal e devoluções](docs/RETORNOS-E-CONTINUIDADE-FISCAL.md)
    acrescenta cancelamento comercial, estorno de recebimentos de compra, emissão e
    eventos NF-e 55/SP em homologação com adaptador interno, distribuição DF-e,
    manifestação e conversão de XML em compra. O recorte de regras fiscais e a
    configuração do motor estão documentados; não há inferência de tributação.
    Mantenha `NFE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED=false`. Testes locais não substituem homologação
    com certificado real nem publicam a funcionalidade em produção.
    
    A [segunda etapa de reconciliação](docs/COMISSOES-PRODUCAO-E-FISCAL.md) adiciona
    comissões sobre recebimentos, produção com consumo declarado e reconciliação
    atômica de cancelamentos. Também amplia a declaração fiscal para CRT 3 interno
    SP e prepara a imagem/overlay privado do motor. Percentuais e decisões fiscais
    continuam explícitos, sem preenchimento presumido.
    
    O [monitor fiscal canônico](docs/MONITOR-FISCAL-CANONICO.md) acrescenta coleta
    incremental com cursor por empresa, XML original e manifestação explícita do
    destinatário. Usa o cofre A1 existente e permanece desativado por padrão, sem
    alterar emissão, estoque ou financeiro.
    
    ## Domínios planejados
    
    O [verificador de rotas e fluxos](verification/README.md) gera um inventário
    atualizado e relatórios locais com `pnpm verify:erp`. A descoberta estática não
    aprova fluxos; probes e suítes de integração são registrados separadamente.
    
    Plataforma, Cadastros, Comercial, Estoque, Financeiro, Fiscal, Logística e Serviços. Um domínio não escreve diretamente nas tabelas de outro domínio.
    
    
    ## Conteúdo e contratos
    
    A integração de tipos OpenAPI na web, a ajuda MDX e o layout pessoal estão descritos em [Conteúdo e contratos](docs/CONTEUDO-E-CONTRATOS.md).
    
    Os [exemplos fiscais HTTP, n8n e MCP](docs/integrations/FISCAL-N8N-MCP.md)
    reutilizam a API Rust e documentam credenciais, idempotência, acompanhamento de
    estado, XML/DANFE e as dependências restantes para homologação e webhooks.

    # ERP Next em produção
    
    Imagens são construídas somente pelo GitHub CI, pelo workflow
    `production-release.yml`, com `source_ref` fixado no commit completo,
    depois das verificações de cada componente. PRs não reempacotam imagens.
    A implantação exige o resultado completo da execução aprovado.
    Os artefatos `erp-api-<sha>` e `erp-web-<sha>` contêm imagens Docker por SHA.
    O artefato `erp-fiscal-<sha>` contém o motor fiscal, após os testes próprios.
    
    O workflow de release tem timeout de 20 minutos para API e 15 para web.
    Falhas não autorizam build no servidor ou a retirada de testes.
    Os navegadores usam Chrome do runner.
    
    O workflow `production-migrate.yml`, com `release_run` apontando para uma
    execução já aprovada, executa migrations/bootstrap e importação **no runner GitHub**,
    conectado ao PostgreSQL por túnel SSH restrito a `172.17.0.1:5432`, sujeito a
    autenticação SCRAM em vez das regras trust de loopback. A chave do
    túnel não permite sessão ou execução de comandos. Os segredos são configurados
    no GitHub: `ERP_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`, `ERP_DB_TUNNEL_KEY`,
    `ERP_DB_KNOWN_HOSTS`, `ERP_DB_SSH_HOST`, `ERP_BOOTSTRAP_SUB` e
    `ERP_BOOTSTRAP_TENANT` e `ERP_LEGACY_DATABASE_URL`. Nunca executar o comando
    `migrate` no servidor. O importador recusa um destino que já contém os schemas
    legados; não repetir o fluxo após a importação concluída.
    Antes de usar a imagem, confere que a revisão de origem possui os mesmos fontes
    Rust, lockfile e migrations da revisão que está fazendo o provisionamento.
    
    O bootstrap cria uma empresa com cadastro fiscal pendente e associa a identidade
    real confirmada de `nicolas@avilaops.com` ao papel de administrador. O banco é
    independente do legado e recebe a cópia e projeção dos dados após o bootstrap.
    A conexão de runtime usa papel sem superusuário,
    sem BYPASSRLS e sem propriedade das tabelas.
    
    O diretório de release recebe somente `compose.yaml`, imagens prontas e arquivos
    privados `api.env`, `web.env` e `.env`. `api.env` contém `DATABASE_URL`,
    `AUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.avilaops.com`, `NFE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED=false` e
    `NFE_PRODUCTION_TENANT_ID` vazio. Se a emissão de produção for liberada para
    uma única empresa, as duas variáveis devem ser ativadas juntas e o UUID do
    tenant autorizado deve ser informado; não existe liberação global segura.
    Quando o pacote documental estiver habilitado, o mesmo `api.env` recebe
    `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` e `SMTP_FROM`; esses
    valores são secretos do relay e não podem ser copiados para `web.env` ou
    versionados.
    O workflow de migração também aplica `deploy/grant-commercial-contracts.sql`,
    concedendo ao papel runtime somente `SELECT`, `INSERT` e `UPDATE` na tabela de
    estado do pacote; a API não recebe permissão de exclusão desses registros.
    `web.env` contém `ERP_AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `ERP_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`,
    `ERP_SESSION_SECRET` e `ERP_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`. `.env` fixa `ERP_API_IMAGE` e
    `ERP_WEB_IMAGE` e `ERP_RELEASE_SHA`. Não versionar esses arquivos preenchidos.
    
    Web e API compartilham o namespace de rede do serviço API; o BFF usa
    `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Isso mantém a exigência existente de HTTPS ou loopback,
    sem liberar HTTP para hosts arbitrários. As duas portas são publicadas pelo
    serviço API, somente no loopback do servidor.
    
    O cliente OIDC dedicado `erp-next` pertence ao app Auth `erp` e aceita somente
    `https://erp.avilaops.com/api/auth/callback` como redirect de login e
    `https://erp.avilaops.com/api/auth/logout/central/callback` como post-logout
    redirect. Não alterar o segredo do cliente
    legado `erp`. O BFF mantém tokens em cookie HttpOnly cifrado e a API consulta
    userinfo e valida a associação da empresa. O usuário conclui o login no Auth;
    nenhuma senha pessoal é necessária ao deploy.
    
    A saída começa com POST de mesma origem, apaga os cookies locais e cria um
    marcador cifrado HttpOnly com validade de dois minutos. A navegação seguinte
    consulta o `end_session_endpoint` do discovery do issuer configurado e usa
    somente o cliente e o retorno definidos pelo servidor. Os GETs de continuação
    e callback exigem a fase correspondente desse marcador; o callback não apaga
    uma sessão criada depois da saída. Falha no Auth não comprova logout global.
    Os controles de saída usam fetch com redirecionamento manual antes de navegar,
    preservando a verificação de origem sob a política `no-referrer`.
    
    Carregar imagens com `docker load`; iniciar por `docker compose up -d --no-build
    --wait`. O web escuta somente em `127.0.0.1:3140`, compatível com o proxy do
    domínio; a API em `127.0.0.1:3141`. Conferir saúde da API, web e redirect OIDC.
    O legado permanece parado e preservado em seu diretório. Rollback interrompe
    somente o projeto Compose `erp-next`; nunca restaura dados por troca de imagem.
    
    ## Motor fiscal em homologação
    
    O overlay opcional `fiscal-compose.yaml` adiciona a imagem fiscal validada pela
    mesma execução de release. Carregar `fiscal-image.tar.gz` e configurar, no `.env`
    privado do release, `ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_IMAGE=erp-next-fiscal:sha-<sha-completo>` e
    `ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_TOKEN` com segredo aleatório de pelo menos 24 caracteres. Não
    usar token de exemplo nem imprimir `docker compose config` sem ocultar segredos.
    
    O motor compartilha o namespace da API e escuta somente `127.0.0.1:8091`, sem
    publicação de porta. O overlay configura a mesma origem/token na API. O health
    check autenticado confirma o processo e o ambiente de homologação; não consulta
    a SEFAZ e não comprova certificado ou autorização de uma nota.
    
    Após migrations e configuração autorizadas, usar os dois arquivos Compose com
    `up -d --no-build --wait`. A imagem do motor roda sem root, com filesystem somente
    leitura e diretório temporário limitado. A API conserva os certificados cifrados
    e envia material em memória somente durante uma operação autenticada.
    
    A habilitação de consulta automática DF-e requer também o tenant e responsável
    explicitamente configurados no `api.env`. Não configurar automação como efeito
    colateral do provisionamento do motor. Produção fiscal continua bloqueada.
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -Eeuo pipefail
    umask 077
    
    readonly ROOT=/mnt/HC_Volume_106542212/erp-next
    readonly APPLICATION=erp-next
    
    fail() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
    
    [[ $# == 0 ]] || fail 'invalid dispatcher arguments'
    original_command=${SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND:-}
    [[ "$original_command" =~ ^deploy\ erp-next\ ([0-9a-f]{40})$ ]] || fail 'invalid deploy command'
    source_sha=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
    [[ $EUID == 0 ]] || fail 'dispatcher requires root'
    
    exec 9>"$ROOT/.deploy.lock"
    flock -n 9 || fail 'another ERP deployment is running'
    
    previous_release=$(docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir" }}' erp-next-web-1)
    [[ "$previous_release" == "$ROOT/releases/"* ]] || fail 'active release is not managed by this dispatcher'
    
    staging=$(mktemp -d "$ROOT/.incoming.XXXXXX")
    release="$ROOT/releases/$source_sha"
    cleanup() { rm -rf -- "$staging"; }
    trap cleanup EXIT
    
    # Extract the complete stream first, then enforce the allow-list below. GNU tar
    # does not reliably match the selected names when the sender emits ./ prefixes.
    tar --extract --gzip --no-same-owner --directory "$staging" --file -
    
    for file in api-image.tar.gz web-image.tar.gz fiscal-image.tar.gz compose.yaml fiscal-compose.yaml; do
      [[ -s "$staging/$file" ]] || fail "missing artifact: $file"
    done
    [[ ! -e "$release" ]] || fail 'release already exists'
    
    for image in api web fiscal; do
      docker load --input "$staging/$image-image.tar.gz" >/dev/null
      docker image inspect "erp-next-$image:sha-$source_sha" >/dev/null || fail "image not loaded: $image"
    done
    
    mkdir -m 700 "$release"
    
    if [[ -f "$previous_release/compose.json" ]]; then
      # Current production still uses a generated, self-contained Compose JSON.
      # Keep its private runtime configuration on the server and replace only the
      # three immutable image references.
      cp -p "$previous_release/compose.json" "$release/compose.json"
      python3 - "$release/compose.json" <<'PY'
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    import sys
    
    target = Path(sys.argv[1])
    config = json.loads(target.read_text())
    config["services"]["fiscal-engine"]["healthcheck"]["test"] = ["CMD", "node", "scripts/healthcheck.mjs"]
    target.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2))
    PY
      # The generated JSON carries the public release marker in the web
      # environment; update it together with the immutable image references.
      sed -i "s|\"ERP_RELEASE_SHA\": \"[0-9a-f]*\"|\"ERP_RELEASE_SHA\": \"$source_sha\"|g" "$release/compose.json"
      previous_api=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' erp-next-api-1)
      previous_web=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' erp-next-web-1)
      previous_fiscal=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' erp-next-fiscal-engine-1)
      for pair in \
        "$previous_api|erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha" \
        "$previous_web|erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha" \
        "$previous_fiscal|erp-next-fiscal:sha-$source_sha"; do
        old=${pair%%|*}
        new=${pair#*|}
        escaped_old=$(printf '%s' "$old" | sed 's/[.[\*^$()+?{|\\]/\\&/g')
        sed -i "s|$escaped_old|$new|g" "$release/compose.json"
      done
      grep -q "erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'API image was not pinned'
      grep -q "erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'web image was not pinned'
      grep -q "erp-next-fiscal:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'fiscal image was not pinned'
      grep -q "\\\"ERP_RELEASE_SHA\\\": \\\"$source_sha\\\"" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'release SHA was not pinned'
      compose_file=compose.json
      compose_env_args=()
    else
      [[ -f "$previous_release/compose.yaml" && -f "$previous_release/api.env" && -f "$previous_release/web.env" && -f "$previous_release/.env" ]] || fail 'active release has an unknown layout'
      cp -p "$staging/compose.yaml" "$staging/fiscal-compose.yaml" "$release/"
      cp -p "$previous_release/api.env" "$previous_release/web.env" "$previous_release/.env" "$release/"
      chmod 600 "$release/api.env" "$release/web.env" "$release/.env"
      sed -i \
        -e "s|^ERP_API_IMAGE=.*|ERP_API_IMAGE=erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha|" \
        -e "s|^ERP_WEB_IMAGE=.*|ERP_WEB_IMAGE=erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha|" \
        -e "s|^ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_IMAGE=.*|ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_IMAGE=erp-next-fiscal:sha-$source_sha|" \
        -e "s|^ERP_RELEASE_SHA=.*|ERP_RELEASE_SHA=$source_sha|" \
        "$release/.env"
      grep -q "^ERP_API_IMAGE=erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'API image was not pinned'
      grep -q "^ERP_WEB_IMAGE=erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'web image was not pinned'
      grep -q "^ERP_RELEASE_SHA=$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'release SHA was not pinned'
      compose_file=compose.yaml
      compose_env_args=(--env-file "$release/.env")
    fi
    
    compose() {
      docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$1" \
        "${compose_env_args[@]}" --file "$1/$compose_file" "${@:2}"
    }
    
    rollback() {
      local status=$?
      trap - EXIT
      printf '%s\n' 'ERP deploy failed; restoring previous release' >&2
      if [[ -f "$previous_release/compose.json" ]]; then
        docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$previous_release" \
          --file "$previous_release/compose.json" up --detach --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 120 || true
      else
        docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$previous_release" \
          --env-file "$previous_release/.env" --file "$previous_release/compose.yaml" \
          --file "$previous_release/fiscal-compose.yaml" up --detach --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 120 || true
      fi
      exit "$status"
    }
    
    trap rollback ERR
    compose "$release" config --quiet
    compose "$release" up --detach --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 120
    
    curl --fail --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
      http://127.0.0.1:3141/health/ready >/dev/null
    
    python3 - "$source_sha" <<'PY'
    import json
    import sys
    import urllib.request
    
    expected = sys.argv[1]
    with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:3140/api/health", timeout=10) as response:
        health = json.load(response)
    if health.get("commit") != expected or health.get("ok") is not True:
        raise SystemExit("ERP health does not match the requested release")
    for path in ("/entrar", "/erp-preview.webp"):
        with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:3140" + path, timeout=10) as response:
            if response.status != 200:
                raise SystemExit(f"ERP public path failed: {path}")
    print(json.dumps({"application": health.get("application"), "commit": health.get("commit")}))
    PY
    
    trap - EXIT
    printf 'ERP deploy completed: %s\n' "$source_sha"
    services:
      api:
        image: ${ERP_API_IMAGE:?CI image required}
        restart: unless-stopped
        env_file: api.env
        extra_hosts:
          - host.docker.internal:host-gateway
        networks: [erp]
        ports:
          - "127.0.0.1:3141:8080"
          - "127.0.0.1:3140:3000"
        security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
        cap_drop: [ALL]
      web:
        image: ${ERP_WEB_IMAGE:?CI image required}
        restart: unless-stopped
        env_file: web.env
        environment:
          ERP_API_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080
          ERP_WEB_ORIGIN: https://erp.avilaops.com
          AUTH_ISSUER: https://auth.avilaops.com
          ERP_RELEASE_SHA: ${ERP_RELEASE_SHA:?CI revision required}
        depends_on:
          api:
            condition: service_healthy
        network_mode: service:api
        security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
        cap_drop: [ALL]
    networks:
      erp:
    name: Production release
    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          source_ref:
            description: Exact source commit to validate and package
            required: true
            type: string
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    jobs:
      fiscal-engine:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: npm test
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: docker build -f apps/fiscal-engine/Dockerfile -t erp-next-fiscal:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} .
          - run: docker save erp-next-fiscal:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} | gzip > fiscal-image.tar.gz
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-fiscal-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: fiscal-image.tar.gz
              compression-level: 0
              retention-days: 7
      api:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 20
        services:
          postgres:
            image: postgres:18-alpine
            env:
              POSTGRES_DB: erp_next_test
              POSTGRES_USER: postgres
              POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ci_isolated_only
            ports: ['5432:5432']
            options: >-
              --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres"
              --health-interval 2s --health-timeout 3s --health-retries 20
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:ci_isolated_only@127.0.0.1:5432/erp_next_test
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.99.1
            with:
              components: rustfmt,clippy
          - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
          - run: cargo fmt --all --check
          - run: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
          - name: Test and export the exact source contract
            run: |
              mkdir -p artifacts/contracts
              ERP_OPENAPI_OUTPUT="$PWD/artifacts/contracts/candidate.json" cargo test --locked --workspace -- --test-threads=2
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-release-openapi-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/contracts/candidate.json
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 7
          - run: cargo build --release --locked -p erp-next-api
          - run: docker build -f deploy/api.Dockerfile -t erp-next-api:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} .
          - run: docker save erp-next-api:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} | gzip > api-image.tar.gz
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-api-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: api-image.tar.gz
              compression-level: 0
              retention-days: 7
      web:
        needs: api
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 20
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
            with:
              version: 11.11.0
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
              cache: pnpm
          - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          - run: pnpm --filter web lint
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-release-openapi-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/contracts/
          - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
            working-directory: scripts/contracts/consumer
          - run: node scripts/contracts/generate-web.mjs
          - run: node --test tests/fiscal-tax-model.node.mjs
            working-directory: apps/web
          - run: pnpm --filter web build

    ---
    name: executing-plans
    description: Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available
    ---
    
    # Executing Plans
    
    Execute the plan yourself, task by task, in this session: no implementer
    subagent per task, no reviewer per task. One fresh-context review of the
    whole branch at the end.
    
    **Why inline:** Subagent-driven development pays for a fresh implementer
    and a fresh reviewer on every task, each re-reading the codebase from zero.
    Inline execution pays for one context (yours) plus one reviewer at the end.
    What it gives up is a fresh context per task and a second pair of eyes per
    task. This skill keeps what those two things bought, by other means: the
    brief is the spec, the ledger is your memory, TDD is the per-task gate, and
    the final reviewer is the second pair of eyes.
    
    **Core principle:** The plan already did the thinking. Execute it exactly,
    prove each step with a test you watched fail and then pass, and leave a
    record that survives your own forgetting.
    
    **Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
    ledger and the tool results carry the record.
    
    **Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner
    between tasks. They chose inline execution to spend less, not to answer
    "should I continue?" after every task. Execute all tasks from the plan
    without stopping.
    
    **Rulings, not stalls.** Conflicts, ambiguities, plan defects — decide them.
    The spec is the binding authority, the plan is its argument, and your
    judgment settles what neither answers. Record every decision in the ledger
    as `Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`, and keep
    going. Deviating from the plan without a ledgered ruling is a decision made
    in secret.
    
    Four things stop you, and only these: an irreversible or destructive
    operation; a security-sensitive action; a side effect outside this worktree
    that norms say you ask about first (a merge, a push to a shared branch, a
    publish); and a plan so broken that every path forward is a guess. For
    those, stop and ask.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    - You have a plan from superpowers:writing-plans and your human partner
      chose inline execution at the handoff.
    - Your harness has no subagent tool (see the per-platform references in
      `../using-superpowers/references/`). Never fabricate a dispatch; run
      the plan here.
    - Tasks are mostly independent — the same precondition as
      superpowers:subagent-driven-development.
    
    A fully specified plan makes inline execution transcription plus testing:
    it runs well on a mid-tier session model, and the one place the most
    capable model earns its cost is the final review, which this skill
    dispatches separately. Tell your human partner so when they choose inline.
    
    Prefer superpowers:subagent-driven-development when your human partner
    wants a review gate on every task, or when the plan is long enough that
    its later tasks would run on a compacted context. Inline execution over a
    long plan still works — the ledger is what makes it recoverable — but the
    last tasks get the least of you.

    ---
    name: writing-plans
    description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
    ---
    
    # Writing Plans
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.
    
    **Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."
    
    **Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.
    
    **Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
    - (User preferences for plan location override this default)
    
    ## Scope Check
    
    If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.
    
    ## File Structure
    
    Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.
    
    - Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
    - You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
    - Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.
    
    This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.
    
    ## Task Right-Sizing
    
    A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
    fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
    configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
    deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
    reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
    independently testable deliverable.
    
    ## Step Granularity
    
    **Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
    - "Write the failing test" - step
    - "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
    - "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
    - "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
    - "Commit" - step

    # Publicação da versão local do ERP
    
    Solicitação: publicar a aplicação atualmente editada neste computador.
    
    ## Restrições
    
    - Preservar a orientação do usuário de não usar Git durante a preparação.
    - Usar o fluxo documentado em deploy/README.md: imagens validadas no GitHub CI, sem compilação no servidor.
    - Preservar configurações privadas e os dados existentes; nenhuma emissão fiscal é parte do deploy.
    - Não habilitar emissão em produção nem automações fiscais como efeito colateral.
    
    ## Etapas
    
    1. Identificar destino, dependências e fluxo de release pelos arquivos locais.
    2. Validar formatação Rust, frontend e testes fiscais; registrar resultados e corrigir falhas dentro do escopo.
    3. Conferir compatibilidade das migrations e das dependências do MCP fiscal local com o ambiente de publicação.
    4. Preparar inventário e manifesto da versão local, sem segredos ou arquivos de desenvolvimento.
    5. Resolver a autorização para versionamento/publicação somente após apresentar a versão concreta e os resultados, pois a orientação anterior proíbe Git e o fluxo de release exige um commit remoto.
    6. Com autorização compatível, executar CI e deploy, validar domínio, saúde e revisão; usar rollback do dispatcher se necessário.
    
    ## Evidências iniciais
    
    - Destino documentado: https://erp.avilaops.com; dispatcher no host applications.
    - Componentes: API Rust, frontend Next.js e motor fiscal Node.js.
    - Dependência adicional das novas modalidades: MCP fiscal Python local com ferramentas e schemas ampliados; não presumir que o MCP remoto possui essas alterações.
    - O banco já recebeu as migrations fiscais 202611060003, 202611060004, 202611060005 e 202611080003 nesta sessão.
    - O fluxo exige fmt, clippy sem warnings, testes Rust, lint/build/UI web e testes do motor.

    Imagens são construídas somente pelo GitHub CI, pelo workflow

    depois das verificações de cada componente. PRs não reempacotam imagens.

    O workflow de release tem timeout de 20 minutos para API e 15 para web.

    # Imagem Docker do mcp-fiscal-brasil
    # Multi-stage para imagem final enxuta com uv.
    #
    # Build:
    #   docker build -t mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0 .
    #
    # Run (servidor MCP stdio):
    #   docker run --rm -i mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0
    #
    # Run (REST API + Web UI):
    #   docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0 mcp-fiscal-api
    #
    # Run (MCP HTTP transport):
    #   docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 mcp-fiscal-brasil:0.2.0 mcp-fiscal-brasil --transport http
    #
    # Variaveis de ambiente uteis:
    #   MCP_FISCAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT=30
    #   MCP_FISCAL_CACHE_TTL=300
    #   MCP_FISCAL_RATE_LIMIT=10
    #   HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=8000
    
    # ---- Build stage ----
    FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
    
    ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
        PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    
    WORKDIR /build
    
    COPY pyproject.toml README.md LICENSE ./
    COPY src/ ./src/
    
    RUN pip install --no-cache-dir hatchling build && \
        python -m build --wheel
    
    # ---- Runtime stage ----
    FROM python:3.12-slim AS runtime
    
    ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
        PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
        PORT=8000 \
        HOST=0.0.0.0
    
    WORKDIR /app
    
    COPY --from=builder /build/dist/*.whl ./
    COPY scripts/docker_healthcheck.py ./docker_healthcheck.py
    
    RUN pip install --no-cache-dir *.whl && \
        rm -f *.whl && \
        groupadd -r app && useradd -r -g app -d /app -s /usr/sbin/nologin app && \
        chown -R app:app /app
    
    USER app
    
    EXPOSE 8000
    
    # O CMD padrao (mcp-fiscal-brasil, stdio) nao abre porta HTTP. O healthcheck
    # detecta automaticamente qual modo esta rodando: se a porta estiver
    # escutando, valida via GET /health; caso contrario, confirma so que o
    # pacote importa (modo stdio). Ver scripts/docker_healthcheck.py.
    HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
        CMD python docker_healthcheck.py || exit 1
    
    # Comando padrao: servidor MCP via stdio (uso por clientes MCP nativos).

        needs: [fiscal-engine, api, web, mlops-evidence]

    ---
    name: requesting-code-review
    description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
    ---
    
    # Requesting Code Review
    
    Dispatch a code reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade. The reviewer gets precisely crafted context for evaluation — never your session's history.
    
    **Core principle:** Review early, review often.
    
    ## When to Request Review
    
    **Mandatory:**
    - After each task in subagent-driven development
    - After completing major feature
    - Before merge to main
    
    **Optional but valuable:**
    - When stuck (fresh perspective)
    - Before refactoring (baseline check)
    - After fixing complex bug
    
    ## How to Request
    
    **1. Get git SHAs:**
    ```bash
    BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or: git merge-base origin/main HEAD
    HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    ```
    
    **2. Dispatch code reviewer subagent:**
    
    Dispatch a `general-purpose` subagent, filling the template at [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)
    
    **Placeholders:**
    - `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary of what you built
    - `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
    - `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
    - `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit
    
    **3. Act on feedback:**
    - Fix Critical issues immediately
    - Fix Important issues before proceeding
    - Note Minor issues for later
    - Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)
    
    ## Example
    
    ```
    [Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]
    
    You: Let me request code review before proceeding.
    
    BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1)
    HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    
    [Dispatch code reviewer subagent]
      DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types
      PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/superpowers/plans/deployment-plan.md
      BASE_SHA: a7981ec
      HEAD_SHA: 3df7661
    
    [Subagent returns]:
      Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
      Issues:
        Important: Missing progress indicators
        Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
      Assessment: Ready to proceed
    
    You: [Fix progress indicators]
    [Continue to Task 3]
    ```
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "I'll just review the diff myself instead of dispatching a reviewer" | You're the coordinator — reviewing the diff inline burns the context window you need to keep driving the work. Dispatch a reviewer subagent: the diff and the evaluation live in its context, and only the findings come back to you. |
    | "The reviewer needs my whole session history to understand the change" | Hand it precisely crafted context, never your session's history. That keeps the reviewer on the work product, not your thought process. |
    
    ## Red Flags
    
    **Never:**
    - Skip review because "it's simple"
    - Ignore Critical issues
    - Proceed with unfixed Important issues
    - Argue with valid technical feedback
    
    **If reviewer wrong:**
    ---
    name: verification-before-completion
    description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
    ---
    
    # Verification Before Completion
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.
    
    **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
    ```
    
    If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.
    
    ## The Gate Function
    
    ```
    BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:
    
    1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
    2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
    3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
    4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
       - If NO: State actual status with evidence
       - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
    5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim
    
    Skip any step = lying, not verifying
    ```
    
    ## Common Failures
    
    | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |

    const TENANT: &str = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111";

    const PRODUCT: &str = "11111111-2222-4333-8444-666666666666";
    const EDITOR_ROLE: &str = "99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999";
    
    async fn call(
        router: &Router,
        method: &str,
        uri: &str,
        subject: &str,
        revision: Option<i64>,
        key: Option<Uuid>,
        body: Value,
    ) -> (StatusCode, Value, Option<String>) {
        let mut request = Request::builder()
            .method(method)
            .uri(uri)
            .header("x-tenant-id", TENANT)
            .header("content-type", "application/json")
            .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {subject}"));
        if let Some(revision) = revision {
            request = request.header("if-match", format!("\"{revision}\""));
        }
        if let Some(key) = key {
            request = request.header("idempotency-key", key.to_string());
        }
        let result = router
            .clone()
            .oneshot(request.body(Body::from(body.to_string())).unwrap())
            )

    import { createHash } from "node:crypto";

    const root = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../", import.meta.url));
    const sha256 = bytes => createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex");
    const SHA = /^[a-f0-9]{40}$/;
    const TEXT_MAX = 20 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    export function validateReleaseInputs(input) {
      if (!SHA.test(input.sourceSha ?? "") || !SHA.test(input.checkoutSha ?? "") ||
          input.sourceSha !== input.checkoutSha) throw new Error("SOURCE_SHA_MISMATCH");
      if (input.ref !== "refs/heads/main") throw new Error("NOT_MAIN_BRANCH");
      if (!/^[0-9]+$/.test(String(input.runId ?? "")) || !/^[1-9][0-9]*$/.test(String(input.runAttempt ?? ""))) {
        throw new Error("INVALID_RUN_ID");
      }
      if (typeof input.repository !== "string" || input.repository.toLowerCase() !== "avilaops/erp-next") {
        throw new Error("REPOSITORY_MISMATCH");
      }
      for (const name of ["fiscal-engine", "api", "web"]) {
        if (input.jobs?.[name]?.result !== "success") throw new Error("REQUIRED_JOB_NOT_SUCCESS:" + name);
      }
    }
    
    export function inspectOpenApi(bytes) {
      if (!bytes.length || bytes.length > TEXT_MAX) throw new Error("INVALID_OPENAPI_SIZE");
      const doc = JSON.parse(bytes.toString("utf8"));
      if (!/^3\.[01]\.\d+$/.test(doc.openapi ?? "") ||
          !doc.info?.title || !doc.paths || Array.isArray(doc.paths) ||
          Object.keys(doc.paths).length === 0) throw new Error("INVALID_OPENAPI");
      function refs(value) {
        if (!value || typeof value !== "object") return;
        if (Object.hasOwn(value, "$ref") && (typeof value.$ref !== "string" || !value.$ref.startsWith("#/"))) {
          throw new Error("EXTERNAL_OPENAPI_REF");
        }
        for (const child of Object.values(value)) refs(child);
      }
      refs(doc);
      return { pathCount: Object.keys(doc.paths).length, sha256: sha256(bytes) };
    }
    
    export function inspectValidation(manifestBytes, pdfBytes, pngBytes) {
      if (manifestBytes.length > 100_000 || pdfBytes.length > TEXT_MAX || pngBytes.length > TEXT_MAX) throw new Error("INVALID_VALIDATION_SIZE");
      const doc = JSON.parse(manifestBytes.toString("utf8"));
      if (!Array.isArray(doc.fields) || doc.fields.length !== 11 || new Set(doc.fields.map(f => f.name)).size !== 11) {
        throw new Error("INVALID_VALIDATION_FIELDS");
      }
      if (!pdfBytes.subarray(0, 5).equals(Buffer.from("%PDF-"))) throw new Error("INVALID_VALIDATION_PDF");
      if (!pngBytes.subarray(0, 8).equals(Buffer.from([137,80,78,71,13,10,26,10]))) throw new Error("INVALID_VALIDATION_PNG");
      if (sha256(pdfBytes) !== doc.sha256) throw new Error("VALIDATION_PDF_HASH_MISMATCH");
      return { fieldCount: 11, manifestSha256: sha256(manifestBytes), pdfSha256: sha256(pdfBytes), pngSha256: sha256(pngBytes) };
    }
    
    export async function evaluateRelease(input, artifactDirectory) {
      validateReleaseInputs(input);
      const evidence = resolve(artifactDirectory);
      const [contract, manifest, pdf, png] = await Promise.all([
        readFile(join(evidence, "contracts", "candidate.json")),
        readFile(join(evidence, "validation", "validation.json")),
        readFile(join(evidence, "validation", "validation.pdf")),
        readFile(join(evidence, "validation", "validation.png")),
      ]);
      return {
        schemaVersion: "avila-mlops-release-evidence/1",
        identity: {
          repository: input.repository, sourceSha: input.sourceSha,
          workflowRunId: String(input.runId), attempt: Number(input.runAttempt),
        },
        jobs: Object.fromEntries(["fiscal-engine", "api", "web"].map(n => [n, "success"])),
        evidence: { openapi: inspectOpenApi(contract), validation: inspectValidation(manifest, pdf, png) },
        metrics: { aiQuality: null, tokenCostUsd: null, llmLatencyMs: null, regressionsMeasured: null },
        technicalVerdict: "passed",
        humanApproval: "not_evaluated",
        productionSmoke: "not_evaluated",
        note: "Apenas contrato e artefatos produzidos nos jobs reais deste workflow. Não prova deploy nem aprovação humana.",
      };
    }
    
    async function main() {
      const input = {
        repository: process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY,
        sourceSha: process.env.SOURCE_SHA,
        checkoutSha: execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8", cwd: root }).trim(),

        env:

    """Exercise the packaged MCP using synthetic XML; never calls SEFAZ."""
    import base64
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    import runpy
    import sys
    import time
    import urllib.request
    
    origin = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://127.0.0.1:8093"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"}
    
    
    def rpc(method, request_id=None, params=None):
        body = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
        if request_id is not None:
            body["id"] = request_id
        if params is not None:
            body["params"] = params
        request = urllib.request.Request(origin + "/mcp", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers=headers)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
            if response.headers.get("Mcp-Session-Id"):
                headers["Mcp-Session-Id"] = response.headers["Mcp-Session-Id"]
            if response.status == 202:
                return None
            if "application/json" in response.headers.get("Content-Type", ""):
                value = json.load(response)
            else:
                value = None
                for line in response:
                    if line.startswith(b"data:"):
                        candidate = json.loads(line[5:])
                        if candidate.get("id") == request_id:
                            value = candidate
                            break
            if not value or "error" in value:
                raise RuntimeError("MCP request failed: " + method)
            return value["result"]
    
    
    def tool(name, arguments, request_id):
        value = rpc("tools/call", request_id, {"name": name, "arguments": arguments})
        if value.get("isError"):
            raise RuntimeError("MCP tool failed: " + name)
        return value.get("structuredContent") or json.loads(next(item["text"] for item in value["content"] if item["type"] == "text"))
    
    
    for attempt in range(30):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(origin + "/health", timeout=3) as response:
                assert response.status == 200
            break
        except Exception:
            if attempt == 29:
                raise
            time.sleep(1)
    
    rpc("initialize", 1, {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "erp-release-smoke", "version": "1"}})
    rpc("notifications/initialized")
    headers["MCP-Protocol-Version"] = "2025-06-18"
    tools = rpc("tools/list", 2)["tools"]
    names = {entry["name"] for entry in tools}
    assert {"validar_xml_fiscal", "validar_assinatura_nfe", "gerar_danfe_simplificado_tipo2"} <= names
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    xml = (root / "tests/fixtures/schema-valid-nfe.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert tool("validar_xml_fiscal", {"xml_content": xml}, 3)["valido"] is True
    synthetic = runpy.run_path(str(root / "tests/test_simplified_danfe.py"))["fixture"]()
    pdf = tool("gerar_danfe_simplificado_tipo2", {"xml_content": synthetic}, 4)
    assert base64.b64decode(pdf["pdf_base64"], validate=True).startswith(b"%PDF-")
    print(json.dumps({"tools": len(names), "schemaValidation": "passed", "syntheticPdf": "passed"}))

    import { expect, test, type BrowserContext } from "@playwright/test"
    import { createCipheriv, createHash, randomBytes } from "node:crypto"
    import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises"
    
    const origin = process.env.ERP_TEST_WEB_ORIGIN || "http://127.0.0.1:3202"

    let fixture: Record<string, string>
    test.beforeAll(async () => { fixture = JSON.parse(await readFile("../api/tests/fixtures/a1-synthetic.json", "utf8")) })
    
    // Synthetic identity and synthetic CA, restricted to the isolated local database.
    async function session(context: BrowserContext, reader = false) {
      const iv = randomBytes(12)
      const cipher = createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", createHash("sha256").update(process.env.ERP_SESSION_SECRET!).digest(), iv)
      cipher.setAAD(Buffer.from("erp-session"))
      const encrypted = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(JSON.stringify({ accessToken: reader ? "fixture-reader-token" : "fixture-editor-token", tenantId: tenant, expiresAt: Date.now() + 3600_000 })), cipher.final()])
      await context.addCookies([{ name: "erp_session", value: Buffer.concat([iv, cipher.getAuthTag(), encrypted]).toString("base64url"), url: origin, httpOnly: true, sameSite: "Lax" }])
    }
    
    test("certificado A1 conecta, persiste, substitui com revisão e remove pela interface", async ({ page, context }, info) => {

    202611060107_logistics_postings.sql
    CREATE TABLE logistics_postings (
        id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
        code text NOT NULL,
        order_id uuid,
        recipient_name text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(btrim(recipient_name)) BETWEEN 2 AND 200),
        carrier text,
        service text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(btrim(service)) BETWEEN 2 AND 80),
        tracking_code text,
        destination_city text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(btrim(destination_city)) BETWEEN 2 AND 120),
        destination_state text NOT NULL CHECK (destination_state ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'),
        package_count integer NOT NULL CHECK (package_count BETWEEN 1 AND 999),
        weight_grams bigint NOT NULL CHECK (weight_grams BETWEEN 1 AND 999999999),
        declared_value_cents bigint NOT NULL CHECK (declared_value_cents BETWEEN 0 AND 99999999999999),
        status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'prepared' CHECK (status IN ('prepared', 'posted', 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'cancelled')),
        revision bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (revision > 0),
        created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, id),
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, code),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, order_id) REFERENCES sales_orders(tenant_id, id)
    );
    CREATE INDEX logistics_postings_tenant_created_idx ON logistics_postings(tenant_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);
    CREATE INDEX logistics_postings_tenant_status_idx ON logistics_postings(tenant_id, status, created_at DESC);
    
    ALTER TABLE logistics_postings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    ALTER TABLE logistics_postings FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    CREATE POLICY logistics_postings_isolation ON logistics_postings
        USING (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid)
        WITH CHECK (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid);
    
    INSERT INTO permissions(code, description) VALUES

    ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING;

    CREATE TABLE logistics_checkouts (
        id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
        order_id uuid NOT NULL,
        status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'counting' CHECK (status IN ('counting', 'completed', 'cancelled')),
        revision bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (revision > 0),
        started_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        completed_at timestamptz,
        created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, id),
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, order_id),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, order_id) REFERENCES sales_orders(tenant_id, id),
        CHECK ((status = 'completed' AND completed_at IS NOT NULL) OR (status <> 'completed'))
    );
    
    CREATE TABLE logistics_checkout_lines (
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
        checkout_id uuid NOT NULL,
        line_number integer NOT NULL CHECK (line_number BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
        product_id uuid NOT NULL,
        sku text NOT NULL,
        name text NOT NULL,
        expected_quantity_micros bigint NOT NULL CHECK (expected_quantity_micros > 0),
        checked_quantity_micros bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (checked_quantity_micros >= 0),
        PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, checkout_id, line_number),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, checkout_id) REFERENCES logistics_checkouts(tenant_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        CHECK (checked_quantity_micros <= expected_quantity_micros)
    );
    
    CREATE INDEX logistics_checkouts_tenant_created_idx ON logistics_checkouts(tenant_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);
    CREATE INDEX logistics_checkout_lines_product_idx ON logistics_checkout_lines(tenant_id, product_id, checkout_id);

    -- Outbound customer packages are separate from the signing-provider state.
    -- SMTP acceptance is recorded without storing message bodies or credentials.
    CREATE TABLE commercial_contract_deliveries (
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
        contract_id uuid NOT NULL,
        status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('sending', 'sent', 'failed', 'unknown')),
        recipients jsonb NOT NULL CHECK (jsonb_typeof(recipients) = 'array'),
        attachments jsonb NOT NULL CHECK (jsonb_typeof(attachments) = 'array'),
        message_sha256 text NOT NULL CHECK (message_sha256 ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
        attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (attempts > 0),
        last_error text,
        sent_at timestamptz,
        updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, contract_id),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, contract_id) REFERENCES commercial_contracts(tenant_id, id),
        CHECK ((status = 'sent') = (sent_at IS NOT NULL))
    );
    
    ALTER TABLE commercial_contract_deliveries ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    ALTER TABLE commercial_contract_deliveries FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

        USING (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid)
        WITH CHECK (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid);

    CREATE TABLE financial_account_transfers (

        reference text CHECK (reference IS NULL OR char_length(reference) <= 200),
        created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, id),
        CHECK (source_account_id <> target_account_id),

        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, target_account_id) REFERENCES financial_accounts(tenant_id, id)

    202611070002_inventory_counts.sql
    CREATE TABLE inventory_counts (
        id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
        status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open','approved','cancelled')),
        reference text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(btrim(reference)) BETWEEN 2 AND 120),
        revision bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (revision > 0),
        created_by text NOT NULL,
        approved_by text,
        created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
        approved_at timestamptz,
        cancelled_at timestamptz,
        UNIQUE (tenant_id,id),
        CHECK ((status='open' AND approved_at IS NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL)
            OR (status='approved' AND approved_at IS NOT NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL)
            OR (status='cancelled' AND cancelled_at IS NOT NULL AND approved_at IS NULL))
    );
    CREATE INDEX inventory_counts_tenant_created ON inventory_counts(tenant_id,created_at DESC,id DESC);
    
    CREATE TABLE inventory_count_lines (
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
        count_id uuid NOT NULL,
        product_id uuid NOT NULL,
        expected_quantity_micros bigint NOT NULL CHECK (expected_quantity_micros BETWEEN 0 AND 999999999999999999),
        counted_quantity_micros bigint CHECK (counted_quantity_micros BETWEEN 0 AND 999999999999999999),
        note text CHECK (note IS NULL OR char_length(note) <= 500),
        counted_at timestamptz,

    -- Custom commercial price lists never change catalog base prices or order snapshots.
    CREATE TABLE price_lists (
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
        id uuid NOT NULL,
        code text NOT NULL CHECK (code ~ '^[A-Z0-9._-]{1,40}$'),
        name text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
        status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('active','archived')),
        valid_from date,
        valid_until date,
        notes text CHECK (char_length(notes) <= 1000),
        revision bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (revision > 0),
        created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,id),
        UNIQUE (tenant_id,code),
        CHECK (valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from <= valid_until)
    );
    CREATE TABLE price_list_items (
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
        price_list_id uuid NOT NULL,
        product_id uuid NOT NULL,
        price_cents bigint NOT NULL CHECK (price_cents BETWEEN 0 AND 99999999999999),
        PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id,price_list_id,product_id),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id,price_list_id) REFERENCES price_lists(tenant_id,id),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id,product_id) REFERENCES products(tenant_id,id)
    );
    CREATE INDEX price_lists_name_idx ON price_lists(tenant_id,name,id);
    ALTER TABLE price_lists ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    ALTER TABLE price_lists FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    CREATE POLICY price_lists_isolation ON price_lists
        USING (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id',true),'')::uuid)
        WITH CHECK (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id',true),'')::uuid);
    ALTER TABLE price_list_items ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    ALTER TABLE price_list_items FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    CREATE POLICY price_list_items_isolation ON price_list_items
        USING (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id',true),'')::uuid)
        WITH CHECK (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id',true),'')::uuid);

    CREATE TABLE sales_proposal_email_deliveries (
        id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
        tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
        proposal_id uuid NOT NULL,
        version integer NOT NULL,
        proposal_revision bigint NOT NULL CHECK (proposal_revision > 0),
        result_revision bigint NOT NULL CHECK (result_revision > 0),
        subject_id text NOT NULL,
        command_key uuid NOT NULL,
        recipient text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(recipient) BETWEEN 3 AND 254),
        snapshot_html text NOT NULL,
        status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('uncertain', 'sent', 'failed')),
        created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        sent_at timestamptz,
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, subject_id, command_key),
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, proposal_id, version)
            REFERENCES sales_proposal_versions(tenant_id, proposal_id, version),
        CHECK (status <> 'sent' OR sent_at IS NOT NULL)
    );
    CREATE INDEX sales_proposal_email_history_idx
        ON sales_proposal_email_deliveries(tenant_id, proposal_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);
    ALTER TABLE sales_proposal_email_deliveries ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    ALTER TABLE sales_proposal_email_deliveries FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    CREATE POLICY sales_proposal_email_deliveries_isolation ON sales_proposal_email_deliveries
        USING (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid)

    # ERP Next em produção
    
    Imagens são construídas somente pelo GitHub CI, pelo workflow
    `production-release.yml`, com `source_ref` fixado no commit completo,
    depois das verificações de cada componente. PRs não reempacotam imagens.
    A implantação exige o resultado completo da execução aprovado.
    Os artefatos `erp-api-<sha>` e `erp-web-<sha>` contêm imagens Docker por SHA.
    O artefato `erp-fiscal-<sha>` contém o motor fiscal, após os testes próprios.
    
    O workflow de release tem timeout de 20 minutos para API e 15 para web.
    Falhas não autorizam build no servidor ou a retirada de testes.
    Os navegadores usam Chrome do runner.

    # Publicação da versão local do ERP
    
    Solicitação: publicar a aplicação atualmente editada neste computador.
    
    ## Restrições
    
    - Preservar a orientação do usuário de não usar Git durante a preparação.
    - Usar o fluxo documentado em deploy/README.md: imagens validadas no GitHub CI, sem compilação no servidor.
    - Preservar configurações privadas e os dados existentes; nenhuma emissão fiscal é parte do deploy.
    - Não habilitar emissão em produção nem automações fiscais como efeito colateral.
    
    ## Etapas
    
    1. Identificar destino, dependências e fluxo de release pelos arquivos locais.
    2. Validar formatação Rust, frontend e testes fiscais; registrar resultados e corrigir falhas dentro do escopo.
    3. Conferir compatibilidade das migrations e das dependências do MCP fiscal local com o ambiente de publicação.
    4. Preparar inventário e manifesto da versão local, sem segredos ou arquivos de desenvolvimento.
    5. Resolver a autorização para versionamento/publicação somente após apresentar a versão concreta e os resultados, pois a orientação anterior proíbe Git e o fluxo de release exige um commit remoto.
    6. Com autorização compatível, executar CI e deploy, validar domínio, saúde e revisão; usar rollback do dispatcher se necessário.
    
    ## Evidências iniciais
    
    - Destino documentado: https://erp.avilaops.com; dispatcher no host applications.
    - Componentes: API Rust, frontend Next.js e motor fiscal Node.js.
    - Dependência adicional das novas modalidades: MCP fiscal Python local com ferramentas e schemas ampliados; não presumir que o MCP remoto possui essas alterações.
    - O banco já recebeu as migrations fiscais 202611060003, 202611060004, 202611060005 e 202611080003 nesta sessão.
    - O fluxo exige fmt, clippy sem warnings, testes Rust, lint/build/UI web e testes do motor.
    
    ## Preparação local concluída
    
    - Formatação Rust e clippy workspace/all-targets com `-D warnings`: aprovados.
    - Interface: build de produção aprovado, 365 páginas; lint sem erros (8 avisos).
    - Motor fiscal: 146 testes aprovados.
    - MCP vendorizado com licença MIT, lockfile e dependências verificadas por hash: 60 testes aprovados.
    - Wheel verificado com módulos e XSDs; smoke HTTP local confirmou 47 ferramentas, schema e PDF sintético.
    - CI ampliado para construir/testar o quarto container, incluindo smoke sob restrições de runtime; essa verificação de container ainda será executada no runner.
    - Dispatcher preparado para quatro imagens, configuração MCP/CA e rollback com remoção de órfãos.
    - Rotas de aprovação/e-mail de propostas e módulo de testes agora registrados.
    - Suíte browser de release inclui os novos cenários NF-e. Testes completos Rust/UI e imagens devem passar no CI antes de publicar.
    
    ## Pré-condições de publicação
    
    1. Resolver com o usuário a autorização de Git, pois a orientação anterior o proíbe e o release exige commit remoto.
    2. Conferir/aplicar somente migrations incrementais ausentes e grants mínimos: há fontes locais posteriores à versão de warranty 202611060106 (logística, ledger, inventário, listas e e-mail de propostas). Evitar o workflow antigo de importação completa do legado.
    3. Instalar o dispatcher atualizado pelo acesso administrativo autorizado antes de disparar a execução que fará deploy automaticamente.
    4. Versionar a versão local revisada, preservar segredos/ambientes privados e executar CI antes de troca de serviços.
    
    Nenhum Git, push, publicação de imagens, atualização de dispatcher remoto ou troca de aplicação em produção foi executado nesta preparação.

    test("release dispatcher preserves private config and pins the restricted MCP runtime", () => {
      const dispatcher = readFileSync(new URL("../../../deploy/production-deploy.sh", import.meta.url), "utf8");
      const code = dispatcher.match(/python3 - "\$release\/compose.json" "\$source_sha" <<'PY'\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\nPY/)[1];
      const directory = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "erp-deploy-config-"));
      const file = join(directory, "compose.json");
      const sha = "a".repeat(40);
      const privateToken = "synthetic-private-fiscal-token-123456";
      try {
        writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify({ services: {
          api: { environment: { ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_TOKEN: privateToken } },
          web: { environment: { ERP_SESSION_SECRET: "synthetic-original-session-secret" } },
          "fiscal-engine": { healthcheck: {}, environment: {} },
        } }));
        const result = spawnSync(process.env.ERP_TEST_PYTHON || "python3", ["-c", code, file, sha], { encoding: "utf8" });
        assert.equal(result.status, 0, result.stderr || result.error?.message);
        const value = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, "utf8")).services;
        assert.equal(value.api.environment.DANFE_MCP_TOKEN, privateToken);
        assert.equal(value.api.environment.DANFE_MCP_TOOL_PREFIX, "bare");
        assert.equal(value.api.environment.DANFE_MCP_URL, "http://127.0.0.1:8093/mcp");
        assert.equal(value.web.environment.ERP_SESSION_SECRET, "synthetic-original-session-secret");
        assert.equal(value["fiscal-mcp"].image, "erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-" + sha);
        assert.equal(value["fiscal-mcp"].read_only, true);
        assert.equal(value["fiscal-mcp"].network_mode, "service:api");
        assert.match(dispatcher, /compose_overlay_args=\(--file "\$release\/fiscal-compose.yaml"\)/);
        assert.equal((dispatcher.match(/up --detach --no-build --remove-orphans --wait/g) || []).length, 2);
      } finally { rmSync(directory, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
    });

        Série, número e regime tributário podem ser informados no rascunho. A numeração continua validada atomicamente no servidor. As rotas de aprovação e e-mail de propostas passam a integrar o contrato e a cobertura HTTP.
        
        A publicação inclui o MCP fiscal Python com schemas fixados, dependências com hashes, teste de runtime em container e integração no Compose. O dispatcher preserva a configuração privada, publica quatro imagens e restaura o conjunto anterior de serviços em falhas.
