    name: CI
    
    on:
      pull_request:
      push:
        branches: [main]
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      npm_config_fetch_retries: 0
      npm_config_fetch_timeout: 10000
    
    jobs:
      context-source:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
            with:
              version: 11.11.0
          - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          - run: pnpm test:architecture
          - name: Validate MLOps release evidence gate (deterministic fixtures)
            run: node --test scripts/mlops/release-gate.test.mjs
          - name: Enforce documented architecture
            run: |
              mkdir -p artifacts
              pnpm --silent check:architecture > artifacts/architecture.json
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            if: always()
            with:
              name: erp-architecture-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/architecture.json
          - run: pnpm context:erp
    
      fiscal-engine:
        timeout-minutes: 3
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: npm test
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
    
      rust-build:
        timeout-minutes: 10
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.99.1
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: |
                /home/runner/.cargo/bin
                /home/runner/.cargo/.crates.toml
                /home/runner/.cargo/.crates2.json
                /home/runner/.cargo/registry
                /home/runner/.cargo/git
                ${{ github.workspace }}/target
              key: v0-rust-rust-Linux-x64-daeb8fa6-9ef83cd1
          - name: Compile complete Rust test suite
            run: |
              mkdir -p artifacts
              timeout 480s cargo test --workspace --locked --no-run --message-format=json > artifacts/rust-build.jsonl
              python3 -B scripts/contracts/package-test-binary.py
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-rust-tests-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/rust-tests/
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 1
    
      rust:
        needs: rust-build
        timeout-minutes: 7
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        services:
          postgres:
            image: postgres:18-alpine

    test("fiscal development override is limited to loopback and fiscal preparation routes", () => {

      for (const route of ["/products", "/fiscal/danfe", "/fiscal/incoming", "/fiscal/nfe-other"]) assert.equal(fiscalApiOrigin(route, original, "http://127.0.0.1:8081", "development"), original)

      for (const invalid of ["https://external.example", "http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:8081", "http://127.0.0.1:8081/path", "http://127.0.0.1:8081/?token=secret"]) assert.throws(() => fiscalApiOrigin("/fiscal/nfe", original, invalid, "development"))

    /** Local development can run the fiscal API without changing the other ERP services. */
    export function fiscalApiOrigin(resource: string, defaultOrigin: string, override: string | undefined, environment: string | undefined): string {
      if (environment !== "development" || !override || !/^\/fiscal\/(?:nfe(?:\/|$)|issued-nfes$|outgoing-imports(?:\/|$)|readiness$|config$|certificate$|order-preparations\/|ibpt(?:\/|$))/.test(resource)) return defaultOrigin
      const url = new URL(override)
      if (!["http:", "https:"].includes(url.protocol) || !["127.0.0.1", "[::1]"].includes(url.hostname) || url.username || url.password || url.pathname !== "/" || url.search || url.hash) throw new Error("Destino fiscal local inválido")
      return url.origin
    }

    ---
    name: dispatching-parallel-agents
    description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
    ---
    
    # Dispatching Parallel Agents
    
    ## Overview
    
    You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
    
    When you have multiple unrelated failures (different test files, different subsystems, different bugs), investigating them sequentially wastes time. Each investigation is independent and can happen in parallel.
    
    **Core principle:** Dispatch one agent per independent problem domain. Let them work concurrently.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    ```dot
    digraph when_to_use {
        "Multiple failures?" [shape=diamond];
        "Are they independent?" [shape=diamond];
        "Single agent investigates all" [shape=box];
        "One agent per problem domain" [shape=box];
        "Can they work in parallel?" [shape=diamond];
        "Sequential agents" [shape=box];
        "Parallel dispatch" [shape=box];
    
        "Multiple failures?" -> "Are they independent?" [label="yes"];
        "Are they independent?" -> "Single agent investigates all" [label="no - related"];
        "Are they independent?" -> "Can they work in parallel?" [label="yes"];
        "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Parallel dispatch" [label="yes"];
        "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Sequential agents" [label="no - shared state"];
    }
    ```
    
    **Use when:**
    - 3+ test files failing with different root causes
    - Multiple subsystems broken independently
    - Each problem can be understood without context from others
    - No shared state between investigations
    
    **Don't use when:**
    - Failures are related (fix one might fix others)
    - Need to understand full system state
    - Agents would interfere with each other
    
    ## The Pattern
    
    ### 1. Identify Independent Domains
    
    Group failures by what's broken:
    - File A tests: Tool approval flow
    - File B tests: Batch completion behavior
    - File C tests: Abort functionality
    
    Each domain is independent - fixing tool approval doesn't affect abort tests.
    
    ### 2. Create Focused Agent Tasks
    
    Each agent gets:
    - **Specific scope:** One test file or subsystem
    - **Clear goal:** Make these tests pass
    - **Constraints:** Don't change other code
    - **Expected output:** Summary of what you found and fixed
    
    ### 3. Dispatch in Parallel
    
    Issue all three subagent dispatches in the same response — they run in parallel:
    
    ```text
    # Verificação de rotas e fluxos do ERP-Next
    
    Ferramenta local de descoberta, ligação estática, probes HTTP e execução das
    suítes existentes. Os relatórios preservam a distinção entre código encontrado,
    requisição observada e operação testada. Não é um emissor, um backend novo ou
    um agente que altera o ERP automaticamente.
    
    ## Executar
    
    O catálogo [contracts.json](contracts.json) descreve as operações Rust
    existentes, suas precondições, estados, permissões, efeitos e recuperação, além
    das ações dinâmicas do BFF e das famílias de fluxos que ainda exigem definição.
    O verificador cruza essas fichas com os métodos/rotas/páginas descobertos. Rota
    sem ficha, método divergente ou contrato apontando para rota ausente produz erro.
    O relatório mostra a cobertura contratual separada do resultado de execução.
    `p0Ready=false` permanece enquanto houver decisões contratuais pendentes.
    
    Este catálogo documenta os tipos Rust existentes em vez de duplicar seus campos
    em outro schema. Os testes conferem que as referências de tipos e fontes existem.
    As oito dimensões de aceite não são resultados de testes. Veja o
    [escopo e a matriz de ações](../docs/CONTRATOS-ACOES-P0.md).
    
    ## Contexto por funcionalidade
    
    O campo `productFlows` do mesmo catálogo associa os grupos de ações a nomes e
    objetivos de produto, dependências e próximos passos. As definições de sequência
    incluem Usuários, Produtos, Compras, cancelamentos integrais, comissões,
    produção, emissão NF-e em homologação e entrada fiscal. Uma sequência declarada
    documenta os comandos e suas dependências; continua sem comprovar execução ou
    publicação. Os demais grupos mantêm `actions_mapped`.
    
    O catálogo cobre 222 operações API, incluindo `GET /openapi.json`, e 195 métodos
    de handlers BFF. Despachos `[action]` e `[...resource]` enumeram destinos
    explícitos, ligados a uma ficha API; um destino sem ficha ou que aponte para
    outra operação impede a verificação. A emissão é implementada somente para
    SP/homologação, com motor, certificado e validações; emissão em produção e
    aceite externo continuam pendentes. O monitor de produção mantém cursor e
    permissões próprios. Importar uma NF-e ou criar sua compra não recebe
    mercadoria nem cria conta a pagar.
    
    ```powershell
    pnpm context:erp
    pnpm context:erp --flow users
    pnpm context:erp --flow products
    pnpm context:erp --flow proposals
    pnpm context:erp --flow purchase_payment_chain
    pnpm context:erp:mcp
    ```
    
    O comando grava `context.json` e `context.md` em
    `artifacts/product-context/<contentSha256>/`. Inclui as dependências transitivas
    da funcionalidade selecionada, as ações canônicas, as permissões e os caminhos
    das fontes com seus hashes. Não copia os campos dos tipos Rust para outro contrato.
    Repetir entradas idênticas produz os mesmos bytes e reutiliza os arquivos;
    um arquivo existente com conteúdo diferente é preservado e causa erro.
    
    As definições e a saída têm JSON Schemas Draft 2020-12 em `schemas/`, validados
    com Ajv. Referências inexistentes, propriedade desconhecida, grupo com mais de
    um responsável e dependência circular impedem a geração. O comando confere
    as fontes e o estado Git antes e depois da captura; essas leituras observam
    intervalos e não bloqueiam o checkout como um snapshot atômico.
    
    `routes_mapped` significa que o catálogo relaciona páginas e BFF. Publicação e
    execução ficam como `not_observed`; o artefato não transforma commit, catálogo,
    HTTP 200 ou sugestão de modelo em evidência de uso. O hash permite conferir o

    import { forwardErp } from "@/server/bff/erp-proxy"
    
    export async function POST(request: Request, { params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string; action: string }> }) {
      const { id, action } = await params
      if (!["send", "accept", "reject", "cancel", "revise", "convert"].includes(action)) {
        return Response.json({ title: "Ação de proposta não encontrada" }, { status: 404 })
      }
      return forwardErp(request, `/proposals/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/${action}`)
    }

        #[test]
        fn contract_contains_only_implemented_resources_and_company_preconditions() {
            let doc = serde_json::to_value(ApiDoc::openapi()).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(doc["paths"].as_object().unwrap().len(), 222);
            assert!(doc["paths"]["/api/v1/financial-account-entries"]["get"].is_object());

    const occurredOn = "2026-10-31"
    const permissions = ["sales.orders.manage", "purchasing.orders.manage", "inventory.stock.manage", "finance.receivables.manage", "finance.payables.manage"]

    test("cancelamento integral repete o mesmo comando após resposta perdida e mostra histórico", async ({ page }) => {
      let cancelled = false
      const calls: Command[] = []
      const dialogs: string[] = []
      page.on("dialog", dialog => { dialogs.push(dialog.message()); void dialog.accept() })
      await page.route("**/api/erp/me", route => route.fulfill({ json: { tenant: { id: tenant }, permissions } }))
      await page.route(`**/api/erp/orders/${record}`, route => route.fulfill({ headers: { ETag: cancelled ? '"4"' : '"3"' }, json: { tenantId: tenant, canEdit: true, data: { id: record, customerName: "Cliente devolução", status: cancelled ? "cancelled" : "completed", revision: cancelled ? 4 : 3, amount: "20.00", dueDate: "2026-11-01" }, items: [] } }))
      await page.route(`**/api/erp/orders/${record}/cancel-completed`, route => {
        calls.push({ key: route.request().headers()["idempotency-key"], revision: route.request().headers()["if-match"], body: route.request().postDataJSON() })
        cancelled = true
        return calls.length === 1 ? route.abort("failed") : route.fulfill({ headers: { ETag: '"4"' }, json: { tenantId: tenant, data: { id: reversalId, revision: 4 } } })
      })
      await page.route(`**/api/erp/orders/${record}/cancellations`, route => route.fulfill({ json: { tenantId: tenant, data: [{ id: reversalId, reason, occurredOn, revision: 4, reconciliation: { commission: { status: "applied" }, production: { status: "applied", cancelledCount: 1, stockMovementIds: [record] } }, fiscalCancellation: { requested: true } }] } }))
      await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 })
      await page.goto(`/vendas/pedidos/${record}`)
      await page.getByLabel("Motivo do cancelamento integral", { exact: true }).fill(reason)
      await page.getByLabel("Data do cancelamento integral", { exact: true }).fill(occurredOn)
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Confirmar cancelamento integral", exact: true }).click()
      await expect(page.getByLabel("Motivo do cancelamento integral", { exact: true })).toBeDisabled()
      await expect(page.getByLabel("Data do cancelamento integral", { exact: true })).toHaveValue(occurredOn)
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Conferir cancelamento integral", exact: true }).click()
      await expect(page.getByText("Situação: Cancelado", { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
      expect(calls).toHaveLength(2)
      expect(calls[0]).toEqual(calls[1])
      expect(calls[0]).toMatchObject({ revision: '"3"', body: { reason, occurredOn } })
      expect(calls[0].key).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/)
      expect(dialogs).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(dialogs[0]).toContain("estoque")
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Consultar histórico de cancelamento", exact: true }).click()
      await expect(page.getByText(reason, { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.getByText("Comissões de recebimentos estornadas. Pagamentos anteriores preservados.", { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.getByText("Produção: 1 ordem(ns) cancelada(s) e 1 consumo(s) estornado(s).", { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.getByText("Solicitação de cancelamento fiscal registrada. Confira a situação da NF-e.", { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.getByLabel("Motivo do cancelamento integral", { exact: true })).toHaveCount(0)
      expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth)).toBe(true)
    })

    type WorkspaceAccess =

    export function isErpLoginConfigured(): boolean {
      try {
        const config = erpConfiguration()
        return Boolean(config.clientId?.trim() && config.clientSecret?.trim())
      } catch {
        return false
      }
    }
    
    export async function currentWorkspaceAccess(): Promise<WorkspaceAccess> {
      try {
        erpConfiguration()
      } catch {
        return { state: "configuration", session: null }
      }
      const identity = await currentIdentitySession()
      if (identity?.tenantId) return { state: "ready", session: { ...identity, tenantId: identity.tenantId } }
      if (identity) return { state: "company", session: null }
      return { state: isErpLoginConfigured() ? "login" : "configuration", session: null }
    }

    function currentArea(pathname: string) {
      const area = moduleLinks.find(([, href]) => href !== "/" && matches(pathname, href))?.[0]
      const named = desktopMenus.findIndex(menu => menu.label === area || menu.columns.some(group => group.title === area))
      if (named >= 0) return named
      return desktopMenus.flatMap((menu, index) => menu.columns.flatMap(group => group.items
        .filter(item => matches(pathname, item.href)).map(item => ({ index, length: item.href.length }))))
        .sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)[0]?.index ?? (area && area !== "Histórico importado" ? menus.length - 1 : undefined)
    }
    
    function currentPage(pathname: string) {
      return menus.flatMap((menu, index) => menu.columns.flatMap(group => group.items
        .filter(item => matches(pathname, item.href)).map(item => ({ index, label: item.label, length: item.href.length }))))
        .sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)[0]
    }
    
    function Options({ index, pathname, onNavigate }: { index: number; pathname: string; onNavigate: () => void }) {
      const active = menus[index].columns.flatMap(group => group.items).filter(item => matches(pathname, item.href))
        .sort((a, b) => b.href.length - a.href.length)[0]?.href
      return <div className="erp-module-groups">
        {menus[index].columns.map(group => <section key={group.title || group.items[0]?.href}>
          {group.title && <h3>{group.title}</h3>}
          <ul>{group.items.map(item => <li key={item.href}>
            <Link href={item.href} onNavigate={onNavigate} className="erp-option" aria-current={item.href === active ? "page" : undefined}>{item.label}</Link>
          </li>)}</ul>
        </section>)}
      </div>
    }

          <label className="grid gap-2 text-sm font-medium">Nome, tipo ou hash<Input value={query} onChange={event=>filter(()=>setQuery(event.target.value))} placeholder="Ex.: nota.xml ou application/pdf" /></label>

        </div></section>

    ---
    name: verification-before-completion
    description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
    ---
    
    # Verification Before Completion
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.
    
    **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
    ```
    
    If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.
    
    ## The Gate Function
    
    ```
    BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:
    
    1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
    2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
    3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
    4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
       - If NO: State actual status with evidence
       - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
    5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim
    
    Skip any step = lying, not verifying
    ```
    
    ## Common Failures
    
    | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
    |-------|----------|----------------|
    | Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
    | Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
    | Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
    | Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
    | Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
    | Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
    | Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |
    
    ## Red Flags - STOP
    
    - Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
    - Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
    - About to commit/push/PR without verification
    - Trusting agent success reports
    - Relying on partial verification
    - Thinking "just this once"
    - Tired and wanting work over
    - **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**
    
    ## Rationalization Prevention
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
    | "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
    | "Just this once" | No exceptions |
    | "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
    | "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
    | "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
    | "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
    | "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |
    
    ## Key Patterns
    
    **Tests:**
    ```
    ✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
    ❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
    ```
    
    **Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
    ```
    ✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
    ❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
    ```
    
    **Build:**
    ```
    ✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
    ❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
    ```
    
    **Requirements:**
    ```
    ✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
    ❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
    ```
    
    **Agent delegation:**
    ```
    ✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
    ❌ Trust agent report
    ```
    
    ## When To Apply
    
    **ALWAYS before:**
    - ANY variation of success/completion claims
    - ANY expression of satisfaction
    - ANY positive statement about work state
    - Committing, PR creation, task completion
    - Moving to next task
    - Delegating to agents
    
    **Rule applies to:**
    - Exact phrases
    - Paraphrases and synonyms
    - Implications of success
    - ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

    name: Production release
    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          source_ref:
            description: Exact source commit to validate and package
            required: true
            type: string
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    jobs:
      fiscal-mcp:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 15
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
            with:
              version: 0.12.24
          - run: uv sync --frozen --extra dev --python 3.12
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-mcp
          - run: node --test scripts/fiscal/test/deploy-config.test.mjs
          - run: uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest tests/test_fiscal_schema.py tests/test_simplified_danfe.py tests/test_nfe_assinatura.py
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-mcp
          - run: docker build -f apps/fiscal-mcp/Dockerfile -t erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} .
          - name: Exercise MCP in its restricted runtime container
            shell: bash
            run: |
              docker run --detach --name fiscal-mcp-smoke --network host --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=64m,mode=1777 --security-opt no-new-privileges:true --cap-drop ALL --memory 512m --pids-limit 128 -e XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/cache erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              trap 'docker rm -f fiscal-mcp-smoke >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
              cd apps/fiscal-mcp
              uv run --frozen --extra dev python scripts/smoke_runtime.py
          - run: docker save erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} | gzip > fiscal-mcp-image.tar.gz
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-fiscal-mcp-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: fiscal-mcp-image.tar.gz
              compression-level: 0
              retention-days: 7
      fiscal-engine:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: npm test
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: docker build -f apps/fiscal-engine/Dockerfile -t erp-next-fiscal:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} .
          - run: docker save erp-next-fiscal:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} | gzip > fiscal-image.tar.gz
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-fiscal-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: fiscal-image.tar.gz
              compression-level: 0
              retention-days: 7
      api:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 20
        services:
          postgres:
            image: postgres:18-alpine
            env:
              POSTGRES_DB: erp_next_test
              POSTGRES_USER: postgres
              POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ci_isolated_only
            ports: ['5432:5432']

      mlops-evidence:
        name: MLOps verified release evidence
        needs: [fiscal-engine, fiscal-mcp, api, web]
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        permissions:
          contents: read
          actions: read
        env:
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          MLOPS_ARTIFACTS_DIR: artifacts/mlops-input
        steps:
          - name: Checkout exact evaluated source
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - name: Download actual OpenAPI contract from API job
            uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-release-openapi-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/mlops-input/contracts
          - name: Download actual browser-validated template from web job
            uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-contract-model-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/mlops-input/validation
          - name: Validate source, job outcomes, contract and evidence digests
            run: node scripts/mlops/release-gate.mjs
          - name: Preserve signed-by-digest evidence
            uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-mlops-evidence-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
              path: artifacts/mlops-release/
              retention-days: 30
              if-no-files-found: error
    
      deploy:
        name: Deploy production
        needs: [fiscal-engine, fiscal-mcp, api, web, mlops-evidence]
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 15
        environment: production
        permissions:
          contents: read
          actions: read
        concurrency:
          group: erp-production-deploy
          cancel-in-progress: false
        env:
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-api-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: bundle
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-web-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: bundle
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-fiscal-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: bundle
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-fiscal-mcp-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: bundle
          - name: Send immutable release to applications
            env:
              DEPLOY_HOST: ${{ secrets.ERP_DEPLOY_HOST }}
              DEPLOY_USER: ${{ secrets.ERP_DEPLOY_USER }}
              DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.ERP_DEPLOY_SSH_KEY }}
              DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS: ${{ secrets.ERP_DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              [[ "$SOURCE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
              [[ "$DEPLOY_HOST" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*$ ]]
              [[ "$DEPLOY_USER" =~ ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$ ]]
              test -s bundle/api-image.tar.gz
              test -s bundle/web-image.tar.gz
              test -s bundle/fiscal-image.tar.gz
              test -s bundle/fiscal-mcp-image.tar.gz
              bundle_dir=$(mktemp -d)
              ssh_dir=$(mktemp -d)
              trap 'rm -rf "$bundle_dir" "$ssh_dir"' EXIT
              cp bundle/api-image.tar.gz bundle/web-image.tar.gz bundle/fiscal-image.tar.gz bundle/fiscal-mcp-image.tar.gz "$bundle_dir/"
              cp deploy/compose.yaml deploy/fiscal-compose.yaml "$bundle_dir/"
              chmod 700 "$ssh_dir"
              printf '%s\n' "$DEPLOY_KEY" > "$ssh_dir/key"
              printf '%s\n' "$DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS" > "$ssh_dir/known_hosts"
              chmod 600 "$ssh_dir/key" "$ssh_dir/known_hosts"
              tar -C "$bundle_dir" -czf - . | ssh -T \
                -i "$ssh_dir/key" -o BatchMode=yes -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
                -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile="$ssh_dir/known_hosts" \
                -o ConnectTimeout=20 -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
                "$DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST" "deploy erp-next $SOURCE_SHA"
    
    # Publicação da versão local do ERP
    
    Solicitação: publicar a aplicação atualmente editada neste computador.
    
    ## Restrições
    
    - Preservar a orientação do usuário de não usar Git durante a preparação.
    - Usar o fluxo documentado em deploy/README.md: imagens validadas no GitHub CI, sem compilação no servidor.
    - Preservar configurações privadas e os dados existentes; nenhuma emissão fiscal é parte do deploy.
    - Não habilitar emissão em produção nem automações fiscais como efeito colateral.
    
    ## Etapas
    
    1. Identificar destino, dependências e fluxo de release pelos arquivos locais.
    2. Validar formatação Rust, frontend e testes fiscais; registrar resultados e corrigir falhas dentro do escopo.
    3. Conferir compatibilidade das migrations e das dependências do MCP fiscal local com o ambiente de publicação.
    4. Preparar inventário e manifesto da versão local, sem segredos ou arquivos de desenvolvimento.
    5. Resolver a autorização para versionamento/publicação somente após apresentar a versão concreta e os resultados, pois a orientação anterior proíbe Git e o fluxo de release exige um commit remoto.
    6. Com autorização compatível, executar CI e deploy, validar domínio, saúde e revisão; usar rollback do dispatcher se necessário.
    
    ## Evidências iniciais
    
    - Destino documentado: https://erp.avilaops.com; dispatcher no host applications.
    - Componentes: API Rust, frontend Next.js e motor fiscal Node.js.
    - Dependência adicional das novas modalidades: MCP fiscal Python local com ferramentas e schemas ampliados; não presumir que o MCP remoto possui essas alterações.
    - O banco já recebeu as migrations fiscais 202611060003, 202611060004, 202611060005 e 202611080003 nesta sessão.
    - O fluxo exige fmt, clippy sem warnings, testes Rust, lint/build/UI web e testes do motor.
    
    ## Preparação local concluída
    
    - Formatação Rust e clippy workspace/all-targets com `-D warnings`: aprovados.
    - Interface: build de produção aprovado, 365 páginas; lint sem erros (8 avisos).
    - Motor fiscal: 146 testes aprovados.
    - MCP vendorizado com licença MIT, lockfile e dependências verificadas por hash: 60 testes aprovados.
    - Wheel verificado com módulos e XSDs; smoke HTTP local confirmou 47 ferramentas, schema e PDF sintético.
    - CI ampliado para construir/testar o quarto container, incluindo smoke sob restrições de runtime; essa verificação de container ainda será executada no runner.
    - Dispatcher preparado para quatro imagens, configuração MCP/CA e rollback com remoção de órfãos.
    - Rotas de aprovação/e-mail de propostas e módulo de testes agora registrados.
    - Suíte browser de release inclui os novos cenários NF-e. Testes completos Rust/UI e imagens devem passar no CI antes de publicar.
    
    ## Pré-condições de publicação
    
    1. Resolver com o usuário a autorização de Git, pois a orientação anterior o proíbe e o release exige commit remoto.
    2. Conferir/aplicar somente migrations incrementais ausentes e grants mínimos: há fontes locais posteriores à versão de warranty 202611060106 (logística, ledger, inventário, listas e e-mail de propostas). Evitar o workflow antigo de importação completa do legado.
    3. Instalar o dispatcher atualizado pelo acesso administrativo autorizado antes de disparar a execução que fará deploy automaticamente.
    4. Versionar a versão local revisada, preservar segredos/ambientes privados e executar CI antes de troca de serviços.
    
    Nenhum Git, push, publicação de imagens, atualização de dispatcher remoto ou troca de aplicação em produção foi executado nesta preparação.
    
    ## Publicação autorizada
    
    O usuário autorizou explicitamente a publicação após a pergunta sobre commit e push. A restrição anterior de Git foi substituída para este deploy.
    
    - Git remoto e base local conferidos: main bb51680, sem commits remotos novos; aplicação atual saudável nessa revisão.
    - Banco: 11 migrations incrementais pendentes aplicadas atomicamente; 160 produtos preservados. Três checksums foram normalizados apenas de CRLF para LF com verificação do hash anterior; fontes SQL agora têm checkout LF explícito.
    - Grants mínimos das tabelas novas aplicados; não houve reimportação do legado.
    - Teste do dispatcher preserva segredos sintéticos e valida a quarta imagem, isolamento e rollback. Sintaxe Bash e YAML verificadas.
    - Próximos passos: commit da versão local, backup/instalação do dispatcher revisado, push/CI completo e conferência da revisão publicada.

      # The generated JSON carries the public release marker in the web
      # environment; update it together with the immutable image references.
      sed -i "s|\"ERP_RELEASE_SHA\": \"[0-9a-f]*\"|\"ERP_RELEASE_SHA\": \"$source_sha\"|g" "$release/compose.json"
      previous_api=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' erp-next-api-1)
      previous_web=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' erp-next-web-1)
      previous_fiscal=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' erp-next-fiscal-engine-1)
      for pair in \
        "$previous_api|erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha" \
        "$previous_web|erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha" \
        "$previous_fiscal|erp-next-fiscal:sha-$source_sha"; do
        old=${pair%%|*}
        new=${pair#*|}
        escaped_old=$(printf '%s' "$old" | sed 's/[.[\*^$()+?{|\\]/\\&/g')
        sed -i "s|$escaped_old|$new|g" "$release/compose.json"
      done
      grep -q "erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'API image was not pinned'
      grep -q "erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'web image was not pinned'
      grep -q "erp-next-fiscal:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'fiscal image was not pinned'
      grep -q "erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-$source_sha" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'MCP image was not pinned'
      grep -q "\\\"ERP_RELEASE_SHA\\\": \\\"$source_sha\\\"" "$release/compose.json" || fail 'release SHA was not pinned'
      compose_file=compose.json
      compose_env_args=()
    else
      [[ -f "$previous_release/compose.yaml" && -f "$previous_release/api.env" && -f "$previous_release/web.env" && -f "$previous_release/.env" ]] || fail 'active release has an unknown layout'
      cp -p "$staging/compose.yaml" "$staging/fiscal-compose.yaml" "$release/"
      cp -p "$previous_release/api.env" "$previous_release/web.env" "$previous_release/.env" "$release/"
      chmod 600 "$release/api.env" "$release/web.env" "$release/.env"
      sed -i \
        -e "s|^ERP_API_IMAGE=.*|ERP_API_IMAGE=erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha|" \
        -e "s|^ERP_WEB_IMAGE=.*|ERP_WEB_IMAGE=erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha|" \
        -e "s|^ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_IMAGE=.*|ERP_FISCAL_ENGINE_IMAGE=erp-next-fiscal:sha-$source_sha|" \
        -e "s|^ERP_RELEASE_SHA=.*|ERP_RELEASE_SHA=$source_sha|" \
        "$release/.env"
      sed -i '/^ERP_FISCAL_MCP_IMAGE=/d' "$release/.env"
      printf '\nERP_FISCAL_MCP_IMAGE=erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-%s\n' "$source_sha" >> "$release/.env"
      grep -q "^ERP_API_IMAGE=erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'API image was not pinned'
      grep -q "^ERP_WEB_IMAGE=erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'web image was not pinned'
      grep -q "^ERP_RELEASE_SHA=$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'release SHA was not pinned'
      compose_file=compose.yaml
      compose_overlay_args=(--file "$release/fiscal-compose.yaml")
      compose_env_args=(--env-file "$release/.env")
    fi
    
    compose() {
      docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$1" \
        "${compose_env_args[@]}" --file "$1/$compose_file" "${compose_overlay_args[@]}" "${@:2}"
    }
    
    rollback() {
      local status=$?
      trap - EXIT
      printf '%s\n' 'ERP deploy failed; restoring previous release' >&2
      if [[ -f "$previous_release/compose.json" ]]; then
        docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$previous_release" \
          --file "$previous_release/compose.json" up --detach --no-build --remove-orphans --wait --wait-timeout 120 || true
      else
        docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$previous_release" \
          --env-file "$previous_release/.env" --file "$previous_release/compose.yaml" \
          --file "$previous_release/fiscal-compose.yaml" up --detach --no-build --remove-orphans --wait --wait-timeout 120 || true
      fi
      exit "$status"
    }
    
    trap rollback ERR
    compose "$release" config --quiet
    compose "$release" up --detach --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 120
    
    curl --fail --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
      http://127.0.0.1:3141/health/ready >/dev/null
    
    python3 - "$source_sha" <<'PY'
    import json
    import sys
    import urllib.request
    
    expected = sys.argv[1]
    with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:3140/api/health", timeout=10) as response:
        health = json.load(response)
    if health.get("commit") != expected or health.get("ok") is not True:
        raise SystemExit("ERP health does not match the requested release")
    for path in ("/entrar", "/erp-preview.webp"):
        with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:3140" + path, timeout=10) as response:
            if response.status != 200:
                raise SystemExit(f"ERP public path failed: {path}")
    print(json.dumps({"application": health.get("application"), "commit": health.get("commit")}))
    PY
    
    trap - EXIT
    printf 'ERP deploy completed: %s\n' "$source_sha"

    name: CI
    
    on:
      pull_request:
      push:
        branches: [main]
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      npm_config_fetch_retries: 0
      npm_config_fetch_timeout: 10000
    
    jobs:
      context-source:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
            with:
              version: 11.11.0
          - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          - run: pnpm test:architecture
          - name: Validate MLOps release evidence gate (deterministic fixtures)
            run: node --test scripts/mlops/release-gate.test.mjs
          - name: Enforce documented architecture
            run: |
              mkdir -p artifacts
              pnpm --silent check:architecture > artifacts/architecture.json
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            if: always()
            with:
              name: erp-architecture-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/architecture.json
          - run: pnpm context:erp
    
      fiscal-engine:
        timeout-minutes: 3
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
          - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: npm test
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
    
      rust-build:
        timeout-minutes: 10
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.99.1
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: |
                /home/runner/.cargo/bin
                /home/runner/.cargo/.crates.toml
                /home/runner/.cargo/.crates2.json
                /home/runner/.cargo/registry
                /home/runner/.cargo/git
                ${{ github.workspace }}/target
              key: v0-rust-rust-Linux-x64-daeb8fa6-9ef83cd1
          - name: Compile complete Rust test suite
            run: |
              mkdir -p artifacts
              timeout 480s cargo test --workspace --locked --no-run --message-format=json > artifacts/rust-build.jsonl
              python3 -B scripts/contracts/package-test-binary.py
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-rust-tests-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/rust-tests/
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 1
    
      rust:
        needs: rust-build
        timeout-minutes: 7
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        services:
          postgres:
            image: postgres:18-alpine
            env:
              POSTGRES_DB: erp_next_test
              POSTGRES_USER: postgres
              POSTGRES_PASSWORD: erp_next_ci_only
            ports:
              - 5432:5432
            options: >-
              --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres -d erp_next_test"
              --health-interval 2s
              --health-timeout 3s
              --health-retries 20
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:erp_next_ci_only@127.0.0.1:5432/erp_next_test
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-rust-tests-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/rust-tests/
          - name: Test Rust and export candidate contract
            run: timeout 300s python3 -B scripts/contracts/run-test-binaries.py
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            if: always()
            with:
              name: erp-openapi-candidate-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/contracts/
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 14
    
      rust-lint:
        timeout-minutes: 10
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.99.1
            with:
              components: clippy,rustfmt
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: |
                /home/runner/.cargo/bin
                /home/runner/.cargo/.crates.toml
                /home/runner/.cargo/.crates2.json
                /home/runner/.cargo/registry
                /home/runner/.cargo/git
                ${{ github.workspace }}/target
              key: v0-rust-rust-Linux-x64-daeb8fa6-9ef83cd1
          - name: Check Rust formatting and preserve a repair patch
            run: |
              if ! cargo fmt --all --check; then
                mkdir -p artifacts
                cargo fmt --all
                git diff --binary > artifacts/rustfmt.patch
                exit 1
              fi
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            if: failure()
            with:
              name: erp-rustfmt-${{ github.sha }}
              path: artifacts/rustfmt.patch

      await page.addInitScript(() => localStorage.setItem("erp-theme", "system"))
      for (const theme of ["light", "dark"]) {
        await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: theme as "light" | "dark", reducedMotion: "reduce" })
        for (const route of ["/preferencias/empresa", "/preferencias/certificado-digital", "/fiscal/notas-saida", "/fiscal/notas-saida/nova"]) {
          await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 })
          await page.goto(route)
          await expect(page.locator("h1")).toBeVisible()
          const unavailable = route === "/fiscal/notas-saida" ? page.getByRole("region", { name: "Notas fiscais de saída", exact: true }).getByRole("alert") : page.locator('main [role="alert"], main [role="status"]').filter({ hasText: "Operação indisponível" })
          await expect(unavailable).toContainText("Operação indisponível")
          await expect.poll(() => page.locator("html").evaluate(element => element.classList.contains("dark"))).toBe(theme === "dark")
          // Theme changes can precede the inherited color transition on settings links.
          if (route === "/preferencias/empresa") await expect.poll(() => page.locator('[aria-labelledby^="company-settings-"] strong').evaluateAll(elements => {
            const foreground = getComputedStyle(document.querySelector("main")!).color
            return elements.length > 0 && elements.every(element => getComputedStyle(element).color === foreground)
          })).toBe(true)
          if (route === "/fiscal/notas-saida") await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Atualizar lista", exact: true })).toBeEnabled()
          await page.evaluate(() => Promise.all(document.getAnimations().filter(animation => animation.effect?.getTiming().iterations !== Infinity).map(animation => animation.finished.catch(() => {}))))
          await page.addScriptTag({ content: axe.source })
          const result = await page.evaluate(async () => {
            const scanner = (window as unknown as { axe: typeof axe }).axe
            return scanner.run(document, { runOnly: { type: "tag", values: ["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21aa"] } })
          })
          await info.attach(route.replaceAll("/", "-") + "-" + theme, { body: JSON.stringify({ violations: result.violations, incomplete: result.incomplete }), contentType: "application/json" })
          await page.screenshot({ path: info.outputPath(route.replaceAll("/", "-") + "-" + theme + ".png"), fullPage: true })
          expect(result.violations.map(item => ({ id: item.id, nodes: item.nodes.map(node => node.target) }))).toEqual([])
          expect(result.incomplete.filter(item => item.id === "color-contrast").flatMap(item => item.nodes).filter(node => node.any.some(check => check.data?.messageKey === "equalRatio")), "Texto com contraste 1:1 exige correção, mesmo quando o scanner o classifica como inconclusivo").toEqual([])
        }
      }
    })

    "use client";
    
    import { useEffect, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
    
    type Theme = "light" | "dark" | "system" | "avila";
    
    function getTheme(): Theme {
      const stored = window.localStorage.getItem("erp-theme");
      return stored === "dark" || stored === "system" || stored === "avila" ? stored : "light";
    }
    
    function subscribe(listener: () => void) {
      window.addEventListener("storage", listener);
      window.addEventListener("erp-theme-change", listener);
      return () => {
        window.removeEventListener("storage", listener);
        window.removeEventListener("erp-theme-change", listener);
      };
    }
    
    function setTheme(theme: Theme) {
      window.localStorage.setItem("erp-theme", theme);
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event("erp-theme-change"));
    }
    
    function getServerTheme(): Theme {
      return "light";
    }
    
    export function useTheme() {
      const theme = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getTheme, getServerTheme);
      return [theme, setTheme] as const;
    }
    
    export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
      const [theme] = useTheme();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const media = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
        const update = () => {
          document.documentElement.classList.toggle(
            "dark",
            theme === "dark" || (theme === "system" && media.matches),
          );
          document.documentElement.classList.toggle("avila-theme", theme === "avila");
        };
        update();
        media.addEventListener("change", update);
        return () => media.removeEventListener("change", update);
      }, [theme]);
    
      return children;
    }

      | { state: "ready"; session: ErpSession }
      | { state: "configuration" | "login" | "company"; session: null }
    
    export function isErpLoginConfigured(): boolean {
      try {
        const config = erpConfiguration()
        return Boolean(config.clientId?.trim() && config.clientSecret?.trim())
      } catch {
        return false
      }
    }
    
    export async function currentWorkspaceAccess(): Promise<WorkspaceAccess> {
      // Configuration can be supplied at server startup, after the build completes.
      await connection()
      try {
        erpConfiguration()
      } catch {
        return { state: "configuration", session: null }
      }
      const identity = await currentIdentitySession()
      if (identity?.tenantId) return { state: "ready", session: { ...identity, tenantId: identity.tenantId } }
      if (identity) return { state: "company", session: null }
      return { state: isErpLoginConfigured() ? "login" : "configuration", session: null }
    }
    
    export function WorkspaceAccessNotice({ state }: { state: WorkspaceAccess["state"] }) {
      return <section className="form-section space-y-3">
        <p role="status">{state === "configuration"
          ? "O login do ERP ainda não foi configurado neste ambiente. A configuração é necessária para acessar e salvar os cadastros."
          : state === "company"
            ? "Você já entrou. Selecione uma empresa ou cadastre a sua para continuar."
            : "Entre com sua conta Avila Ops para acessar os cadastros da sua empresa."}</p>
        {state === "login" && <AccessLink />}
        {state === "company" && <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
          <AccessLink page="/empresas">Selecionar empresa</AccessLink>
          <Link className="font-medium text-primary underline" href="/cadastro/empresa">Cadastrar empresa</Link>
        </div>}
      </section>
    }

    name: brainstorming
    description: "You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation)."
    ---
    
    # Brainstorming
    
    You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
    partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
    skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
    anything gets built.
    
    People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
    help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
    hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.
    
    ## First: What Do You Actually Know?
    
    Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
    why?
    
    - **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
      blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
    - **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.
    
    Before you start implementing, you must, in order:
    
    1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
       human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
    2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
    3. Get their approval of that doc.
    4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.
    
    Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
    feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
    the questions.
    
    ## Look Before You Ask
    
    In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
    a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
    first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
    connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
    parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
    project or their context already answers.
    
    ## Your First Message
    
    Move the work forward, with one of these:
    
    - **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
      request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
      request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
      shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
      Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
      and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
      have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
      has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
      so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
      want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
      corrections, then one question about what they want: the thing their
      request leaves open whose answer would most change what gets built.
      Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
    - **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
      biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
      what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
      my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
      I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
      different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"
    
    How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
    brainstorming:
    
    - **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
      design discussion): end with your question. They want this
      conversation.
    - **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. After your
      question, add a light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
      "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
      it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
      (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
      asked through the normal workflow.
    
    That's the whole message.
    
    ## The Conversation
    
    Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
    example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
    above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
    process jargon. You never need to quote this skill to your human
    partner.
    
    Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
    report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
    the rest.
    
    **Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
    intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
    stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
    something concrete.
    
    **How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
    materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
    libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
    of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
    they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
    want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
    said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
    uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
    something they agreed to.
    
    **Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
    out as questions:
    
    - what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
    - why now, and what success looks like to them
    - goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
      if it technically works)
    - prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
    - current state: what exists now, what they've tried
    - the details they care about
    
    **Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
    you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
    question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
    them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
    ("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
    Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
    already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
    change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
    beats a question.
    
    **Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
    would help, offer to go look: deeper into their codebase or project,
    their own files and data, or the web. Say what you'd look for. They
    decide whether you go.
    
    **Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
    before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
    of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
    ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
    existing work rules out. Present the two or three that remain, grounding
    each in what the project actually does and saying what it trades off.
    Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want to go. When
    there's genuinely one sensible way, say so and explain why the others
    don't fit. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
    describing first.
    
    **Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
    would help more than reading:
    
    - something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
    - a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
    - a flow or a sequence of steps
    - options that would look different from each other
    - a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map
    
    Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
    options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.
    
    **Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
    fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
    they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
    When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
    or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
    and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
    conversation.
    
    ## Play It Back
    
    Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
    describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
    behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
    questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
    the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.
    
    Only what they said goes in as theirs. Anything you filled in goes in
    as your proposal, with your reason. End each chunk by asking what's wrong
    or missing.
    
    Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
    look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
    they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
    (its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
    they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.
    
    ## Size the Work
    
    Once you understand what they want and they've picked an approach, say
    how big the work is in plain words. They can override it.
    
    | Size | The design doc |
    |------|----------------|
    | A small change | a short one: what you already covered together, written down |
    | A project | the full written design (below) |
    
    Short or full, the design doc has an **Approaches** part: the two or
    three ways you considered building it, what each trades off, which one
    they picked, and why. They pick in the conversation, before you write
    the doc.
    
    If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.
    
    If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
    order, and brainstorm them one at a time.
    
    ## The Written Design
    
    Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan
    from without going back to your human partner. Cover:
    
    - intent and the why
    - goals, non-goals, anti-goals
    - constraints
    - approaches (above)
    - the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
    - what's left to the builder
    
    For a small change, the short design covers the same points in a line
    or two each and goes straight to your human partner, without the
    builder check.
    
    **Where it goes:** in a software repo,
    `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
    Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.
    
    **Builder check** (for a project): dispatch a fresh subagent with
    `builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
    partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
    may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
    until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:
    
    - **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
      in the document.
    - **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
      built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
    - **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
      what gets built.
    
    Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
    document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
    calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
    round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
    document as that builder yourself.
    
    <HARD-GATE>
    Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the design doc:
    the short one for a small change, the full one for a project.
    Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
    dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
    Reading and exploring are fine.
    
    Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
    and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
    stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
    that comes back through this gate.
    
    After the design doc is approved, the next step is the plan: invoke
    superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
    </HARD-GATE>
    
    ## Red Flags
    
    | Thought | Reality |
    |---------|---------|
    | "I'll offer a menu of what they might want" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
    | "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
    | "I've answered their questions, so I'll write the doc" | Lay out the approaches first, in a message of their own. |
    | "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
    | "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A design doc you haven't written isn't approved. |
    | "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |
    
    ## Visual Companion
    
    A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
    tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
    browser.
    
    **Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
    above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
    else in it:
    
    > "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"
    
    If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.
    
    **Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
    Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
    Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
    question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.
    
    If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
    starting the server.

    import type { CompanyData } from "./company-types"
    
    export const companySections = {
      identificacao: { heading: "identificacao-title", label: "Dados cadastrais" },
      endereco: { heading: "endereco-title", label: "Endereço" },
      contato: { heading: "contato-title", label: "Contatos" },
      fiscal: { heading: "fiscal-title", label: "Dados fiscais e atividade" },
      inscricoes: { heading: "substitutos-title", label: "Inscrições substitutas" },
    } as const
    
    export type CompanySection = keyof typeof companySections
    
    export function companySectionStatus(data: CompanyData, section: CompanySection) {
      const count = (fields: (keyof CompanyData)[]) => fields.filter(field => typeof data[field] === "string" && data[field].trim()).length
      switch (section) {
        case "identificacao": return `${count(["legalName", "taxId"])} de 2 dados básicos informados`
        case "endereco": return `${count(["postalCode", "state", "city", "street", "number", "district"])} de 6 campos de endereço informados`
        case "contato": return `${count(["contactName", "phone", "mobile", "email", "billingEmail", "website"])} campos de contato informados`
        case "fiscal": return data.taxRegime.trim() ? "Regime tributário informado" : "Regime tributário não informado"
        case "inscricoes": return data.substituteRegistrations.length ? `${data.substituteRegistrations.length} inscrições substitutas informadas` : "Sem inscrições substitutas informadas"
      }
    }

    import { DataTable } from "@/components/workspace/data-table"
    import type { Schema } from "@/lib/api/types"

    export type ProposalIssuer = { legalName: string; tradeName?: string | null; taxId?: string | null; email?: string | null; phone?: string | null }
    const labels: Record<string, string> = { draft: "Rascunho", sent: "Enviada", accepted: "Aceita", rejected: "Rejeitada", cancelled: "Cancelada", expired: "Expirada", superseded: "Substituída" }
    function date(value: string) {
      const match = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})/.exec(value)
      return match ? `${match[3]}/${match[2]}/${match[1]}` : value
    }
    
    export function ProposalDocument({ snapshot, issuer, issuerName }: { snapshot: Schema<"ProposalSnapshot">; issuer?: ProposalIssuer; issuerName?: string }) {
      const { data, items } = snapshot
      const name = issuer?.legalName || issuerName
      const status = data.expired ? "expired" : data.status
      return <article data-proposal-document className="proposal-document" aria-label={`Proposta comercial ${data.number}`}>
        <header className="proposal-document-header">
          <div className="proposal-issuer">
            {name && <p className="proposal-issuer-name">{name}</p>}
            {issuer?.tradeName && issuer.tradeName !== name && <p>{issuer.tradeName}</p>}
            {issuer?.taxId && <p>CPF/CNPJ: {issuer.taxId}</p>}
            {issuer?.email && <p>{issuer.email}</p>}{issuer?.phone && <p>{issuer.phone}</p>}
          </div>
          <div className="proposal-document-title"><h2>Proposta comercial</h2><p className="proposal-number">Nº {data.number}</p><p>Versão {data.version} · {labels[status] || status}</p></div>
        </header>
        <div className="proposal-parties">
          <section><h3>Cliente</h3><p className="proposal-customer-name">{data.customerName}</p>{data.customerTaxId && <p className="proposal-aux">CPF/CNPJ: {data.customerTaxId}</p>}</section>
          <dl className="proposal-dates">{data.createdAt && <div><dt>Emissão</dt><dd>{date(data.createdAt)}</dd></div>}<div><dt>Validade</dt><dd>{date(data.validUntil)}</dd></div></dl>
        </div>
        <section className="proposal-items" aria-label="Itens da proposta"><DataTable className="proposal-items-table">
          <caption className="sr-only">Itens da proposta</caption><colgroup><col className="proposal-product-column" /><col /><col /><col /></colgroup>
          <thead><tr><th scope="col">Produto</th><th scope="col">Quantidade</th><th scope="col">Unitário</th><th scope="col">Total</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>{items.map(item => <tr key={item.productId}>
            <td><p className="proposal-item-name">{item.name}</p><p className="proposal-aux">{item.sku}</p>{(item.structureColor || item.plateHolderColor || item.plateHolderType || item.upholsteryColor) && <p className="proposal-aux">{[item.structureColor && `Estrutura: ${item.structureColor}`, item.plateHolderColor && `Anilheiros: ${item.plateHolderColor}`, item.plateHolderType && `Tipo de anilheiro: ${item.plateHolderType}`, item.upholsteryColor && `Estofado: ${item.upholsteryColor}`].filter(Boolean).join(" · ")}</p>}</td>
            <td>{commercialQuantity(item.quantity)} {item.unit}</td><td>{commercialMoney(item.unitPrice)}</td><td>{commercialMoney(item.amount)}</td>
          </tr>)}</tbody>
        </DataTable></section>
        <div className="proposal-total"><p>Total: {commercialMoney(data.amount)}</p></div>
        <div className="proposal-conditions">
          {data.paymentTerms && <section><h3>Pagamento</h3><p>{data.paymentTerms}</p></section>}
          {data.deliveryTerms && <section><h3>Entrega</h3><p>{data.deliveryTerms}</p></section>}
          {data.notes && <section className="proposal-notes"><h3>Observações</h3><p>{data.notes}</p></section>}
        </div>
        {!data.isCurrent && <p className="proposal-history">Versão histórica · versão {data.version}</p>}
      </article>
    }

    "use client"
    
    import { erpFetch } from "@/lib/api/client"
    
    import { AccessLink } from "@/components/feedback/session-recovery"
    
    import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react"
    import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
    import { LogoutButton } from "@/components/shell/logout-button"
    import { CompanyDataForm } from "./company-data-form"
    import { CompanyPartnerForm } from "./company-partner-form"
    import type { CompanyData, CompanyProblem, CompanySnapshot } from "./company-types"
    
    export function CompanyEditor({ partner = false }: { partner?: boolean }) {
      const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState<CompanySnapshot | null>(null)
      const [etag, setEtag] = useState("")
      const [status, setStatus] = useState("loading")
      const [problem, setProblem] = useState<CompanyProblem | null>(null)
      const [conflict, setConflict] = useState(false)
    
      const receive = useCallback(({ response, result }: { response: Response; result: CompanySnapshot & CompanyProblem }) => {
        if (!response.ok) { setProblem(result); setStatus(response.status === 401 ? "unauthorized" : "error"); return }
        if (!response.headers.get("etag")) throw new Error("missing revision")
        setSnapshot(result)
        setEtag(response.headers.get("etag")!)
        setConflict(false)
        setStatus("ready")
      }, [])
    
      const failed = useCallback(() => { setProblem({ title: "Não foi possível carregar a empresa" }); setStatus("error") }, [])
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const controller = new AbortController()
        erpFetch("/api/erp/company", { cache: "no-store", signal: controller.signal })
          .then(async (response) => ({ response, result: await response.json() }))
          .then((result) => { if (!controller.signal.aborted) receive(result) })
          .catch(() => { if (!controller.signal.aborted) failed() })
        return () => controller.abort()
      }, [receive, failed])
    
      function reload() {
        setSnapshot(null)
        setProblem(null)
        setStatus("loading")
        erpFetch("/api/erp/company", { cache: "no-store" })
          .then(async (response) => ({ response, result: await response.json() }))
          .then(receive).catch(failed)
      }
    
      async function save(data: CompanyData) {
        if (!snapshot || conflict) return false
        setStatus("saving")
        setProblem(null)
        try {
          const response = await erpFetch("/api/erp/company", { method: "PUT", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "If-Match": etag, "X-Tenant-Id": snapshot.tenantId }, body: JSON.stringify(data) })
          const result = await response.json()
          if (!response.ok) {
            setProblem(result)
            setConflict(response.status === 412 || response.status === 409)
            setStatus("ready")
            return false
          }
          const nextEtag = response.headers.get("etag")
          if (!nextEtag || result.tenantId !== snapshot.tenantId) {
            setProblem({ title: "Gravação recebida sem confirmação da empresa ou revisão. Sua edição foi preservada; recarregue para conferir." })
            setConflict(true)
            setStatus("ready")
            return false
          }
          setSnapshot(result)
          setEtag(nextEtag)
          setStatus("saved")
          return true
        } catch {
          setProblem({ title: "Não foi possível confirmar a gravação. Sua edição foi preservada; recarregue para conferir a revisão antes de tentar novamente" })
          setConflict(true)
          setStatus("ready")
          return false
        }
      }
    
      if (!snapshot) return <section className="form-section space-y-4" aria-live="polite">
        {status === "loading" ? <p role="status">Carregando dados da empresa…</p> : <>
          <p role="alert">{problem?.title || "Empresa indisponível"}</p>
          {status === "unauthorized" ? <AccessLink className="font-medium text-primary underline" >Entrar com Avila Ops</AccessLink> : <Button onClick={reload}>Tentar novamente</Button>}
        </>}
      </section>
    
      return <div className="space-y-5">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3">
          <p className="break-words text-sm text-muted-foreground">Empresa: {snapshot.data.tradeName || snapshot.data.legalName}</p>
          <LogoutButton label="Sair desta sessão" className="inline-flex min-h-11 items-center gap-1.5 rounded-xl border border-border px-4 text-sm disabled:opacity-60" />
        </div>
        {!snapshot.canEdit && <p role="status">Você tem acesso de consulta. Solicite permissão para alterar o cadastro.</p>}
        {status === "saved" && <p role="status" className="rounded-xl border border-primary/30 p-4">Cadastro salvo no servidor.</p>}
        {problem && <div role="alert" className="space-y-2 rounded-xl border border-destructive p-4">
          <p>{problem.title || "Não foi possível salvar"}</p>
          {problem.errors?.length ? <ul>{problem.errors.map((error, index) => <li key={`${error.field}-${index}`}>{error.field}: {error.message}</li>)}</ul> : null}
          {conflict && <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => { if (window.confirm("Recarregar os dados do servidor e descartar sua edição atual?")) reload() }}>Recarregar e descartar edição</Button>}
        </div>}
        {partner ? <CompanyPartnerForm key={`${snapshot.tenantId}-${snapshot.revision}`} initial={snapshot.data} canEdit={snapshot.canEdit} saving={status === "saving"} conflict={conflict} onSave={save} /> : <CompanyDataForm key={`${snapshot.tenantId}-${snapshot.revision}`} tenantId={snapshot.tenantId} initial={snapshot.data} canEdit={snapshot.canEdit} saving={status === "saving"} conflict={conflict} onSave={save} />}
      </div>
    }

    export function companySectionStatus(data: CompanyData, section: CompanySection) {
      const count = (fields: (keyof CompanyData)[]) => fields.filter(field => typeof data[field] === "string" && data[field].trim()).length
      switch (section) {
        case "identificacao": return `${count(["legalName", "taxId"])} de 2 dados básicos informados`
        case "endereco": return `${count(["postalCode", "state", "city", "street", "number", "district"])} de 6 campos de endereço informados`
        case "contato": return `${count(["contactName", "phone", "mobile", "email", "billingEmail", "website"])} campos de contato informados`
        case "fiscal": return data.taxRegime.trim() ? "Regime tributário informado" : "Regime tributário não informado"
        case "inscricoes": return data.substituteRegistrations.length ? `${data.substituteRegistrations.length} inscrições substitutas informadas` : "Sem inscrições substitutas informadas"
      }
    }

    export type JsonBody<Path extends ApiPath, Method extends keyof paths[Path]> =
      Operation<Path, Method> extends { requestBody?: { content: { "application/json": infer Body } } } ? Body : never
    export type JsonReply<Path extends ApiPath, Method extends keyof paths[Path], Status extends number = 200> =
      Operation<Path, Method> extends { responses: infer Replies }
