    name: brainstorming
    description: "You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation)."
    ---
    
    # Brainstorming
    
    You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
    partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
    skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
    anything gets built.
    
    People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
    help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
    hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.
    
    ## First: What Do You Actually Know?
    
    Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
    why?
    
    - **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
      blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
    - **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.
    
    Before you start implementing, you must, in order:
    
    1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
       human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
    2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
    3. Get their approval of that doc.
    4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.
    
    Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
    feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
    the questions.
    
    ## Look Before You Ask
    
    In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
    a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
    first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
    connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
    parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
    project or their context already answers.
    
    ## Your First Message
    
    Move the work forward, with one of these:
    
    - **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
      request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
      request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
      shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
      Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
      and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
      have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
      has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
      so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
      want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
      corrections, then one question about what they want: the thing their
      request leaves open whose answer would most change what gets built.
      Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
    - **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
      biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
      what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
      my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
      I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
      different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"
    
    How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
    brainstorming:
    
    - **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
      design discussion): end with your question. They want this
      conversation.
    - **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. After your
      question, add a light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
      "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
      it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
      (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
      asked through the normal workflow.
    
    That's the whole message.
    
    ## The Conversation
    
    Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
    example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
    above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
    process jargon. You never need to quote this skill to your human
    partner.
    
    Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
    report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
    the rest.
    
    **Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
    intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
    stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
    something concrete.
    
    **How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
    materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
    libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
    of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
    they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
    want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
    said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
    uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
    something they agreed to.
    
    **Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
    out as questions:
    
    - what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
    - why now, and what success looks like to them
    - goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
      if it technically works)
    - prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
    - current state: what exists now, what they've tried
    - the details they care about
    
    **Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
    you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
    question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
    them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
    ("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
    Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
    already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
    change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
    beats a question.
    
    **Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
    would help, offer to go look: deeper into their codebase or project,
    their own files and data, or the web. Say what you'd look for. They
    decide whether you go.
    
    **Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
    before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
    of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
    ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
    existing work rules out. Present the two or three that remain, grounding
    each in what the project actually does and saying what it trades off.
    Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want to go. When
    there's genuinely one sensible way, say so and explain why the others
    don't fit. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
    describing first.
    
    **Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
    would help more than reading:
    
    - something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
    - a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
    - a flow or a sequence of steps
    - options that would look different from each other
    - a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map
    
    Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
    options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.
    
    **Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
    fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
    they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
    When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
    or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
    and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
    conversation.
    
    ## Play It Back
    
    Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
    describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
    behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
    questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
    the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.
    
    Only what they said goes in as theirs. Anything you filled in goes in
    as your proposal, with your reason. End each chunk by asking what's wrong
    or missing.
    
    Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
    look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
    they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
    (its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
    they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.
    
    ## Size the Work
    
    Once you understand what they want and they've picked an approach, say
    how big the work is in plain words. They can override it.
    
    | Size | The design doc |
    |------|----------------|
    | A small change | a short one: what you already covered together, written down |
    | A project | the full written design (below) |
    
    Short or full, the design doc has an **Approaches** part: the two or
    three ways you considered building it, what each trades off, which one
    they picked, and why. They pick in the conversation, before you write
    the doc.
    
    If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.
    
    If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
    order, and brainstorm them one at a time.
    
    ## The Written Design
    
    Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan
    ---
    name: writing-plans
    description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
    ---
    
    # Writing Plans
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.
    
    **Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."
    
    **Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.
    
    **Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
    - (User preferences for plan location override this default)
    
    ## Scope Check
    
    If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.
    
    ## File Structure
    
    Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.
    
    - Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
    - You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
    - Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.
    
    This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.
    
    ## Task Right-Sizing
    
    A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
    fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
    configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
    deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
    reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
    independently testable deliverable.
    
    ## Step Granularity
    
    **Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
    - "Write the failing test" - step
    - "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
    - "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
    - "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
    - "Commit" - step
    
    ## Plan Document Header
    
    **Every plan MUST start with this header:**
    
    ```markdown
    # [Feature Name] Implementation Plan
    
    > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
    
    **Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]
    
    **Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]
    
    **Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]
    
    **Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
    argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]
    
    ## Global Constraints
    
    [The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
    naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
    values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
    include this section.]
    
    ## Review Focus
    
    [The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
    tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
    — one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
    reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
    document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
    meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
    break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
    you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
    owns the code, in that task's own step style.]
    
    ---
    ```
    
    ## Task Structure
    
    ````markdown
    ### Task N: [Component Name]
    
    **Files:**
    - Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
    - Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
    - Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`
    
    **Interfaces:**
    - Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
    - Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
      and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
      block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]
    
    - [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**
    
    ```python
    def test_specific_behavior():
        result = function(input)
        assert result == expected
    ```
    
    - [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**
    
    Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
    Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"
    
    - [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**
    
    One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
    (which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
    algorithm they do not determine.
    
    - [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**
    
    Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
    Expected: PASS
    
    - [ ] **Step 5: Commit**
    
    ```bash
    git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
    git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
    ```
    ````
    
    ## What a Step Contains
    
    A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
    from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
    of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:
    
    - **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
      spec's exact values in them.
    - **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
      file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
      writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
      tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
    - **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
      passed.
    - **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
      to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.
    
    A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
    longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
    decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
    "write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
    opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.
    
    ## Self-Review
    
    After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.
    
    **1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.
    
    **2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.
    
    **3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.
    
    **4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.
    
    **5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.
    
    If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

    # Simulador comercial por versão publicada
    
    A página `/vendas/simulador` consulta as linhas Importada e Nacional e permite
    selecionar qualquer versão publicada. Os preços, custos e parâmetros vêm da
    mesma versão imutável. Alterações posteriores de cadastro não recalculam a venda.
    
    ## Condições e resultado
    
    O usuário seleciona equipamento, quantidade inteira, UF e condição de
    contribuinte. Pode informar desconto percentual, desconto em reais sobre o
    valor sem IPI, ou total desejado com IPI, além do frete pago pela empresa.
    A condição de contribuinte exige escolha explícita; nenhuma alíquota é inventada.
    
    O servidor calcula preço por unidade, total sem IPI, IPI, total da venda,
    entrada mínima da política e situação da margem. Quantidades vão de 1 a
    1.000.000, com limites monetários explícitos e rejeição de valores inválidos.
    O preço sem IPI é arredondado por unidade; o preço com IPI e o total mantêm
    a igualdade entre quantidade, unitário e total. O unitário com IPI usa o mesmo
    arredondamento para cima da publicação, preservando o preço sem desconto.
    Um total desejado nunca é
    ultrapassado pelo arredondamento e pode resultar em diferença de centavos.
    
    A gestão recebe também composição de custos, resultado antes e depois do IR,
    limites de desconto na meta e sem prejuízo, preço mínimo na meta e entrada
    necessária. A fórmula do fornecedor é custo de compra/assessoria com segurança,
    sem descontar crédito tributário. A entrada necessária cobre esse pagamento,
    o lucro líquido desejado e a comissão sobre a entrada sem IPI.
    A apresentação diferencia pagamento na China e fornecedor nacional.
    
    Aritmética racional inteira preserva crédito, segurança e tributos até o
    arredondamento. IRPJ/CSLL incide apenas sobre resultado positivo. A taxa fixa
    é aplicada uma vez por pedido. O ajuste de arredondamento fica explícito na
    composição. O cálculo é gerencial; não é apuração nem emissão fiscal.
    
    ## Acesso e pedidos
    
    - `sales.orders.read`: consultar tabelas e simular.
    - `sales.orders.manage`: criar rascunho com as condições conferidas.
    - `platform.company.manage`: visualizar custos e aprovar exceções comerciais.
    
    Custos e lucro são removidos no servidor para usuários sem gestão, tanto na
    simulação quanto na consulta do pedido. O navegador não recebe esses campos.
    O BFF conserva sessão, empresa, origem, revisão, chave idempotente e proíbe
    recursos, métodos e filtros não previstos.
    
    Criar pedido exige cliente, vencimento e acabamentos válidos. A API recalcula
    a simulação dentro da transação e compara seu digest antes de gravar.
    O pedido recebe preços unitários com IPI, coerentes com o total mostrado, e
    um snapshot privado imutável associado à versão publicada. Nenhum produto,
    tabela, proposta ou pedido anterior recebe atualização de preços.
    
    Desconto acima do livre ou lucro abaixo da meta exige aprovação explícita da
    gestão, com motivo. A aprovação usa revisão, auditoria e idempotência e altera
    a revisão do pedido. Confirmar/reservar recusa qualquer exceção pendente,
    independentemente dos controles da interface. Pedidos originados da simulação
    não aceitam edição de itens: cancelar e refazer preserva a integridade do acordo.
    O fluxo normal continua verificando estoque e regras de vendas.
    A preparação fiscal usa os valores preservados sem IPI para evitar tributação
    em duplicidade. As alíquotas gerenciais não preenchem a declaração fiscal.

    A migração `202611050901_order_pricing_snapshots.sql` cria armazenamento com RLS

    arredondamento e entradas inválidas. Teste HTTP com PostgreSQL real cobre
    isolamento, proteção de custos, versão publicada, digest, repetição de criação,
    aprovação, revisão e reserva. Testes de navegador cobrem telas pequenas,
    resultado desatualizado, entrada de desconto e recuperação de comando incerto.
    A validação em produção continua separada de código, CI e merge.

    name: dispatching-parallel-agents
    description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

    # Dispatching Parallel Agents
    
    ## Overview
    
    You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
    
    When you have multiple unrelated failures (different test files, different subsystems, different bugs), investigating them sequentially wastes time. Each investigation is independent and can happen in parallel.
    
    **Core principle:** Dispatch one agent per independent problem domain. Let them work concurrently.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    ```dot
    digraph when_to_use {
        "Multiple failures?" [shape=diamond];
        "Are they independent?" [shape=diamond];
        "Single agent investigates all" [shape=box];
        "One agent per problem domain" [shape=box];
        "Can they work in parallel?" [shape=diamond];
        "Sequential agents" [shape=box];
        "Parallel dispatch" [shape=box];
    
        "Multiple failures?" -> "Are they independent?" [label="yes"];
        "Are they independent?" -> "Single agent investigates all" [label="no - related"];
        "Are they independent?" -> "Can they work in parallel?" [label="yes"];
        "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Parallel dispatch" [label="yes"];
        "Can they work in parallel?" -> "Sequential agents" [label="no - shared state"];
    }
    ```
    
    **Use when:**
    - 3+ test files failing with different root causes
    - Multiple subsystems broken independently
    - Each problem can be understood without context from others
    - No shared state between investigations
    
    **Don't use when:**
    - Failures are related (fix one might fix others)
    - Need to understand full system state
    - Agents would interfere with each other
    
    ## The Pattern
    
    ### 1. Identify Independent Domains
    
    Group failures by what's broken:
    - File A tests: Tool approval flow
    - File B tests: Batch completion behavior
    - File C tests: Abort functionality
    
    Each domain is independent - fixing tool approval doesn't affect abort tests.
    
    ### 2. Create Focused Agent Tasks
    
    Each agent gets:
    - **Specific scope:** One test file or subsystem
    - **Clear goal:** Make these tests pass
    - **Constraints:** Don't change other code
    - **Expected output:** Summary of what you found and fixed
    
    ### 3. Dispatch in Parallel
    
    Issue all three subagent dispatches in the same response — they run in parallel:
    
    ```text
    Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts failures"
    Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts failures"
    Subagent (general-purpose): "Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts failures"
    # All three run concurrently.
    ```
    
    Multiple dispatch calls in one response = parallel execution. One per response = sequential.
    
    ### 4. Review and Integrate
    
    When agents return:
    - Read each summary
    - Verify fixes don't conflict
    - Run full test suite
    - Integrate all changes
    
    ## Agent Prompt Structure
    
    Good agent prompts are:
    1. **Focused** - One clear problem domain
    2. **Self-contained** - All context needed to understand the problem
    3. **Specific about output** - What should the agent return?
    
    ```markdown
    Fix the 3 failing tests in src/agents/agent-tool-abort.test.ts:
    
    1. "should abort tool with partial output capture" - expects 'interrupted at' in message
    2. "should handle mixed completed and aborted tools" - fast tool aborted instead of completed
    3. "should properly track pendingToolCount" - expects 3 results but gets 0
    
    These are timing/race condition issues. Your task:
    
    1. Read the test file and understand what each test verifies
    2. Identify root cause - timing issues or actual bugs?
    3. Fix by:
       - Replacing arbitrary timeouts with event-based waiting
       - Fixing bugs in abort implementation if found
       - Adjusting test expectations if testing changed behavior
    
    Do NOT just increase timeouts - find the real issue.
    
    Return: Summary of what you found and what you fixed.
    ```
    
    ## Common Mistakes
    
    **❌ Too broad:** "Fix all the tests" - agent gets lost
    **✅ Specific:** "Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts" - focused scope
    
    **❌ No context:** "Fix the race condition" - agent doesn't know where
    **✅ Context:** Paste the error messages and test names
    
    **❌ No constraints:** Agent might refactor everything
    **✅ Constraints:** "Do NOT change production code" or "Fix tests only"
    
    **❌ Vague output:** "Fix it" - you don't know what changed
    **✅ Specific:** "Return summary of root cause and changes"
    
    ## When NOT to Use
    
    **Related failures:** Fixing one might fix others - investigate together first
    **Need full context:** Understanding requires seeing entire system
    **Exploratory debugging:** You don't know what's broken yet
    **Shared state:** Agents would interfere (editing same files, using same resources)
    
    ## Real Example from Session
    
    **Scenario:** 6 test failures across 3 files after major refactoring
    
    **Failures:**
    - agent-tool-abort.test.ts: 3 failures (timing issues)
    - batch-completion-behavior.test.ts: 2 failures (tools not executing)
    - tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts: 1 failure (execution count = 0)
    
    **Decision:** Independent domains - abort logic separate from batch completion separate from race conditions
    
    **Dispatch:**
    ```
    Agent 1 → Fix agent-tool-abort.test.ts
    Agent 2 → Fix batch-completion-behavior.test.ts
    Agent 3 → Fix tool-approval-race-conditions.test.ts
    ```
    
    **Results:**
    - Agent 1: Replaced timeouts with event-based waiting
    - Agent 2: Fixed event structure bug (threadId in wrong place)
    - Agent 3: Added wait for async tool execution to complete
    
    **Integration:** All fixes independent, no conflicts, full suite green
    
    ## Verification
    
    After agents return:
    1. **Review each summary** - Understand what changed
    2. **Check for conflicts** - Did agents edit same code?
    3. **Run full suite** - Verify all fixes work together
    4. **Spot check** - Agents can make systematic errors

    name: systematic-debugging
    description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
    ---
    
    # Systematic Debugging
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
    
    **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
    ```
    
    If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Use for ANY technical issue:
    - Test failures
    - Bugs in production
    - Unexpected behavior
    - Performance problems
    - Build failures
    - Integration issues
    
    **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
    - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
    - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
    - You've already tried multiple fixes
    - Previous fix didn't work
    - You don't fully understand the issue
    
    **Don't skip when:**
    - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
    - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
    - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
    
    ## The Four Phases
    
    You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
    
    ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
    
    **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
    
    1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
       - Don't skip past errors or warnings
       - They often contain the exact solution
       - Read stack traces completely
       - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
    
    2. **Reproduce Consistently**
       - Can you trigger it reliably?
       - What are the exact steps?
       - Does it happen every time?
       - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess
    
    3. **Check Recent Changes**
       - What changed that could cause this?
       - Git diff, recent commits
       - New dependencies, config changes
       - Environmental differences
    
    4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
    
       **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**
    
       **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
       ```
       For EACH component boundary:
         - Log what data enters component
         - Log what data exits component
         - Verify environment/config propagation
         - Check state at each layer
    
       Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
       THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
       THEN investigate that specific component
       ```
    
       **Example (multi-layer system):**
       ```bash
       # Layer 1: Workflow
       echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
       echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"
    
       # Layer 2: Build script
       echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
       printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"
    
       # Layer 3: Signing script
       echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
       security list-keychains
       security find-identity -v
    
       # Layer 4: Actual signing
       codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
       ```
    
       **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)
    
    5. **Trace Data Flow**
    
       **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**
    
       See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.
    
       **Quick version:**
       - Where does bad value originate?
       - What called this with bad value?
       - Keep tracing up until you find the source
       - Fix at source, not at symptom
    
    ### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis
    
    **Find the pattern before fixing:**
    
    1. **Find Working Examples**
       - Locate similar working code in same codebase
       - What works that's similar to what's broken?
    
    2. **Compare Against References**
       - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
       - Don't skim - read every line
       - Understand the pattern fully before applying
    
    3. **Identify Differences**
       - What's different between working and broken?
       - List every difference, however small
       - Don't assume "that can't matter"
    
    4. **Understand Dependencies**
       - What other components does this need?
       - What settings, config, environment?
       - What assumptions does it make?
    
    ### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing
    
    **Scientific method:**
    
    1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
       - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
       - Write it down
       - Be specific, not vague
    
    2. **Test Minimally**
       - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
       - One variable at a time
       - Don't fix multiple things at once
    
    3. **Verify Before Continuing**
       - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
       - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
       - DON'T add more fixes on top
    
    4. **When You Don't Know**
       - Say "I don't understand X"
       - Don't pretend to know
       - Ask for help
       - Research more
    
    ### Phase 4: Implementation
    
    **Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

    name: test-driven-development
    description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
    ---
    
    # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
    
    **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
    
    **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
    
    ## When to Use
    
    **Always:**
    - New features
    - Bug fixes
    - Refactoring
    - Behavior changes
    
    **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
    - Throwaway prototypes
    - Generated code
    - Configuration files
    
    Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
    ```
    
    Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
    
    **No exceptions:**
    - Don't keep it as "reference"
    - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
    - Don't look at it
    - Delete means delete
    
    Implement fresh from tests. Period.
    
    ## Red-Green-Refactor
    
    ```dot
    digraph tdd_cycle {
        rankdir=LR;
        red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
        verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
        green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
        verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
        refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
        next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];
    
        red -> verify_red;
        verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
        verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
        green -> verify_green;
        verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
        verify_green -> green [label="no"];
        refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
        verify_green -> next;
        next -> red;
    }
    ```
    
    ### RED - Write Failing Test
    
    Write one minimal test showing what should happen.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
      let attempts = 0;
      const operation = () => {
        attempts++;
        if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
        return 'success';
      };
    
      const result = await retryOperation(operation);
    
      expect(result).toBe('success');
      expect(attempts).toBe(3);
    });
    ```
    Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    test('retry works', async () => {
      const mock = jest.fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
      await retryOperation(mock);
      expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    });
    ```
    Vague name, tests mock not code
    </Bad>
    
    **Requirements:**
    - One behavior
    - Clear name
    - Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)
    
    ### Verify RED - Watch It Fail
    
    **MANDATORY. Never skip.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test fails (not errors)
    - Failure message is expected
    - Fails because feature missing (not typos)
    
    **Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.
    
    **Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.
    
    ### GREEN - Minimal Code
    
    Write simplest code to pass the test.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        try {
          return await fn();
        } catch (e) {
          if (i === 2) throw e;
        }
      }
      throw new Error('unreachable');
    }
    ✓ • 349ms

Critérios de aceite\n\n- [ ] Todos os campos e resultados enumerados acima estão disponíveis no fluxo e foram conferidos contra todas as referências anexadas.\n- [ ] Tabela → simulação → pedido funciona com dados reais da empresa, mantendo os dados negociados e a versão utilizada.\n- [ ] Preenchimento por percentual, reais e total desejado produz resultados coerentes; quantidade e frete atualizam os valores corretamente.\n- [ ] UF e condição de contribuinte alteram os cálculos conforme o contrato verificado.\n- [ ] Entrada comercial e entrada necessária têm cálculo, rótulo e aplicação distintos e verificáveis.\n- [ ] Descontos dentro e acima do limite, fora da meta e com prejuízo seguem as regras verificadas e não podem ser contornados pela API.\n- [ ] Custos/margens restritos não aparecem em respostas para usuários sem a permissão correspondente.\n- [ ] Arredondamento, entradas inválidas, valor zero, ausência de tabela/custos/parâmetros, alteração de revisão e repetição da criação possuem comportamento validado.\n- [ ] Testes relevantes cobrem cálculo, persistência, autorização, isolamento entre empresas e aprovação.\n- [ ] Conferência visual real em desktop e celular, com teclado e estados de carregamento, vazio, erro e cálculo desatualizado.\n- [ ] Publicar tabela ou mudar parâmetros preserva pedidos e preços comerciais anteriores.\n- [ ] Relatar separadamente implementação, testes locais, CI, migrações, deploy e validação autenticada. Cadastro completo dos parâmetros comerciais\n\nOrganizar os campos em grupos legíveis, com unidade, explicação de uso, validação e edição por linha. A referência distingue parâmetros da linha de configurações gerais da empresa; confirmar no legado a abrangência de cada campo. A tela informa que logo, dia da comissão e regras de aprovação valem para toda a empresa; seus formulários completos não estão visíveis nos anexos, portanto não inferir campos adicionais.\n\n### Política comercial\n\n* Lucro líquido desejado em cada venda.\n* Desconto livre do vendedor.\n* Margem de segurança da importação / margem sobre o custo de compra para Nacional.\n* Entrada mínima pedida ao cliente.\n* Validade da proposta em dias.\n* Explicar a base da meta e o uso da margem de segurança sem expor a meta interna a quem não tenha autorização.\n* Manter a distinção entre entrada comercial configurada e sugestão/necessidade calculada para cobrir fornecedor e comissão.\n\n### Impostos usados na formação gerencial\n\n* ICMS dentro da UF de origem (a referência mostra SP).\n* PIS + COFINS.\n* IPI destacado na nota.\n* IRPJ + CSLL sobre o lucro.\n* UF de origem e ICMS interestadual padrão por linha.\n* Distinguir valores gerenciais dos perfis e cálculos efetivos do documento fiscal; evitar divergências silenciosas entre configurações.\n\n### Canal de venda\n\n* Comissão.\n* Anúncios / Ads.\n* Gateway e antecipação.\n* ICMS interestadual padrão e substituição por saída específica da UF.\n* Outras taxas de venda.\n* Taxa fixa por pedido em reais, aplicada uma única vez no pedido; conferir seu efeito sobre o lucro junto do frete.\n\n### Provisões e despesas\n\n* Perdas, garantia e inadimplência.\n* Despesas fixas mensais, integradas ao cadastro vigente de despesas fixas.\n* Explicar bases de aplicação; a referência apresenta provisões sobre o valor sem IPI.\n* Salvar parâmetros com controle de revisão, distinguir simulação/prévia de publicação e informar que pedidos anteriores mantêm suas condições.\n\n### Valores observados para conferência, sem adoção automática\n\n| Campo | Importada | Nacional |\n| -- | -- | -- |\n| Lucro líquido desejado | 15% | 15% |\n| Desconto livre | 20% | 30% |\n| Segurança sobre custo | 5% | 0% |\n| Entrada comercial | 70% | 60% |\n| Validade | 7 dias | 7 dias |\n| ICMS dentro de SP | 18% | 18% |\n| PIS + COFINS | 9,25% | 9,25% |\n| IPI | 13% | 0% |\n| IRPJ + CSLL | 34% | 34% |\n| Comissão | 2% | 2% |\n| Ads | 0,5% | 0,5% |\n| Gateway e antecipação | 0% | 0% |\n| Interestadual padrão | 4% | 4% |\n| Outras taxas | 0% | 0% |\n| Taxa fixa por pedido | R$ 0,00 | R$ 0,00 |\n| Perdas | 1% | 1% |\n| Garantia | 1,5% | 1,5% |\n| Inadimplência | 0% | 0% |\n| Despesas fixas mostradas | R$ 0,00 | R$ 0,00 |\n\n## 11. Emitente e regras fiscais por linha\n\n### Emitente\n\nDisponibilizar, organizar e integrar os campos exibidos:\n\n* Razão social, CNPJ e inscrição estadual.\n* Endereço, número, bairro, CEP, cidade, código IBGE do município e UF.\n* Regime tributário.\n* Série da nota, próximo número e ambiente.\n* Ação explícita de salvar dados fiscais com validação e confirmação.\n\nOs dados exibidos são referência do cadastro Ludus; não sobrescrever empresa ativa, regime, numeração ou ambiente ao implementar a interface. Consulta pública de CNPJ pode auxiliar o cadastro, mas não determina regime ou regras fiscais. Preservar numeração concorrente e documentos anteriores.\n\nAs abas Consultar CNPJ, Certificado, Emitente, Regras da nota, Pagamentos e Numeração aparecem na referência. A presença das abas não especifica o conteúdo não capturado nem comprova funcionamento de certificado ou emissão.\n\n### Regras da nota — Importada e Nacional\n\n* Alternância por linha, com regras persistidas separadamente.\n* Operação comum da linha e ação “Completar CFOPs vazios”, com seleção explícita e preservação dos campos preenchidos.\n* Natureza da operação.\n* CFOP dentro do estado.\n* CFOP para contribuinte de outro estado.\n* CFOP para não contribuinte de outro estado.\n* CST do ICMS.\n* CST do IPI e código de enquadramento.\n* CST e alíquota do PIS.\n* CST e alíquota da COFINS.\n* CST IBS/CBS e classificação cClassTrib.\n* Alíquotas de IBS estadual, IBS municipal e CBS.\n* Condição de consumidor final.\n* Opção de inclusão do IPI na base de ICMS na venda ao consumidor final.\n* Opção de exclusão do ICMS destacado da base de PIS/COFINS, conforme configuração validada; a imagem apresenta uma referência legal, que não deve ser tomada como validação jurídica ou fiscal desta demanda.\n* Informações complementares fixas da nota.\n* Ação “Salvar regras fiscais”.\n\nValores visuais que devem entrar na conferência, sem aplicação automática:\n\n* Importada: natureza “Venda de Mercadoria Importada”; CFOPs 5101 / 6101 / 6101; CST ICMS 00; CST IPI 50; enquadramento 999.\n* Nacional: natureza “Venda de mercadoria adquirida no mercado interno”; CFOPs 5102 / 6102 / 6102; CST ICMS 00; CST IPI 53; enquadramento 999.\n* Ambas: PIS CST 01 e 1,65%; COFINS CST 01 e 7,6%; IBS/CBS CST 000 e cClassTrib 000001; IBS estadual 0,1%, IBS municipal 0% e CBS 0,9%.\n* As três opções de condições da venda aparecem marcadas e informações complementares vazias nas capturas.\n\nConservar os códigos como texto para preservar zeros à esquerda. Enquadramento, alíquotas, CFOPs, regime e condições tributárias dependem da configuração da empresa e conferência contábil. Esta tarefa não autoriza emissão real de nota nem mudança de parâmetros em produção.\n\n## 13. Essas sete referências estão anexadas às 15 anteriores, totalizando 22.\n\n### Resultado gerencial e sugestão de entrada\n\nAlém dos campos já previstos:\n\n* Mostrar entrada mínima sugerida e ação “usar” para aplicar a sugestão de forma explícita ao parâmetro da linha.\n* A sugestão usa o produto com maior necessidade proporcional de entrada, considerando o desconto livre, e arredonda para cima em passos de 5 pontos percentuais; fórmula confirmada no código do Ludus.\n* Sem produtos válidos, não inventar sugestão.\n* Na captura: multiplicador 3,123; markup 212,3%; pior destino MA não contribuinte; ICMS + DIFAL 23%; impostos/taxas no pior caso 37,3%; lucro antes do IR necessário 22,7%; multiplicador com desconto 2,499; despesas/equilíbrio R$ 0; entrada sugerida 65%.\n* Distinguir entrada sugerida da política da linha, da entrada necessária para a venda específica e da entrada efetivamente negociada.\n* Mudança em parâmetros exige confirmação/publicação para chegar à tabela utilizada pela equipe.\n\n### Regras de aprovação da empresa\n\nCobrir a configuração e aplicação efetiva:\n\n* Desconto acima do livre sempre exige aprovação.\n* Entrada negociada abaixo da política sempre exige aprovação.\n* Pedido com prejuízo sempre exige aprovação e alçada de diretoria.\n* Configurar se lucro abaixo da meta exige aprovação.\n* Configurar se frete por conta da empresa exige aprovação.\n* Configurar se uma venda fora da política fechada pela diretoria já fica aprovada.\n* Configurar alçada do gerente: apenas pedidos na meta, ou qualquer pedido que ainda dê lucro.\n* Salvar regras, conferir permissões na API e registrar motivos/autor/data da solicitação e decisão.\n* Recusa deve conservar motivo e permitir retorno à negociação; impedir reaproveitamento de aprovação para condições alteradas.\n* Não confundir reserva/confirmação de estoque ou aprovação de folha com aprovação comercial.\n* Valores vistos: abaixo da meta marcado; frete desmarcado; autoaprovação pela diretoria desmarcada; gerente pode aprovar qualquer pedido ainda lucrativo. São configuração observada, não padrão a impor.\n\n### Formas de pagamento\n\n* Nome, inclusão explícita, lista paginada, acesso à edição e identificação de forma desligada.\n* Tratar indicação de saldo na entrega conforme modalidade/regra verificada.\n* As formas visíveis são PIX, Boleto, Transferência, Cartão de crédito, Cartão de débito, Cheque, Dinheiro, Financiamento, Na entrega e Cartão de crédito presencial.\n* A tela declara 12 formas e mostra só as primeiras dez; não inventar os dois nomes não capturados.\n* Integrar seleção da forma ao plano de entrada/saldo/parcelas do pedido quando aplicável. Cadastro da modalidade não comprova liquidação, autorização de cartão ou emissão de boleto.\n\n### Comissões\n\n* Lançamento manual por número do pedido, valor, tipo de crédito/débito, competência e motivo.\n* Associar ao vendedor correto do pedido; não transformar ajuste de comissão em recebimento de cliente.\n* Comissão gerada a partir de recebimento real, com base sem IPI, estornos preservados e separação entre apurado, pago e saldo.\n* Mostrar mês consultado, recebido líquido dos clientes, comissão do mês, falta pagar com saldos anteriores e comissão futura sobre o que não foi recebido.\n* Reaproveitar o livro de comissões e os ajustes existentes no ERP Next; não construir outro razão financeiro.\n* Distinguir indicadores globais por competência do extrato de um vendedor e da comissão apenas prevista no simulador.\n\n### Funil e nova oportunidade\n\n* Painel com quantidade/valor em andamento, escopo de equipe e busca por venda, empresa, contato ou vendedor.\n* Etapas vistas: Novo, Contato feito, Proposta enviada e Negociação; totais de Ganho e Perdido.\n* Acesso a nova oportunidade e aos módulos de prospecção, painel, campanhas e tarefas; mapear destinos e disponibilidade sem criar páginas ou dados demonstrativos como entrega funcional.\n* Nova oportunidade: CNPJ opcional com consulta cadastral; o que está sendo vendido; valor estimado; cliente existente ou empresa que ainda não é cliente; pessoa de contato; telefone/WhatsApp; e-mail; origem da oportunidade; observações; cancelar e criar.\n* Conservar o vínculo no caminho oportunidade → proposta/simulação → pedido sem exigir cadastro de cliente antes de registrar o contato inicial.\n* As capturas dos botões de campanhas/prospecção/tarefas não especificam os formulários internos desses módulos; registrar dependências e requisitos ainda não demonstrados.\n\n### Central de cadastros e configurações\n\nMapear cada entrada visível para o módulo existente ou a lacuna correspondente:\n\n* Vendas: dados da proposta, linhas de produto, formas de pagamento, cores dos equipamentos, transportadoras e contrato.\n* Funil e clientes: etapas do funil, modelos de mensagem, cadências e lembretes automáticos.\n* Comunicação: e-mail, WhatsApp, telefonia e assistente.\n* Financeiro e fiscal: fiscal/certificado, cobrança PIX, categorias de contas e despesas fixas.\n* Equipe e sistemas: usuários/perfis, produção e integrações.\n\nOrganizar acesso e preenchimento com contexto da empresa e permissões. Regras confirmadas no código original do Ludus\n\nConsulta da main de avilaops/erp-ludus; não é validação da versão implantada:\n\n* [Custo real e pagamento ao fornecedor](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/product.ts>): custo real = compra/assessoria × (1 − crédito) × (1 + segurança) + embalagem. Pagamento fornecedor/China = compra/assessoria × (1 + segurança), sem reduzir por crédito tributário.\n* [Entrada necessária](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/payment.ts>): (pagamento fornecedor + venda sem IPI × meta líquida) ÷ (1 − comissão ÷ (1 + IPI)).\n* [Entrada sugerida](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/results.ts>): escolhe a maior necessidade proporcional entre os produtos com desconto livre e arredonda para cima ao próximo passo de 5 pontos percentuais.\n* [Lucro e limites por pedido](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/order.ts>): lucro antes do IR desconta taxas, DIFAL, equipamentos, frete e taxa fixa única; IR incide nesse cálculo apenas se a sobra for positiva; lucro percentual usa venda sem IPI. Limites de desconto incluem frete e taxa fixa no custo total.\n* [Política e alçadas](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/order.ts>): desconto acima do livre, entrada abaixo da política e prejuízo exigem aprovação; abaixo da meta e frete dependem da configuração; prejuízo cabe à diretoria, e gerente pode ser limitado à meta.\n* [Configuração por empresa](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/db/company.ts>): abaixo da meta, frete, limite do gerente e autoaprovação da diretoria são persistidos.\n* [Decisão de aprovação](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/db/approvals.ts>): autoridade é conferida no servidor; recusa exige motivo e retorna à negociação; decisão usa revisão e conserva autoria.\n\nEssas são regras verificadas no software de origem, não validação de enquadramento tributário. Conferir os dados e a versão utilizados na migração e adaptar cálculos monetários ao contrato inteiro em centavos do ERP Next.\n\n## 17. Lista de pedidos — captura adicional 032924\n\nA captura “Captura de tela 2026-11-05 032924.png”, recebida durante a auditoria, acrescenta a lista de pedidos e eleva o total atual a 23 anexos.\n\nRequisitos visíveis:\n\n* Ação Novo pedido e identificação do escopo “pedidos de toda a equipe”.\n* Indicadores: valor e quantidade em aberto; valor e quantidade fechados no mês; taxa de fechamento sobre fechados e perdidos; desconto médio nos pedidos fechados.\n* Mostrar o período de referência e distinguir mês atual de consultas de todos os períodos.\n* Indicadores expansíveis/recolhíveis, preservando os números essenciais na visão compacta.\n* Abas com contagem: Em aberto, Com aprovação, Fechados (todos os períodos), Perdidos e Todos.\n* Busca por cliente, CPF/CNPJ ou número do pedido.\n* Lista com cliente, número/identificação, resumo de itens/quantidades, vendedor e desconto.\n* Abrir pedido pelo cliente/título.\n* Ordenação pelo cabeçalho, reordenação e ajuste da largura das colunas conforme a referência; garantir alternativa acessível e uso no celular.\n* Tratar cliente ainda não vinculado, mostrado como “sem cliente” no legado, sem criar um cliente fictício.     import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input"
    import { RequestError } from "@/components/feedback/session-recovery"
    import { useResource } from "@/hooks/use-operation"
    import { useNavigationGuard } from "@/components/shell/navigation-guard"
    import { states } from "./commercial-parameters"

    const selectClass = "min-h-11 w-full min-w-0 rounded-lg border border-input bg-background px-3"
    
    export function SalesSimulator() {
      const [line, setLine] = useState<"imported" | "national">("imported")
      const [version, setVersion] = useState("")
      const [locked, setLocked] = useState(false)
      const options = useResource<SimulatorOptions>(`/api/erp/sales-simulator/${line}${version ? `?versionId=${version}` : ""}`)
      useNavigationGuard(locked ? "A criação do pedido ainda não foi confirmada. Sair?" : null)
      return <main className="mx-auto max-w-7xl space-y-5 px-4 pb-24 pt-6">
        <PageHeader eyebrow="Vendas" title="Simulador de preços" description="Confira uma negociação usando os preços e parâmetros de uma tabela publicada." />
        <nav aria-label="Linha de produto" className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">{([["imported", "Importada"], ["national", "Nacional"]] as const).map(([value, label]) => <Button key={value} disabled={locked} variant={line === value ? "default" : "outline"} aria-pressed={line === value} onClick={() => { setLine(value); setVersion("") }}>{label}</Button>)}</nav>
        {options.loading ? <p role="status">Consultando tabelas publicadas…</p> : options.error ? <section role="alert" className="form-section space-y-3"><p><RequestError message={options.error} status={options.status} /></p><Button onClick={options.reload}>Tentar novamente</Button></section> : options.value && <>
          <div className="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-4"><label className="grid gap-2">Tabela publicada<select className={selectClass} value={options.value.data?.id || ""} disabled={locked || !options.value.versions.length} onChange={event => setVersion(event.target.value)}>{options.value.versions.map(row => <option key={row.id} value={row.id}>v{row.version} · {new Date(row.publishedAt).toLocaleDateString("pt-BR")}</option>)}</select></label><Link className="py-2 text-primary underline" href="/preferencias/tabela-precos">Gerenciar tabelas</Link></div>
          {!options.value.data ? <p className="form-section">Nenhuma tabela publicada nesta linha. A gestão precisa publicar uma versão antes de simular.</p> : !options.value.data.items.length ? <p className="form-section">Esta versão não tem equipamentos ativos com unidade compatível. Confira o cadastro ou selecione outra versão.</p> : <SimulatorForm key={`${options.value.tenantId}:${line}:${options.value.data.id}`} table={options.value.data} tenantId={options.value.tenantId} line={line} canCreate={options.value.canCreate} onLocked={setLocked} />}
        </>}
      </main>
    }
    
    function SimulatorForm({ table, tenantId, line, canCreate, onLocked }: {
      table: PublishedTable; tenantId: string; line: string; canCreate: boolean; onLocked: (value: boolean) => void
    }) {
      const [productId, setProductId] = useState("")
      const [search, setSearch] = useState("")
      const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState("1")
      const [destination, setDestination] = useState(table.originState)
      const [taxpayer, setTaxpayer] = useState("")
      const [kind, setKind] = useState<Discount["kind"]>("percent")
      const [discount, setDiscount] = useState("0")
      const [freight, setFreight] = useState("0")
      const [value, setValue] = useState<Simulation | null>(null)
      const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
      const [locked, setLocked] = useState(false)
      const [error, setError] = useState("")
      const generation = useRef(0)
      const product = table.items.find(item => item.productId === productId)
      const frozen = busy || locked
      function invalidate() { generation.current += 1; setValue(null); setError("") }
      function changeKind(next: Discount["kind"]) {
        const current = discountFromEntry(kind, discount)
        const count = /^\d+$/.test(quantity) ? Number(quantity) : 0
        if (current && product && count) {
          const total = product.priceWithoutIpiCents * count
          const rate = kind === "percent" ? current.value / 10000 : kind === "amount" ? current.value / total : 1 - current.value / (product.priceWithIpiCents * count)
          const number = next === "percent" ? rate * 100 : next === "amount" ? total * rate / 100 : product.priceWithIpiCents * count * (1 - rate) / 100
          setDiscount(Math.max(0, number).toFixed(2).replace(".", ","))
        } else setDiscount(next === "target" ? "" : "0")
        setKind(next); invalidate()
      }
      async function simulate(event: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
        event.preventDefault()
        if (frozen || !product) return
        const entry = discountFromEntry(kind, discount)
        const freightCents = hundredths(freight)
        if (!entry || freightCents === null || !/^\d{1,7}$/.test(quantity) || Number(quantity) < 1 || Number(quantity) > 1000000 || !taxpayer) {
          setError("Confira quantidade, inscrição estadual, desconto e frete."); return
        }
        const input: SimulationInput = { versionId: table.id, productId, quantity: Number(quantity), destination, taxpayer: taxpayer === "yes", discount: entry, freightCents }
        const requestGeneration = ++generation.current
        setBusy(true); setValue(null); setError("")
        try {
          const response = await erpFetch(`/api/erp/sales-simulator/${line}/quote`, { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Tenant-Id": tenantId }, body: JSON.stringify(input) })
          const result = await response.json()
          if (!response.ok) throw Error(result.title || "Não foi possível simular.")
          const parsed = parseSimulation(result, tenantId, line, input)
          if (requestGeneration === generation.current) setValue(parsed)
        } catch (reason) { if (requestGeneration === generation.current) setError(reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : "Simulação indisponível.") }
        finally { setBusy(false) }
      }
      return <div className="grid min-w-0 items-start gap-5 xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(22rem,0.9fr)]">
        <form className="form-section min-w-0 space-y-5" onSubmit={simulate}>
          <fieldset disabled={frozen} className="min-w-0 space-y-4">
            <legend className="mb-3 font-semibold">Equipamento e condições</legend>
            <label className="grid gap-2">Buscar equipamento<Input type="search" placeholder="Nome ou código" value={search} onChange={event => setSearch(event.target.value)} /></label>
            <label className="grid gap-2">Equipamento<select required className={selectClass} value={productId} onChange={event => { setProductId(event.target.value); invalidate() }}><option value="">Selecione o equipamento</option>{table.items.filter(item => item.productId === productId || `${item.sku} ${item.name}`.toLocaleLowerCase("pt-BR").includes(search.toLocaleLowerCase("pt-BR"))).map(item => <option key={item.productId} value={item.productId}>{item.sku} · {item.name} · {money(item.priceWithIpiCents)}</option>)}</select></label>
            <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2"><label className="grid gap-2">Quantidade<Input required inputMode="numeric" value={quantity} onChange={event => { setQuantity(event.target.value); invalidate() }} /></label><label className="grid gap-2">Destino<select className={selectClass} value={destination} onChange={event => { setDestination(event.target.value); invalidate() }}>{states.map(state => <option key={state}>{state}</option>)}</select></label></div>
            <label className="grid gap-2">Inscrição estadual<select required className={selectClass} value={taxpayer} onChange={event => { setTaxpayer(event.target.value); invalidate() }}><option value="">Informe a condição do cliente</option><option value="no">Cliente sem IE</option><option value="yes">Cliente com IE</option></select></label>
            <div className="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2"><label className="grid gap-2">Forma de informar o desconto<select className={selectClass} value={kind} onChange={event => changeKind(event.target.value as Discount["kind"])}><option value="percent">Desconto em %</option><option value="amount">Desconto em R$ (sem IPI)</option><option value="target">Cliente quer pagar</option></select></label><label className="grid gap-2">{kind === "percent" ? "Desconto em %" : kind === "amount" ? "Desconto em R$" : "Cliente quer pagar (total com IPI)"}<Input required inputMode="decimal" value={discount} onChange={event => { setDiscount(event.target.value); invalidate() }} /></label></div>
            {kind === "percent" && <label className="grid gap-2 text-sm">Ajustar desconto de 0 a 60%<input aria-label="Desconto de 0 a 60%" type="range" min="0" max="60" step="0.5" value={Math.min(60, (hundredths(discount) || 0) / 100)} onChange={event => { setDiscount(event.target.value.replace(".", ",")); invalidate() }} /></label>}
            <p className="rounded-lg bg-muted p-3 text-sm">Desconto livre até {percent(table.freeDiscountBps)}. Acima disso, ou abaixo da meta de lucro, o pedido exige aprovação.</p>
            <details><summary className="cursor-pointer py-2 text-primary">Frete por nossa conta</summary><label className="mt-2 grid gap-2">Valor do frete que a empresa paga (R$)<Input inputMode="decimal" required value={freight} onChange={event => { setFreight(event.target.value); invalidate() }} /></label></details>
            <Button type="submit" disabled={!product}>{busy ? "Simulando…" : "Simular"}</Button>
          </fieldset>
          {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
          <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Tabela v{table.version}. Simulação gerencial sem emissão fiscal. Simular não grava dados.</p>
        </form>
        <div className="min-w-0 space-y-5">{value ? <><SimulationResult value={value} imported={line === "imported"} />{canCreate && product && <SimulationOrder key={value.digest} value={value} equipment={product} line={line} onLocked={next => { setLocked(next); onLocked(next) }} />}</> : <section className="form-section"><h2 className="font-semibold">Resultado</h2><p className="mt-2 text-muted-foreground">Selecione o equipamento, informe as condições e simule para conferir o resultado.</p></section>}</div>
      </div>
    }

    export function SimulationOrder({ value, equipment, line, onLocked }: {
      value: Simulation; equipment: Equipment; line: string; onLocked: (locked: boolean) => void
    }) {
      const command = useCommand()
      const router = useRouter()
      const [customer, setCustomer] = useState<Choice | null>(null)
      const [dueDate, setDueDate] = useState("")
      const [structure, setStructure] = useState("")
      const [upholstery, setUpholstery] = useState("")
      const [error, setError] = useState("")
      const frozen = command.busy || command.uncertain
      useEffect(() => { onLocked(frozen) }, [frozen, onLocked])
      return <section className="form-section min-w-0 space-y-4" aria-label="Criar pedido da simulação">
        <h2 className="font-semibold">Criar pedido</h2><p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">O rascunho preserva a versão, os preços e as condições desta simulação.</p>
        <Lookup endpoint="parties" label="cliente" disabled={frozen} searchOnly choose={setCustomer} selectedName={customer?.legalName} />
        <form className="space-y-4" onSubmit={async event => {
          event.preventDefault()
          if (!customer || command.busy) return
          setError("")
          const result = await command.send<{ tenantId: string; id: string; status: string }>(`/api/erp/sales-simulator/${line}/orders`, value.tenantId, {
            quote: value.input, digest: value.digest, customerId: customer.id, dueDate,
            structureColor: structure || null, upholsteryColor: upholstery || null,
          })
          if (result?.tenantId === value.tenantId && result.status === "draft" && /^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/.test(result.id)) router.replace(`/vendas/pedidos/${result.id}`)
          else if (result) setError("Confirmação divergente. Consulte os pedidos antes de repetir.")
        }}>
          <fieldset disabled={frozen} className="space-y-4">
            <label className="grid gap-2">Vencimento<Input required type="date" value={dueDate} onChange={event => setDueDate(event.target.value)} /></label>
            <div className="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2"><ColorChoice label="Cor da estrutura" options={equipment.structureColors} value={structure} onChange={setStructure} /><ColorChoice palette={catalogPaletteFor(equipment.structureColors)} label={catalogPaletteFor(equipment.structureColors) ? "Cor dos braços" : "Cor do estofado"} options={equipment.upholsteryColors} value={upholstery} onChange={setUpholstery} /></div>
          </fieldset>
          {(error || command.error) && <p role="alert"><RequestError message={error || command.error} status={error ? undefined : command.status} /></p>}
          {command.stale && <p>Refaça a simulação antes de criar outro pedido.</p>}
          {command.uncertain && <p role="status">Resultado pendente. A repetição confere o mesmo comando.</p>}
          <Button type="submit" disabled={!customer || command.busy || command.stale || !!error}>{command.busy ? "Confirmando…" : command.uncertain ? "Conferir criação do pedido" : "Criar rascunho com estas condições"}</Button>
        </form>
      </section>
    }

    test("aprovação usa revisão do pedido e mantém custo restrito na consulta", async ({ page }) => {
      const orderId = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
      let revision = 1
      let approved = false
      const input = { versionId: version, productId: product, quantity: 1, destination: "SP", taxpayer: false, discount: { kind: "percent", value: 3000 }, freightCents: 0 }
      const snapshot = { tenantId: tenant, line: "imported", versionId: version, version: 6, digest: "a".repeat(64), product: { sku: equipment.sku, name: equipment.name, unit: "UN" }, input, sale: { ...sale, needsApproval: true, approvalReasons: ["discount_above_free"] }, director }
      await page.route(`**/api/erp/orders/${orderId}`, route => route.fulfill({ headers: { ETag: `"${revision}"` }, json: { tenantId: tenant, canEdit: true, pricingOrigin: true, data: { id: orderId, number: "1", customerId: customer, customerName: "Cliente de teste", customerTaxId: "52998224725", dueDate: "2026-12-30", amount: "226.00", status: "draft", revision }, items: [{ productId: product, sku: equipment.sku, name: equipment.name, unit: "UN", quantity: "1.000000", unitPrice: "226.00", amount: "226.00" }] } }))
      await page.route("**/api/erp/sales-settings", route => route.fulfill({ json: { tenantId: tenant, canEdit: false, data: null } }))
      await page.route(`**/api/erp/orders/${orderId}/pricing`, route => route.fulfill({ headers: { ETag: `"${revision}"` }, json: { tenantId: tenant, canApprove: true, data: { snapshot, needsApproval: true, approved } } }))
      await page.route(`**/api/erp/orders/${orderId}/pricing/approve`, route => {
        expect(route.request().headers()["if-match"]).toBe('"1"')
        expect(route.request().headers()["idempotency-key"]).toMatch(/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/)
        expect(route.request().postDataJSON()).toEqual({ reason: "Negociação revisada" })
        revision += 1; approved = true
        return route.fulfill({ headers: { ETag: '"2"' }, json: { tenantId: tenant, id: orderId, revision, approved } })
      })
      await page.goto(`/vendas/pedidos/${orderId}`)
      await expect(page.getByRole("link", { name: "Editar rascunho", exact: true })).toHaveCount(0)
      await page.getByText("Negociação e condições comerciais", { exact: true }).click()
      await page.getByLabel("Motivo da aprovação", { exact: true }).fill("Negociação revisada")
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Aprovar exceção comercial", exact: true }).click()
      const approvedNotice = page.getByText("Exceção comercial aprovada pela gestão.", { exact: true })
      await expect(approvedNotice).toBeAttached()
      // Reloading the order restores its compact sections after the decision.
      if (!await approvedNotice.isVisible()) await page.getByText("Negociação e condições comerciais", { exact: true }).click()
      await expect(approvedNotice).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Aprovar exceção comercial", exact: true })).toHaveCount(0)
    })
    export type Discount = { kind: "percent" | "amount" | "target"; value: number }
    export type SimulationInput = {
      versionId: string; productId: string; quantity: number; destination: string
      taxpayer: boolean; discount: Discount; freightCents: number
    }
    export type Equipment = {
      productId: string; sku: string; name: string; unit: string
      priceWithoutIpiCents: number; priceWithIpiCents: number
      structureColors: string[]; upholsteryColors: string[]
    }
    export type PublishedTable = {
      id: string; version: number; publishedAt: string; originState: string
      freeDiscountBps: number; minimumDownPaymentBps: number; ipiBps: number; items: Equipment[]
    }
    export type SimulatorOptions = {
      tenantId: string; line: string; canCreate: boolean
      versions: { id: string; version: number; publishedAt: string }[]
      data: PublishedTable | null
    }
    export type Sale = {
      quantity: number; tableUnitCents: number; tableTotalCents: number
      discountCents: number; discountBps: number; unitWithoutIpiCents: number
      unitWithIpiCents: number; netSaleCents: number; ipiCents: number; ipiBps: number
      invoiceTotalCents: number; minimumDownPaymentBps: number; minimumDownPaymentCents: number
      freeDiscountBps: number; freightCents: number
      band: "at_target" | "below_target" | "loss"; needsApproval: boolean; approvalReasons: string[]
    }
    export type Director = {
      icmsCents: number; pisCofinsCents: number; channelCents: number; provisionsCents: number
      equipmentCostCents: number; fixedFeeCents: number; roundingCents: number
      profitBeforeIncomeTaxCents: number; incomeTaxCents: number; netProfitCents: number
      netProfitBps: number; targetMarginBps: number; atTargetBps: number | null; noLossBps: number | null
      minimumTargetUnitWithIpiCents: number; supplierPaymentCents: number
      targetProfitCents: number; downPaymentCommissionCents: number
      requiredDownPaymentCents: number; requiredDownPaymentBps: number
    }
    export type Simulation = {
      tenantId: string; line: string; versionId: string; version: number; digest: string
      product: { sku: string; name: string; unit: string }
      input: SimulationInput; sale: Sale; director?: Director
    }
    export const money = (cents: number) => (cents / 100).toLocaleString("pt-BR", { style: "currency", currency: "BRL" })
    export const percent = (bps: number) => (bps / 100).toLocaleString("pt-BR", { maximumFractionDigits: 2 }) + "%"
    export const bands = { at_target: "Na meta", below_target: "Abaixo da meta", loss: "Prejuízo" }
    export const reasons: Record<string, string> = {
      discount_above_free: "Desconto acima do livre", below_target: "Lucro abaixo da meta",
    }
    export function hundredths(raw: string): number | null {
      if (!/^\d{1,12}(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?$/.test(raw.trim())) return null
      const [whole, fraction = ""] = raw.trim().replace(",", ".").split(".")
      const value = Number(whole) * 100 + Number(fraction.padEnd(2, "0"))
      return Number.isSafeInteger(value) ? value : null
    }
    export function discountFromEntry(kind: Discount["kind"], raw: string): Discount | null {
      const value = hundredths(raw)
      if (value === null || (kind === "percent" && value >= 10000) || (kind === "target" && !value)) return null
      return { kind, value }
    }
    
    export function parseSimulation(value: unknown, tenantId: string, line: string, input: SimulationInput): Simulation {
      const fail = () => { throw Error("Resultado incompleto ou divergente. Simule novamente.") }
      if (!value || typeof value !== "object") return fail()
      const result = value as Simulation
      const sale = result.sale
      if (result.tenantId !== tenantId || result.line !== line || result.versionId !== input.versionId
        || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.version) || result.version < 1 || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(result.digest)
        || !result.product || typeof result.product.name !== "string" || typeof result.product.sku !== "string"
        || !sale || !result.input) return fail()
      for (const key of ["versionId", "productId", "quantity", "destination", "taxpayer", "freightCents"] as const) {
        if (result.input[key] !== input[key]) return fail()
      }
      if (result.input.discount?.kind !== input.discount.kind || result.input.discount.value !== input.discount.value) return fail()
      const amounts = [sale.tableUnitCents, sale.tableTotalCents, sale.discountCents, sale.unitWithoutIpiCents, sale.unitWithIpiCents,
        sale.netSaleCents, sale.ipiCents, sale.invoiceTotalCents, sale.minimumDownPaymentCents, sale.freightCents]
      if (!amounts.every(n => Number.isSafeInteger(n) && n >= 0 && n <= 99_999_999_999_999)
        || ![sale.discountBps, sale.ipiBps, sale.minimumDownPaymentBps, sale.freeDiscountBps].every(n => Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 0 && n <= 10000)
        || sale.quantity !== input.quantity || sale.tableUnitCents * sale.quantity !== sale.tableTotalCents
        || sale.unitWithoutIpiCents * sale.quantity !== sale.netSaleCents || sale.unitWithIpiCents * sale.quantity !== sale.invoiceTotalCents
        || sale.netSaleCents + sale.ipiCents !== sale.invoiceTotalCents || sale.tableTotalCents - sale.netSaleCents !== sale.discountCents
        || !sale.invoiceTotalCents || sale.freightCents !== input.freightCents || !Object.hasOwn(bands, sale.band)
        || typeof sale.needsApproval !== "boolean" || !Array.isArray(sale.approvalReasons)
        || !sale.approvalReasons.every(reason => Object.hasOwn(reasons, reason))) return fail()
      if (result.director) {
        for (const [key, amount] of Object.entries(result.director)) {
          if (["atTargetBps", "noLossBps"].includes(key) && amount === null) continue
          if (!Number.isSafeInteger(amount)) return fail()
        }
        if (!Number.isSafeInteger(result.director.netProfitCents) || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.director.requiredDownPaymentCents)) return fail()
      }
      return result
    }
    ---
    title: use client
    description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.
    ---
    
    The `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature.
    
    > **Good to know:**
    >
    > You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client.
    
    ## Usage
    
    To declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function:
    
    ```tsx filename="app/components/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
    'use client'
    
    import { useState } from 'react'
    
    export default function Counter() {
      const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
    
      return (
        <div>
          <p>Count: {count}</p>
          <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>
        </div>
      )
    }
    ```

        </div>
