      { name: "Saddle Brown", x: 510, y: 1695, width: 180, height: 62 },
      { name: "Reddish Brown", x: 760, y: 1695, width: 180, height: 62 },
      { name: "Mocha", x: 1010, y: 1695, width: 180, height: 62 },
    ] as const
    
    function key(value: string) {
      return value.normalize("NFD").replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, "").toLowerCase().replace(/[\s-]+/g, "")
    }
    
    export type CatalogPalette = "dhz-hammerforce"
    
    export function catalogPaletteFor(structureColors?: readonly string[] | null): CatalogPalette | undefined {
      const colors = new Set((structureColors ?? []).map(key))
      return colors.has("pianoblack") && colors.has("titaniumgrey") && (colors.has("graphiteblack") || colors.has("mattegraphiteblack")) ? "dhz-hammerforce" : undefined
    }
    
    const hammerForceAliases: Record<string, string> = {
      preto: "Piano Black",
      grafite: "Matte Graphite Black",
      cinza: "Light Grey",
      vermelho: "Performance Red",
      laranja: "Hermès Orange",
      azul: "Ocean Blue",
    }
    
    export function catalogColorPhoto(value: string, palette?: CatalogPalette) {
      // Resolve legacy swing-arm labels only after the same product identifies its palette.
      const aliasKey = key(value)
      const alias = palette === "dhz-hammerforce" && Object.hasOwn(hammerForceAliases, aliasKey) ? hammerForceAliases[aliasKey] : undefined
      const normalized = key(alias ?? value)
      // The supplier's shortened label refers to the same named graphite finish.
      return photos.find(photo => key(photo.name) === normalized || (photo.name === "Matte Graphite Black" && normalized === "graphiteblack"))
    }
    "use client"
    
    import { catalogColorPhoto, type CatalogPalette } from "./catalog-color-photo-model"
    
    type CatalogColorPhotosProps = {
      label: string
      options?: readonly string[]
      value?: string
      onChange?: (value: string) => void
      disabled?: boolean
      palette?: CatalogPalette
      readOnly?: boolean
    }
    
    export function CatalogColorPhotos({ label, options, value, onChange, disabled, palette, readOnly = false }: CatalogColorPhotosProps) {
      const matches = [...new Set(options ?? [])].flatMap(option => {
        const photo = catalogColorPhoto(option, palette)
        return photo || readOnly ? [{ option, photo }] : []
      })
      if (!matches.length) return null
    
      return <div className="space-y-2" role="group" aria-label={`${label}: fotos do catálogo DHZ`}>
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
          {matches.map(({ option, photo }) => {
            if (!photo) return <span key={option} className="self-center rounded-full border px-3 py-1 text-sm">{option}</span>
            const scale = 56 / photo.width
            const content = <>
              <span aria-hidden="true" className="flex h-10 items-center"><span className="block shrink-0 rounded-sm" style={{
                width: 56,
                height: photo.height * scale,
                backgroundImage: 'url("/catalog/dhz-hammerforce-pro-original-colors.jpeg")',
                backgroundRepeat: "no-repeat",
                backgroundSize: `${1245 * scale}px ${1759 * scale}px`,
                backgroundPosition: `${-photo.x * scale}px ${-photo.y * scale}px`,
              }} /></span>
              <span className="break-words">{option}</span>
            </>
            const cardClass = "flex w-[4.5rem] flex-col items-center gap-1 rounded-md border p-1 text-center text-xs"
            return readOnly ? <div key={option} className={cardClass}>{content}</div> : <button key={option} type="button" disabled={disabled || !onChange} aria-pressed={value === option} onClick={() => onChange?.(option)} title={option}
              className={`${cardClass} focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 ${value === option ? "border-primary ring-1 ring-primary" : "border-border hover:border-primary"}`}>{content}</button>
          })}
        </div>
        {matches.some(match => match.photo) && <a className="text-xs text-muted-foreground underline underline-offset-2" href="/catalog/dhz-hammerforce-pro-original-colors.jpeg" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Ver cores no catálogo DHZ · HammerForce Pro, pág. 101</a>}
      </div>
    }

    import { referenceHierarchy, availableParents, loadReferenceHierarchy } from "../src/features/records/reference/reference-hierarchy.ts"
    
    const a="11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111", b="22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222", c="33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333", d="44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444"
    const node = (id,name,parentId=null,sortOrder=0,status="active")=>({id,name,parentId,sortOrder,status})
    
    test("registry URLs bound pagination, reject invalid filters and keep each list's own roles",()=>{
     assert.deepEqual(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams("q= Casa &status=active&role=supplier&offset=49"),"party"),{q:"Casa",status:"active",role:"supplier",offset:25})
     assert.equal(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams("role=supplier"),"staff").role,"")
     assert.equal(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams("role=seller"),"staff").role,"seller")
     for(const offset of ["-25","Infinity","1e4","100001","999999999999","25abc"]) assert.equal(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams({offset}),"reference").offset,0)
     const query=parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams({q:"x".repeat(200),status:"invalid",role:"employee",offset:"100000"}),"reference")
     assert.equal(query.q.length,160); assert.equal(query.status,""); assert.equal(query.role,""); assert.equal(query.offset,100000)
     assert.equal(registryQueryString({q:"Casa & filial",status:"archived",role:"customer",offset:25}),"q=Casa+%26+filial&status=archived&role=customer&offset=25")
     assert.equal(registryQueryString({q:"",status:"",role:"",offset:0}),"")
    })
    
    test("category paths retain sibling order and prevent self/descendant parenting",()=>{
     const options=referenceHierarchy([node(c,"Série B",a,2),node(a,"Premium",null,1),node(b,"Core",null,0),node(d,"Série A",a,1)])
     assert.deepEqual(options.map(x=>x.path),["Core","Premium","Premium / Série A","Premium / Série B"])
     assert.equal(options.find(x=>x.id===d).depth,1)
     assert.deepEqual(availableParents(options,a).map(x=>x.id),[b])
     assert.deepEqual(availableParents(options,d).map(x=>x.id),[b,a,c])
    })
    
    test("invalid hierarchies fail visibly instead of losing or silently reparenting records",()=>{
     for(const nodes of [[node(a,"A",b)], [node(a,"A",b),node(b,"B",a)], [node(a,"A"),node(a,"Again")], [node(a,"A",a)]]) assert.throws(()=>referenceHierarchy(nodes))
     const deep=Array.from({length:70},(_,index)=>node(`00000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(index).padStart(12,"0")}`,`N${index}`,index?`00000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(index-1).padStart(12,"0")}`:null))
     assert.throws(()=>referenceHierarchy(deep),/profundidade/)
    })
    
    test("archived ancestors and incompatible financial nature are excluded from new choices",()=>{
     const options=referenceHierarchy([{...node(a,"Receitas"),direction:"income"},{...node(b,"Despesas"),direction:"expense"},{...node(c,"Antiga",null,0,"archived"),direction:"income"},{...node(d,"Filha",c),direction:"income"}])
     assert.deepEqual(availableParents(options,null,"income").map(x=>x.id),[a])
     assert.equal(options.find(x=>x.id===d).available,false)
    })
    
    test("category pagination rejects a different company and incomplete/changing snapshots",async()=>{
     const reply=value=>Promise.resolve(new Response(JSON.stringify(value),{status:200,headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"}}))
     const rows=[node(a,"Premium"),node(b,"Linha",a)]
     const calls=[]
     const options=await loadReferenceHierarchy("product-categories",a,new AbortController().signal,async(url,init)=>{calls.push({url,tenant:init.headers["X-Tenant-Id"]});return reply({tenantId:a,total:2,data:calls.length===1?[rows[0]]:[rows[1]]})})
     assert.deepEqual(options.map(x=>x.path),["Premium","Premium / Linha"])
     assert.equal(calls[1].url,"/api/erp/product-categories?limit=100&offset=1");assert.equal(calls[0].tenant,a)
     await assert.rejects(loadReferenceHierarchy("product-categories",a,new AbortController().signal,()=>reply({tenantId:b,total:0,data:[]})),/empresa/)
     await assert.rejects(loadReferenceHierarchy("product-categories",a,new AbortController().signal,()=>reply({tenantId:a,total:1,data:[]})),/completa/)
     let page=0
     await assert.rejects(loadReferenceHierarchy("product-categories",a,new AbortController().signal,()=>reply({tenantId:a,total:++page===1?2:3,data:[rows[page===1?0:1]]})),/mudaram/)
    })

    import NextLink from "next/link"
    import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
    import { listNavigationHref } from "@/lib/list-navigation"
    import { guardBrowserHistory } from "./history-navigation-guard"
    import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useMemo, useRef, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from "react"
    
    type Guard = () => string | null
    type NavigationGuard = { register: (guard: Guard) => () => void; confirmNavigation: () => boolean; allowNextUnload: () => () => void }
    const NavigationGuardContext = createContext<NavigationGuard>({ register: () => () => {}, confirmNavigation: () => true, allowNextUnload: () => () => {} })
    
    export function NavigationGuardProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
      const activeGuards = useRef(new Set<Guard>())
      const approvedUnload = useRef(false)
      const allowNextUnload = useCallback(() => {
        approvedUnload.current = true
        return () => { approvedUnload.current = false }
      }, [])
      const register = useCallback((guard: Guard) => {
        activeGuards.current.add(guard)
        return () => { activeGuards.current.delete(guard) }
      }, [])
      const confirmNavigation = useCallback(() => {
        for (const guard of activeGuards.current) {
          const message = guard()
          if (message) return window.confirm(message)
        }
        return true
      }, [])
      useLayoutEffect(() => guardBrowserHistory(confirmNavigation), [confirmNavigation])
      useEffect(() => {
        const beforeUnload = (event: BeforeUnloadEvent) => {
          if (approvedUnload.current) { approvedUnload.current = false; return }
          if ([...activeGuards.current].some(guard => !!guard())) { event.preventDefault(); event.returnValue = "" }
        }
        window.addEventListener("beforeunload", beforeUnload)
        return () => window.removeEventListener("beforeunload", beforeUnload)
      }, [])
      const value = useMemo(() => ({ register, confirmNavigation, allowNextUnload }), [register, confirmNavigation, allowNextUnload])
      return <NavigationGuardContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</NavigationGuardContext.Provider>
    }
    
    export function useNavigationGuard(message: string | null) {
      const { register } = useContext(NavigationGuardContext)
      useLayoutEffect(() => register(() => message), [message, register])
    }
    
    export function useConfirmNavigation() {
      return useContext(NavigationGuardContext).confirmNavigation
    }
    
    export function useAllowNextUnload() {
      return useContext(NavigationGuardContext).allowNextUnload
    }
    
    export function GuardedLink({ onNavigate, ...props }: ComponentProps<typeof NextLink>) {
      const confirmNavigation = useConfirmNavigation()
      const pathname = usePathname()
      const search = useSearchParams()
      const href = typeof props.href === "string" ? listNavigationHref(props.href, pathname, search.toString()) : props.href
      return <NextLink {...props} href={href} onNavigate={event => {
        if (!confirmNavigation()) { event.preventDefault(); return }
        onNavigate?.(event)
      }} />
    }

    ---
    title: useSearchParams
    description: API Reference for the useSearchParams hook.
    ---
    
    `useSearchParams` is a **Client Component** hook that lets you read the current URL's **query string**.
    
    `useSearchParams` returns a **read-only** version of the [`URLSearchParams`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams) interface.
    
    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/search-bar.tsx" switcher
    'use client'
    
    import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
    
    export default function SearchBar() {
      const searchParams = useSearchParams()
    
      const search = searchParams.get('search')
    
      // URL -> `/dashboard?search=my-project`
      // `search` -> 'my-project'
      return <>Search: {search}</>
    }
    ```
    
    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/search-bar.js" switcher
    'use client'
    
    import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
    
    export default function SearchBar() {
      const searchParams = useSearchParams()
    
      const search = searchParams.get('search')
    
      // URL -> `/dashboard?search=my-project`
      // `search` -> 'my-project'
      return <>Search: {search}</>
    }
    ```
    
    ## Parameters
    
    ```tsx
    const searchParams = useSearchParams()
    ```
    
    `useSearchParams` does not take any parameters.
    
    ## Returns
    
    `useSearchParams` returns a **read-only** version of the [`URLSearchParams`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams) interface, which includes utility methods for reading the URL's query string:
    
    - [`URLSearchParams.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/get): Returns the first value associated with the search parameter. For example:
    
      | URL                  | `searchParams.get("a")`                                                                                         |
      | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | `/dashboard?a=1`     | `'1'`                                                                                                           |
      | `/dashboard?a=`      | `''`                                                                                                            |
      | `/dashboard?b=3`     | `null`                                                                                                          |
      | `/dashboard?a=1&a=2` | `'1'` _- use [`getAll()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/getAll) to get all values_ |
    
    - [`URLSearchParams.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/has): Returns a boolean value indicating if the given parameter exists. For example:
    
      | URL              | `searchParams.has("a")` |
      | ---------------- | ----------------------- |
      | `/dashboard?a=1` | `true`                  |
      | `/dashboard?b=3` | `false`                 |
    
    - Learn more about other **read-only** methods of [`URLSearchParams`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams), including the [`getAll()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/getAll), [`keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/keys), [`values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/values), [`entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/entries), [`forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/forEach), and [`toString()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/toString).

    name: brainstorming
    description: "You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation)."
    ---
    
    # Brainstorming
    
    You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
    partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
    skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
    anything gets built.
    
    People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
    help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
    hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.
    
    ## First: What Do You Actually Know?
    
    Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
    why?
    
    - **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
      blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
    - **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.
    
    Before you start implementing, you must, in order:
    
    1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
       human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
    2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
    3. Get their approval of that doc.
    4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.
    
    Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
    feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
    the questions.
    
    ## Look Before You Ask
    
    In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
    a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
    first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
    connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
    parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
    project or their context already answers.
    
    ## Your First Message
    
    Move the work forward, with one of these:
    
    - **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
      request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
      request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
      shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
      Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
      and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
      have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
      has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
      so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
      want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
      corrections, then one question about what they want: the thing their
      request leaves open whose answer would most change what gets built.
      Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
    - **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
      biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
      what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
      my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
      I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
      different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"
    
    How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
    brainstorming:
    
    - **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
      design discussion): end with your question. They want this
      conversation.
    - **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. After your
      question, add a light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
      "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
      it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
      (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
      asked through the normal workflow.
    
    That's the whole message.
    
    ## The Conversation
    
    Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
    example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
    above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
    process jargon. You never need to quote this skill to your human
    partner.
    
    Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
    report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
    the rest.
    
    **Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
    intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
    stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
    something concrete.
    
    **How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
    materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
    libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
    of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
    they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
    want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
    said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
    uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
    something they agreed to.
    
    **Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
    out as questions:
    
    - what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
    - why now, and what success looks like to them
    - goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
      if it technically works)
    - prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
    - current state: what exists now, what they've tried
    - the details they care about
    
    **Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
    you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
    question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
    them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
    ("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
    Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
    already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
    change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
    beats a question.
    
    **Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
    would help, offer to go look: deeper into their codebase or project,
    their own files and data, or the web. Say what you'd look for. They
    decide whether you go.
    
    **Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
    before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
    of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
    ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
    existing work rules out. Present the two or three that remain, grounding
    each in what the project actually does and saying what it trades off.
    Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want to go. When
    there's genuinely one sensible way, say so and explain why the others
    don't fit. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
    describing first.
    
    **Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
    would help more than reading:
    
    - something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
    - a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
    - a flow or a sequence of steps

    name: image-to-code
    description: "Implement a selected image, screenshot, mockup, or Image Gen reference as a faithful, responsive frontend."
    ---
    
    # Image to Code
    
    You're tasked with translating the visual target image into a high-quality, interactive website or web app.
    
    ## Critical Overrides
    
    - Refer to the Plugin router [$index](../index/SKILL.md) before proceeding.
    - Follow [$critical-overrides](../../references/critical-overrides.md).
    
    ## User Context
    
    Before starting, load [$user-context](../user-context/SKILL.md) and run its preflight script when local shell access is available.
    
    Use saved product URLs, Figma files, screenshots, reference images, codebase paths, Storybook, tokens, design systems, brand assets, component refs, browser preferences, and share targets as grounding material when relevant.
    
    Do not inspect every saved reference. Inspect only what the current task needs.
    
    ### [IMPORTANT] Previewing prototypes in ChatGPT Work Mode
    
    Starting `sites-preview` is not verification. Verification requires opening `http://terminal.local:4173/` in the cloud browser, inspecting the rendered page, testing primary interactions, checking browser console errors, and passing design QA.
    
    Do not substitute HTTP health, build success, preview-service status, or deployment success for browser verification. If the cloud browser cannot be used, report verification as blocked.
    
    For local prototype verification and design QA in ChatGPT Work Mode:
    
    1. Install dependencies if needed. The project must have an npm `dev` script.
    2. `sites-preview` runs `npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4173 --strictPort`. The `dev` script must accept those flags.
    3. For Product Design Vite starters, use `"dev": "vite"`. Configure Vite with `server.host: "0.0.0.0"` and `server.allowedHosts: ["terminal.local"]`. Preserve an existing Sites project's supported dev script; do not replace its runtime.
    4. From the site root, run `sites-preview start "$PWD"`.
    5. Open `http://terminal.local:4173/` in the cloud browser. Do not use `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, HTTPS, or another port.
    6. Verify the rendered site and its primary interactions before reporting completion.
    7. Keep the local preview open for the user. Do not deploy to Sites unless the user explicitly asks to share, publish, or deploy.
    
    ## Workflow
    
    CRITICAL: THIS IS NOT GUIDANCE. THIS IS A CHECKLIST TO COMPLETE.
    
    1. Do not start unless you have a selected image, screenshot, mockup, or Image Gen result to recreate. A written brief is not enough.
    
    2. Resolve the exact selected visual target before building.
    
        - If the user selected a numbered `$ideate` option, use the Nth displayed generated-image result from the most recent ideation set. Do not use the original concept planning order or Image Gen prompt submission order.
        - Use the concept-name list from `$ideate` only when it was explicitly written in the same displayed-image order.
        - A generated-image result ID, selected image attachment, screenshot, mockup, or Figma frame is stronger than a bare ordinal. Prefer that exact reference when available.
        - If the selected result cannot be resolved unambiguously, stop before implementation and ask the user to name the concept or reattach/select the image. Never guess and build a nearby option.
    
        Mobile runtime exception: 1:1 fidelity applies only to app-owned content inside the device screen. `PhoneFrame`, `StatusBar`, `HomeIndicator`, `KeyboardDock`, and the device assets are template-owned infrastructure. Preserve them even if the reference omits them, depicts different device chrome, or includes chrome in the image. Never recreate device chrome as an image asset.
    
    3. Treat the resolved image as the design to recreate.
    
    4. If the provided design is a mobile viewport, build a mobile app. When creating a fresh local app for that case, use [local-prototype-preflight](../../references/local-prototype-preflight.md) with `--template mobile-app`. If it's unclear, default to desktop.
    
       Before planning or implementing with the `mobile-app` template, read its `AGENTS.md` and follow its runtime and component guidance.
    
    5. Review the reference design, catalog every image asset in the design, and use the Image Gen tool to create individual images for each one. Zoom in so you can catch every asset that needs to be generated.
    
        Examples include:
    
        - Hero images including full bleed image backgrounds
        - Featured article imagery
        - Thumbnails
        - Decorative illustrations
        - Textures and background motifs
        - Logos
        - Product images
        - Avatars
    
        Rules:
    
        - CRITICAL RULE: Do not create custom div art, CSS art, inline SVGs, handcrafted SVGs, HTML element drawings, div/span shapes, CSS drawings, gradients, emoji, or text glyphs instead of real icons and image assets ever. Use the built-in Image Gen tool for images and the closest matching icon library for icons.
        - If text is part of an image asset, keep it in the image asset. Examples include full bleed hero images, signs, posters, packaging, storefronts, article art, and illustrations where the type belongs to the visual itself. Do not crop the background image and recreate that text with transparent text boxes, HTML, CSS, or separate overlay layers unless the source clearly shows editable UI text sitting on top of the image.
        - Do not use generic placeholders where the reference implies custom visual content.
        - Generated assets must share the same art direction, palette, rendering style, and design language as the reference mockup.
        - The built-in Image Gen tool does not support transparent images; post-process generated assets when transparency is required.
        - For mobile prototypes, do not catalog or generate device bezels, notches, status bars, clocks, signal or battery indicators, or home indicators. The mobile runtime owns those elements.
    
    ### Parallel asset production
    
    After cataloging and measuring the reference assets, spawn up to three asset subagents while the main agent builds the app structure.
    
    Give each subagent one raster asset task at a time with its reference crop, exact dimensions, focal point, style, output path, and consuming component. Asset subagents generate, inspect, save, and report the asset path only. They must not edit source code, run the browser, or deploy.
    
    Prioritize critical above-the-fold assets first, then reuse agents for supporting assets. Do not delegate standard UI icons or supplied brand logos.
    
    6. Define all sections of the page. For each section, meticulously measure the layout, spacing between elements, and the size and space of the elements themselves.
    
    7. Find freely available fonts that match the target design.
    
    8. Find a freely available icon library that matches the target design. Do not default to Lucide icons. Search for the best match.
    
        Rules:
    
        - CRITICAL RULE: Do not create custom inline SVGs, handcrafted SVGs, HTML element drawings, div/span shapes, CSS drawings, gradients, emoji, or text glyphs. Use the built-in Image Gen tool to generate assets and use the closest matching icon library for icons.
    
    9. Build the app starting with [local-prototype-preflight](../../references/local-prototype-preflight.md). Unless the user asks for a static mock, full production behavior, or a different scope, bring the app or website to life with:
    
        - Working navigation, links, tabs, menus, and primary CTAs.
        - Functional inputs, filters, toggles, selections, and forms shown in the main experience.
        - Visible UI states: hover, focus, selected, open/closed, loading, empty, and success where relevant.
        - The main task, conversion path, or user journey working from start to finish when the product has one.
    
        Controls outside the core experience may be visual-only. Do not build auth, persistence, backend/API calls, integrations, or exhaustive edge cases unless requested.
    
        Rules:
    
        - Place every image asset you generated into its position before proceeding. I repeat, replace all placeholders, including CSS/SVG placeholders, before proceeding.
        - Do not leave controls in the core experience as static chrome. Do not create new pages or routes unless the user asks for them.
    
    10. Run the local app.
    
    11. Capture the local app using the Browser Choice rule in [$index](../index/SKILL.md#browser-choice).
    
    12. Run [design-qa](../design-qa/SKILL.md) as the blocking build gate.
    
        Steps:
    
        - Open the reference image and the latest prototype screenshot before writing the QA report.
        - Compare the same viewport and the same interaction state. If they do not match, capture the missing view first.
        - Save the QA report as `design-qa.md` in the project root.
        - Fix P0/P1/P2 issues, capture the app again, and repeat until the QA report says `final result: passed`.
        - Do not keep looping on P3 polish. Include any remaining P3s as follow-up iteration notes.
        - If source capture, prototype capture, or visual comparison is blocked, stop. `design-qa.md` must say `final result: blocked`.
        - Do not hand off unless `design-qa.md` exists and says `final result: passed`.
    
    13. Handoff the app or website.

    name: writing-plans
    description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
    ---
    
    # Writing Plans
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.
    
    **Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."
    
    **Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.
    
    **Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
    - (User preferences for plan location override this default)
    
    ## Scope Check
    
    If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.
    
    ## File Structure
    
    Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.
    
    - Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
    - You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
    - Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.
    
    This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.
    
    ## Task Right-Sizing
    
    A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
    fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
    configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
    deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
    reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
    independently testable deliverable.
    
    ## Step Granularity
    
    **Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
    - "Write the failing test" - step
    - "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
    - "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
    - "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
    - "Commit" - step
    
    ## Plan Document Header
    
    **Every plan MUST start with this header:**
    
    ```markdown
    # [Feature Name] Implementation Plan
    
    > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
    
    **Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]
    
    **Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]
    
    **Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]
    
    **Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
    argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]
    
    ## Global Constraints
    
    [The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
    naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
    values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
    include this section.]
    
    ## Review Focus
    
    [The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
    tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
    — one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
    reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
    document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
    meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
    break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
    you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
    owns the code, in that task's own step style.]
    
    ---
    ```

    const uuid = /^[a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{12}$/i
    export function productImportHref(id: string, pending = false) {
      if (!uuid.test(id)) throw Error("O identificador da prévia é inválido.")
      return `/preferencias/dados/importacao?job=${id}${pending ? "&pending=1" : ""}`
    }
    export async function readProductImportFile(file: File) {
      if (!file.name.toLowerCase().endsWith(".csv") || file.size === 0 || file.size > 2 * 1024 * 1024) throw Error("Selecione um CSV não vazio de até 2 MiB.")
      if (new TextEncoder().encode(file.name).length > 160) throw Error("Use um nome de arquivo CSV mais curto (até 160 bytes).")
      let content: string
      // Preserve a UTF-8 BOM too: the backend supports it and hashes the original content.
      try { content = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true }).decode(await file.arrayBuffer()) } catch { throw Error("Salve o CSV em UTF-8 e selecione o arquivo novamente.") }
      return { filename: file.name, content }
    }
    export async function readProductImport(response: Response, expectedId?: string): Promise<ProductImport> {
      const body = await response.json().catch(() => null)
      if (!response.ok) throw Error(typeof body?.title === "string" ? body.title : "Não foi possível consultar a importação. Tente novamente.")
      const data = body?.data
      const validRow = (row: ProductImportRow) => row && Number.isInteger(row.line) && row.line >= 2 && typeof row.input?.sku === "string" && typeof row.input?.name === "string" && typeof row.conflict === "boolean" && (row.error == null || typeof row.error === "string" && row.error.length > 0)
      if (!data || typeof data.id !== "string" || !uuid.test(data.id) || expectedId && data.id.toLowerCase() !== expectedId.toLowerCase()
        || typeof data.filename !== "string" || data.format !== "csv" || !["previewed", "imported"].includes(data.status)
        || !Array.isArray(data.rows) || data.rows.length === 0 || data.rows.length > 5000 || !data.rows.every(validRow)
        || new Set(data.rows.map((row: ProductImportRow) => row.line)).size !== data.rows.length
        || data.valid !== data.rows.filter((row: ProductImportRow) => !row.error && !row.conflict).length
        || data.invalid !== data.rows.filter((row: ProductImportRow) => !!row.error).length
        || data.conflicts !== data.rows.filter((row: ProductImportRow) => row.conflict).length
        || data.status === "imported" && (!data.result || !Number.isInteger(data.result.imported) || data.result.imported < 0 || data.result.imported > data.valid || data.result.total !== data.rows.length)) throw Error("O serviço retornou um resultado de importação inválido. Confira a prévia novamente.")
      return data as ProductImport
    }

    impl ProposalInput {
        fn normalize_legacy_component_colors(&mut self) -> Result<(), DomainError> {
            for item in &mut self.items {
                let Some(legacy) = item.arm_color.take() else {
                    continue;
                };
                if item
                    .plate_holder_color
                    .as_deref()
                    .is_some_and(|current| !current.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(legacy.trim()))
                {
                    return Err(DomainError::Invalid(
                        "Informe a cor dos anilheiros apenas em plateHolderColor",
                    ));
                }
                if item.plate_holder_color.is_none() {
                    item.plate_holder_color = Some(legacy);
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    {"id":"AVL-432","title":"ERP Next — simulador comercial completo antes do pedido, com paridade das telas Ludus","description":"## Objetivo\n\nOrganizar no ERP Next uma experiência comercial fácil de visualizar e preencher, cobrindo TODAS as informações das capturas do ERP Ludus fornecidas pelo usuário, incluindo as referências adicionais de parâmetros comerciais, ICMS por UF, emitente e regras fiscais. O fluxo deve permitir consultar a tabela, simular a venda, conferir composição, lucro, entrada e limites e criar um pedido conservando as condições calculadas.\n\nSolicitação: “consegue organizar tudo isso e deixar assim facil de ver e facil de inserir? mas tem que ter TODAS essas informações”.\n\n## Referências e situação verificada\n\nRepositório: [https://github.com/avilaops/erp-next](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-next>)\n\nAs quatro capturas estão anexadas aos recursos desta issue:\n\n* Captura de tela 2026-11-05 031339.png — tabela de preços.\n* screenshot-2026-11-05-031121.png — simulação Nacional, tabela v4.\n* Captura de tela 2026-11-05 031410.png — simulação Importada, tabela v6.\n* Captura de tela 2026-11-05 031439.png — simulação Importada expandida, composição, custos/lucro e entrada necessária.\n\nInspeção de código local e main realizada em 05/11/2026; disponibilidade autenticada em produção não foi validada. Já existem parâmetros por linha, custos de produtos e publicação de tabela versionada. O formulário atual de pedido recebe cliente, vencimento e itens/acabamentos e usa o preço base do catálogo; ainda não integra o simulador descrito aqui.\n\nFontes:\n\n* [Parâmetros comerciais existentes](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-next/blob/main/docs/PARAMETROS-COMERCIAIS-2026-11-04.md>)\n* [Formulário de pedido](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-next/blob/main/apps/web/src/features/sales/orders.tsx>)\n* [API de pedidos](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-next/blob/main/apps/api/src/domains/sales.rs>)\n* [Cálculo gerencial e limites por destino](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-next/blob/main/apps/api/src/platform/commercial_settings_model.rs>)\n\n## 1. Consulta da tabela de preços\n\n* Alternar entre Importada e Nacional.\n* Mostrar número da versão e data da tabela e indicar se o preço destacado contém IPI.\n* Buscar equipamento por nome ou código/SKU, com filtros e paginação.\n* Exibir equipamento, SKU, preço sem IPI, preço com IPI e desconto livre.\n* Permitir iniciar o pedido/simulação pelo equipamento selecionado, sem redigitar seus dados.\n* Disponibilizar os limites de desconto na meta por destino.\n* Manter acesso à edição de custos, parâmetros/metas e publicação conforme permissões.\n\n## 2. Entrada da simulação\n\nOrganizar dados de preenchimento e resultado lado a lado no desktop e em sequência legível no celular, usando os componentes e identidade atuais do ERP Next.\n\n* Linha comercial e versão da tabela utilizada.\n* Estado da simulação: não salva, calculada, alterada após o cálculo.\n* Equipamento com nome, SKU, preço, troca de equipamento e quantidade.\n* UF de destino.\n* Condição de inscrição estadual/contribuinte, incluindo cliente sem IE, conferindo os estados disponíveis no legado.\n* Desconto em percentual e em reais, sincronizados.\n* Campo “Cliente quer pagar (total do pedido)” para calcular o desconto equivalente.\n* Controle visual da faixa de desconto, limite livre e faixa que exige aprovação.\n* Opção “Frete por nossa conta” e valor do frete pago pela empresa.\n* Ação “Simular” e acesso claro às configurações necessárias quando faltarem dados.\n* Preservar seleção de cliente, vencimento e acabamentos já existentes no pedido; evitar redigitação na conversão.\n\n## 3. Resultado comercial e composição\n\nExibir antes de criar o pedido:\n\n* Resumo de equipamento, quantidade e destino.\n* Total da venda com IPI.\n* Indicador de atendimento à meta, como “Na meta”, e indicação clara quando fora dela.\n* Entrada mínima comercial: percentual e valor em reais.\n* Lucro líquido da venda em reais e percentual e meta aplicada, com acesso conforme permissão.\n* Composição expansível: preço de tabela unitário sem IPI; desconto em percentual e reais; valor sem IPI; alíquota e valor do IPI; preço unitário com IPI; total da venda.\n* Preço mínimo na meta com IPI por unidade.\n\n## 4. Custos e lucro restritos à diretoria/gestão autorizada\n\nReproduzir a informação gerencial das capturas:\n\n* Valor da venda sem IPI.\n* Impostos e taxas: percentual e valor.\n* Custo dos equipamentos.\n* Sobra antes do IR.\n* IRPJ + CSLL.\n* Lucro líquido: valor e percentual.\n* Desconto máximo na meta, com identificação da meta percentual.\n* Desconto máximo sem prejuízo.\n* Impacto do frete e das condições negociadas no resultado.\n\nA restrição deve ocorrer no servidor e nos dados retornados, além da interface. Definir a permissão apropriada dentro do RBAC existente; não presumir que qualquer vendedor pode consultar custos ou margens internas.\n\n## 5. Emitente e regras fiscais por linha\n\n### Emitente\n\nDisponibilizar, organizar e integrar os campos exibidos:\n\n* Razão social, CNPJ e inscrição estadual.\n* Endereço, número, bairro, CEP, cidade, código IBGE do município e UF.\n* Regime tributário.\n* Série da nota, próximo número e ambiente.\n* Ação explícita de salvar dados fiscais com validação e confirmação.\n\nOs dados exibidos são referência do cadastro Ludus; não sobrescrever empresa ativa, regime, numeração ou ambiente ao implementar a interface. A presença das abas não especifica o conteúdo não capturado nem comprova funcionamento de certificado ou emissão.\n\n### Regras da nota — Importada e Nacional\n\n* Alternância por linha, com regras persistidas separadamente.\n* Operação comum da linha e ação “Completar CFOPs vazios”, com seleção explícita e preservação dos campos preenchidos.\n* Natureza da operação.\n* CFOP dentro do estado.\n* CFOP para contribuinte de outro estado.\n* CFOP para não contribuinte de outro estado.\n* CST do ICMS.\n* CST do IPI e código de enquadramento.\n* CST e alíquota do PIS.\n* CST e alíquota da COFINS.\n* CST IBS/CBS e classificação cClassTrib.\n* Alíquotas de IBS estadual, IBS municipal e CBS.\n* Condição de consumidor final.\n* Opção de inclusão do IPI na base de ICMS na venda ao consumidor final.\n* Opção de exclusão do ICMS destacado da base de PIS/COFINS, conforme configuração validada; a imagem apresenta uma referência legal, que não deve ser tomada como validação jurídica ou fiscal desta demanda.\n* Informações complementares fixas da nota.\n* Ação “Salvar regras fiscais”.\n\nValores visuais que devem entrar na conferência, sem aplicação automática:\n\n* Importada: natureza “Venda de Mercadoria Importada”; CFOPs 5101 / 6101 / 6101; CST ICMS 00; CST IPI 50; enquadramento 999.\n* Nacional: natureza “Venda de mercadoria adquirida no mercado interno”; CFOPs 5102 / 6102 / 6102; CST ICMS 00; CST IPI 53; enquadramento 999.\n* Ambas: PIS CST 01 e 1,65%; COFINS CST 01 e 7,6%; IBS/CBS CST 000 e cClassTrib 000001; IBS estadual 0,1%, IBS municipal 0% e CBS 0,9%.\n* As três opções de condições da venda aparecem marcadas e informações complementares vazias nas capturas.\n\nConservar os códigos como texto para preservar zeros à esquerda. Cadastro da modalidade não comprova liquidação, autorização de cartão ou emissão de boleto.\n\n### Comissões\n\n* Lançamento manual por número do pedido, valor, tipo de crédito/débito, competência e motivo.\n* Associar ao vendedor correto do pedido; o que está sendo vendido; valor estimado; cliente existente ou empresa que ainda não é cliente; pessoa de contato; telefone/WhatsApp; e-mail; origem da oportunidade; observações; cancelar e criar.\n* Conservar o vínculo no caminho oportunidade → proposta/simulação → pedido sem exigir cadastro de cliente antes de registrar o contato inicial.\n* As capturas dos botões de campanhas/prospecção/tarefas não especificam os formulários internos desses módulos; registrar dependências e requisitos ainda não demonstrados.\n\n### Central de cadastros e configurações\n\nMapear cada entrada visível para o módulo existente ou a lacuna correspondente:\n\n* Vendas: dados da proposta, linhas de produto, formas de pagamento, cores dos equipamentos, transportadoras e contrato.\n* Funil e clientes: etapas do funil, modelos de mensagem, cadências e lembretes automáticos.\n* Comunicação: e-mail, WhatsApp, telefonia e assistente.\n* Financeiro e fiscal: fiscal/certificado, cobrança PIX, categorias de contas e despesas fixas.\n* Equipe e sistemas: usuários/perfis, produção e integrações.\n\nOrganizar acesso e preenchimento com contexto da empresa e permissões. Regras confirmadas no código original do Ludus\n\nConsulta da main de avilaops/erp-ludus; não é validação da versão implantada:\n\n* [Custo real e pagamento ao fornecedor](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/product.ts>): custo real = compra/assessoria × (1 − crédito) × (1 + segurança) + embalagem. Pagamento fornecedor/China = compra/assessoria × (1 + segurança), sem reduzir por crédito tributário.\n* [Entrada necessária](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/payment.ts>): (pagamento fornecedor + venda sem IPI × meta líquida) ÷ (1 − comissão ÷ (1 + IPI)).\n* [Entrada sugerida](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/results.ts>): escolhe a maior necessidade proporcional entre os produtos com desconto livre e arredonda para cima ao próximo passo de 5 pontos percentuais.\n* [Lucro e limites por pedido](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/order.ts>): lucro antes do IR desconta taxas, DIFAL, equipamentos, frete e taxa fixa única; IR incide nesse cálculo apenas se a sobra for positiva; lucro percentual usa venda sem IPI. Limites de desconto incluem frete e taxa fixa no custo total.\n* [Política e alçadas](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/pricing/order.ts>): desconto acima do livre, entrada abaixo da política e prejuízo exigem aprovação; abaixo da meta e frete dependem da configuração; prejuízo cabe à diretoria, e gerente pode ser limitado à meta.\n* [Configuração por empresa](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/db/company.ts>): abaixo da meta, frete, limite do gerente e autoaprovação da diretoria são persistidos.\n* [Decisão de aprovação](<https://github.com/avilaops/erp-ludus/blob/main/src/lib/db/approvals.ts>): autoridade é conferida no servidor; recusa exige motivo e retorna à negociação; decisão usa revisão e conserva autoria.\n\nEssas são regras verificadas no software de origem, não validação de enquadramento tributário. Conferir os dados e a versão utilizados na migração e adaptar cálculos monetários ao contrato inteiro em centavos do ERP Next.\n\n## 17. Lista de pedidos — captura adicional 032924\n\nA captura “Captura de tela 2026-11-05 032924.png”, recebida durante a auditoria, acrescenta a lista de pedidos e eleva o total atual a 23 anexos.\n\nRequisitos visíveis:\n\n* Ação Novo pedido e identificação do escopo “pedidos de toda a equipe”.\n* Indicadores: valor e quantidade em aberto; valor e quantidade fechados no mês; taxa de fechamento sobre fechados e perdidos; desconto médio nos pedidos fechados.\n* Mostrar o período de referência e distinguir mês atual de consultas de todos os períodos.\n* Indicadores expansíveis/recolhíveis, preservando os números essenciais na visão compacta.\n* Abas com contagem: Em aberto, Com aprovação, Fechados (todos os períodos), Perdidos e Todos.\n* Busca por cliente, CPF/CNPJ ou número do pedido.\n* Lista com cliente, número/identificação, resumo de itens/quantidades, vendedor e desconto.\n* Abrir pedido pelo cliente/título.\n* Ordenação pelo cabeçalho, reordenação e ajuste da largura das colunas conforme a referência; garantir alternativa acessível e uso no celular.\n* Tratar cliente ainda não vinculado, mostrado como “sem cliente” no legado, sem criar um cliente fictício. O ERP Next hoje exige customerId para criar pedido; mapear essa diferença entre simulação, oportunidade e pedido formal.\n* A imagem possui rolagem horizontal; colunas fora do enquadramento não foram especificadas nem inferidas.\n\nComparação com ERP Next: orders.tsx:105 apresenta busca por número/cliente/CPF-CNPJ, total, paginação e colunas Pedido, Cliente, Situação, Vencimento e Valor. Não apresenta os indicadores e abas comerciais acima, vendedor/desconto, nem personalização das colunas. As situações atuais são draft, confirmed, completed e cancelled; não considerar confirmed/completed equivalentes automáticos de aprovado/fechado sem contrato de estados.\n\nAceite:\n\n- [ ] Lista e indicadores reconciliam os valores/pedidos do mesmo escopo, empresa e período.\n- [ ] Pedidos aguardando aprovação e perdidos são distinguíveis e consultáveis.\n- [ ] Taxa de fechamento e desconto médio têm denominadores definidos, estado vazio e precisão verificados.\n- [ ] Ordenação/personalização das colunas funciona com teclado e não impede uso em telas pequenas.\n- [ ] Conferência inclui esta referência e todas as imagens anteriores; total atual de 23 anexos.\n\n## 19.     export async function installFrontendFixture(context: BrowserContext, fixtureOrigin = origin, fixtureTenant = tenant, fixtureAccessToken = "frontend-integration-fixture") {
      const iv = randomBytes(12)
      const cipher = createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", createHash("sha256").update(secret).digest(), iv)
      cipher.setAAD(Buffer.from("erp-session"))
      const data = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(JSON.stringify({ accessToken: fixtureAccessToken, tenantId: fixtureTenant, expiresAt: Date.now() + 3600_000 })), cipher.final()])
      const secure = fixtureOrigin.startsWith("https:")
      await context.addCookies([{ name: secure ? "__Host-erp_session" : "erp_session", value: Buffer.concat([iv, cipher.getAuthTag(), data]).toString("base64url"), url: fixtureOrigin, secure, httpOnly: true, sameSite: "Lax" }])
      await context.route("**/api/erp/**", route => route.fulfill({ status: route.request().method() === "GET" ? 503 : 405, json: { title: "Operação indisponível na fixture de leitura" } }))
    }

              tar -C "$bundle_dir" -czf - . | ssh -T \

    # ERP Next em produção
    
    ## CI e publicação
    
    O workflow `CI` valida PRs pelo escopo alterado: lint e testes de modelo da web,
    formatação e testes Rust com PostgreSQL para API/migrations e testes npm do motor
    fiscal. O check obrigatório continua sendo `gate`; skips só são aceitos quando o
    planejador exclui explicitamente o componente, e o artefato registra esse escopo.
    Mudanças em infraestrutura desconhecida executam os três componentes. Não há
    segunda execução de CI no push para `main`.
    
    `CI full regression` conserva arquitetura, contratos, baseline, builds e browsers
    para execução manual ou semanal (segunda-feira, 04:23 UTC). O auto merge verifica
    a evidência do PR e não inicia publicação. Deploy e migrations seguem o procedimento
    direto no servidor; `Production release` permanece disponível apenas manualmente.
    
    ## Publicação direta
    
    O fluxo operacional é compilar na máquina de desenvolvimento, testar o trecho
    alterado e enviar o pacote pronto por SSH. O servidor aplica a versão e as
    migrações pendentes diretamente, sem aguardar o workflow completo. Não compilar
    no servidor de aplicações: ele compartilha memória com outros serviços.
    
    No Windows, a API Linux pode ser gerada localmente com `cargo-zigbuild` e Zig:
    `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.36 --locked -p erp-next-api`.
    Reutilize o cache de `target`; limite `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1` em máquinas com pouca
    memória. Para a web, use `ERP_BUILD_CPUS=2` e `pnpm --filter web build`. A variável
    limita os workers do build sem mudar o layout ou a configuração da aplicação.
    
    Identifique o commit e os hashes dos pacotes. Preserve as dependências Linux das
    imagens de runtime e substitua somente o executável da API ou o build da web
    quando as dependências não mudarem. Uma mudança de dependências exige imagem
    compatível reconstruída e validada. Registre quais componentes foram atualizados.
    
    Antes das migrações, preserve um backup do schema e confira os arquivos/checksums
    contra `_sqlx_migrations`. Execute somente `erp-next-api migrate`, usando as
    migrações da mesma revisão da API. O SQLx aplica apenas as pendentes. Bootstrap e
    importação do legado são operações de provisionamento e não fazem parte de uma
    publicação normal. Não os repita.
    
    Crie um diretório de release separado, copie a configuração privada da versão
    ativa e altere somente as imagens dos componentes atualizados e a revisão.
    Valide o Compose antes de iniciar. Preserve a versão anterior para rollback.
    Após a troca, confira a API, o domínio público, a revisão publicada e os serviços
    fiscais. Se a API for recriada, recrie os quatro serviços juntos, como descrito
    abaixo, porque compartilham seu namespace de rede.
    
    O workflow manual `production-release.yml` continua disponível como alternativa
    para empacotamento completo no runner. Ele não é disparado por push nem por auto
    merge. O antigo fluxo `production-migrate.yml` permanece apenas para as operações
    manuais de provisionamento já existentes; não é necessário para publicar.
    
    O bootstrap cria uma empresa com cadastro fiscal pendente e associa a identidade
    real confirmada de `nicolas@avilaops.com` ao papel de administrador. O banco é
    independente do legado e recebe a cópia e projeção dos dados após o bootstrap.
    A conexão de runtime usa papel sem superusuário,
    sem BYPASSRLS e sem propriedade das tabelas.
    
    O diretório de release recebe somente `compose.yaml`, imagens prontas e arquivos
    privados `api.env`, `web.env` e `.env`. `api.env` contém `DATABASE_URL`,
    `AUTH_ISSUER=https://auth.avilaops.com`, `NFE_PRODUCTION_ENABLED=false` e
    `NFE_PRODUCTION_TENANT_ID` vazio. Se a emissão de produção for liberada para
    uma única empresa, as duas variáveis devem ser ativadas juntas e o UUID do
    tenant autorizado deve ser informado; não existe liberação global segura.
    Nos releases `compose.json` que usam `network_mode: service:api`, uma recriação
    da API exige recriar também `web`, `fiscal-engine` e `fiscal-mcp`, para que todos
    usem a rede da nova API. Recrie os quatro serviços juntos. Depois confira o
    `/api/health` público, a prontidão da API e a resposta do `/mcp`; o estado

    use anyhow::Context;
    use config::Config;
    use platform::auth::AuthClient;
    use platform::state::AppState;
    use sqlx::postgres::PgPoolOptions;
    use tokio::net::TcpListener;
    use tracing::info;
    
    #[tokio::main]
    async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        if std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() == Some("openapi") {
            serde_json::to_writer_pretty(std::io::stdout().lock(), &http::openapi::value())?;
            return Ok(());
        }
        init_tracing();
        platform::langfuse::init();
        let result = run().await;
        platform::langfuse::shutdown().await;
        result
    }
    
    async fn run() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let config = Config::from_env()?;
        let pool = PgPoolOptions::new()
            .max_connections(config.database_max_connections)
            .connect(&config.database_url)
            .await
            .context("failed to connect to PostgreSQL")?;
    
        match std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() {
            Some("migrate") => {
                sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations")
                    .run(&pool)
                    .await
                    .context("failed to apply database migrations")?;
                info!("database migrations applied");
                return Ok(());
            }
            Some(_) => anyhow::bail!("usage: erp-next-api [migrate]"),
            None => {}
        }
    
        let listener = TcpListener::bind(config.bind_address)
            .await
            .context("failed to bind HTTP listener")?;
        let local_address = listener.local_addr()?;
        let auth = AuthClient::new(config.auth_userinfo_url);
        let mut state = AppState::new(pool, auth)
            .with_ibpt(domains::fiscal::ibpt::IbptCatalog::from_env()?)
            .with_registry(domains::registry_lookup::RegistryClient::new(
                std::env::var("ERP_CNPJ_WS_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("true"),
            )?)
            .with_subscriptions(platform::subscriptions::provider::MercadoPago::from_env()?)
            .with_fiscal_engine(domains::fiscal::engine_client::FiscalEngine::from_env()?)

    REVISIONS = {'9c95acbc-cdd0-d010-0dac-18943ecd52f9': 1, '0552be89-b040-0d19-d51d-176c4b3577f4': 2, 'a4e2b4f5-4f58-7ffc-ac7a-277414644c88': 1}
    SOURCES = {'15508514': ('Votuporanga', '3557105'), '15505058': ('Votuporanga', '3557105'), '15075170': ('São José do Rio Preto', '3549805'), '15085480': ('São José do Rio Preto', '3549805')}
    DIRECTORY = Path('/mnt/HC_Volume_106542212/erp-next/private/party-ibge-20261112')
    os.umask(0o077)
    DIRECTORY.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    assert DIRECTORY.resolve().parent == Path('/mnt/HC_Volume_106542212/erp-next/private').resolve()
    
    def psql(sql):
        result = subprocess.run(['sudo', '-n', '-u', 'postgres', 'psql', '-X', '-qAt', '-v', 'ON_ERROR_STOP=1', '-d', 'erp_next'], input=sql, text=True, capture_output=True)
        if result.returncode:
            (DIRECTORY/'last-error.log').write_text(result.stderr, encoding='utf-8')
            raise RuntimeError('Database operation refused; private diagnostic saved')
        return result.stdout.strip()
    
    def folded(value):
        return ''.join(char for char in unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', value.strip().casefold()) if not unicodedata.combining(char))
    
    ids = ','.join("'" + str(uuid.UUID(key)) + "'::uuid" for key in REVISIONS)
    rows = json.loads(psql(f"SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(p) || jsonb_build_object('_address_hash',md5(addresses::text)) ORDER BY id) FROM parties p WHERE tenant_id='{TENANT}'::uuid AND id IN ({ids});"))
    assert len(rows) == 3
    assert {row['id'] for row in rows} == set(REVISIONS)
    known = []
    for row in rows:
        for address in row['addresses']:
            cep = ''.join(char for char in address['postalCode'] if char.isdigit())
            assert cep in SOURCES and address['state'] == 'SP'
            city, code = SOURCES[cep]
            assert folded(address['city']) == folded(city)
            assert address.get('municipalityCode') in (None, '', code)
            known.append((cep, address.get('municipalityCode'), code))
    assert len(known) == 4 and {item[0] for item in known} == set(SOURCES)

      grep -q "^ERP_API_IMAGE=erp-next-api:sha-$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'API image was not pinned'
      grep -q "^ERP_WEB_IMAGE=erp-next-web:sha-$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'web image was not pinned'
      grep -q "^ERP_RELEASE_SHA=$source_sha$" "$release/.env" || fail 'release SHA was not pinned'
      compose_file=compose.yaml
      compose_overlay_args=(--file "$release/fiscal-compose.yaml")
      compose_env_args=(--env-file "$release/.env")
    fi
    
    compose() {
      docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$1" \
        "${compose_env_args[@]}" --file "$1/$compose_file" "${compose_overlay_args[@]}" "${@:2}"
    }
    
    rollback() {
      local status=$?
      trap - EXIT
      printf '%s\n' 'ERP deploy failed; restoring previous release' >&2
      if [[ -f "$previous_release/compose.json" ]]; then
        docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$previous_release" \
          --file "$previous_release/compose.json" up --detach --no-build --remove-orphans --wait --wait-timeout 120 || true
      else
        docker compose --project-name "$APPLICATION" --project-directory "$previous_release" \
          --env-file "$previous_release/.env" --file "$previous_release/compose.yaml" \
          --file "$previous_release/fiscal-compose.yaml" up --detach --no-build --remove-orphans --wait --wait-timeout 120 || true
      fi
      exit "$status"
    }
    
    trap rollback ERR
    compose "$release" config --quiet
    compose "$release" up --detach --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 120
    
    curl --fail --silent --show-error --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \
      http://127.0.0.1:3141/health/ready >/dev/null
    
    python3 - "$source_sha" <<'PY'

    name: Production release
    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          source_ref:
            description: Exact source commit to validate and package
            required: true
            type: string
          automatic:
            description: Skip deployment when main has moved past this release
            required: false
            default: false
            type: boolean
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    jobs:
      fiscal-mcp:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 15
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
          - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
            with:
              version: 0.12.24
          - run: uv sync --frozen --extra dev --python 3.12
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-mcp
          - run: node --test scripts/fiscal/test/deploy-config.test.mjs
          - run: uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest tests/test_fiscal_schema.py tests/test_simplified_danfe.py tests/test_nfe_assinatura.py
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-mcp
          - run: docker build -f apps/fiscal-mcp/Dockerfile -t erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} .
          - name: Exercise MCP in its restricted runtime container
            shell: bash
            run: |
              docker run --detach --name fiscal-mcp-smoke --network host --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=64m,mode=1777 --security-opt no-new-privileges:true --cap-drop ALL --memory 512m --pids-limit 128 -e XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/cache erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              trap 'docker rm -f fiscal-mcp-smoke >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
              cd apps/fiscal-mcp
              uv run --frozen --extra dev python scripts/smoke_runtime.py
          - run: docker save erp-next-fiscal-mcp:sha-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }} | gzip > fiscal-mcp-image.tar.gz
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: erp-fiscal-mcp-${{ inputs.source_ref || github.sha }}
              path: fiscal-mcp-image.tar.gz
              compression-level: 0

    # Acabamentos iguais aos catálogos, sem alterar o histórico
    
    ## Pedido e resultado esperado
    O usuário pediu as mesmas cores, nomes e amostras dos catálogos originais, em cadastro e fechamento de proposta/pedido/venda. Estrutura, braços e estofado são conjuntos distintos. Anilheiro possui somente a escolha de tipo: Standard, Olímpico ou Não se aplica conforme o produto; não existe cor de anilheiro válida na interface.
    
    Os campos atuais misturam upholsteryColors com “Braços”. Corrigir a semântica mantendo upholsteryColors/upholsteryColor para estofado e criando swingArmColors/swingArmColor para braços. armColors/armColor são aliases legados de cor de anilheiro e não podem mudar de significado.
    
    ## Contrato e histórico
    - Acrescentar swingArmColors opcional ao produto e swingArmColor opcional aos itens de simulação, proposta e pedido. Levar a seleção a leitura, gravação, conversões, snapshots e apresentação em documentos/contratos.
    - Acrescentar finishingPalette opcional ao produto, com referências explícitas dhz-hammerforce-pro ou dhz-sforce. Sem referência é válido; string vazia remove a referência; omissão na edição preserva. Não identificar fabricante ou paleta apenas por cor genérica.
    - Listas de cores seguem os limites existentes: até32 nomes únicos,1–60 caracteres, sem controle. Seleções devem pertencer às opções cadastradas para novos itens/escolhas.
    - Omissão de campo novo por clientes antigos preserva os dados na edição. Campos legados de anilheiro continuam independentes. Não reinterpretar Amarelo como Apple Green nem Preto genericamente como uma textura específica.
    - Escolhas históricas inalteradas continuam válidas ao editar quantidade/condições. Não recalcular ou reescrever snapshots antigos após atualizar o produto.
    - A configuração “estofado não configurável” não deve esconder nem apagar a escolha independente dos braços.
    - Manter autorização, isolamento de empresa, revisão, idempotência e preservação de fotos, preços, tributos, status e estoque.
    
    ## Fontes e apresentação
    Usar bytes originais dos rasters dos PDFs, com provenance e SHA, sem geração por IA ou aproximação de cor.     use axum::{
        Router,
        body::{Body, to_bytes},
        http::{Request, StatusCode},
    };
    use serde_json::{Value, json};
    use sqlx::PgPool;
    use tower::ServiceExt;
    use uuid::Uuid;
    
    const TENANT: &str = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111";
    const CUSTOMER: &str = "11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555";
    const PRODUCT: &str = "11111111-2222-4333-8444-666666666666";
    
    async fn call(
        router: &Router,
        method: &str,
        uri: &str,
        subject: &str,
        revision: Option<i64>,
        key: Option<Uuid>,
        body: Value,
    ) -> (StatusCode, Value) {
        let mut request = Request::builder()
            .method(method)
            .uri(uri)
            .header("x-tenant-id", TENANT)
            .header("content-type", "application/json");
        if !subject.is_empty() {
            request = request.header("authorization", format!("Bearer {subject}"));
        }
        if let Some(revision) = revision {
            request = request.header("if-match", format!("\"{revision}\""));
        }
        if let Some(key) = key {
            request = request.header("idempotency-key", key.to_string());
        }
        let result = router
            .clone()
            .oneshot(request.body(Body::from(body.to_string())).unwrap())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let status = result.status();
        let bytes = to_bytes(result.into_body(), 1_000_000).await.unwrap();
        (
            status,
            serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
        )
    }

    import assert from "node:assert/strict"
    import { test } from "node:test"
    import { getCatalogFinishPalette, catalogFinishGroups } from "../src/features/catalog/catalog-finish-palettes.ts"
    
    test("Pro keeps standard paint, signature paint and leather upholstery separate", () => {
     const pro = getCatalogFinishPalette("dhz-hammerforce-pro")
     assert.deepEqual(pro.structure.standard, ["Piano Black", "Matte Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red"])
     assert.deepEqual(pro.structure.special, ["Titanium Grey"])
     assert.deepEqual(pro.swingArm.standard, ["Piano Black", "Matte Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red", "Hermès Orange", "Apple Green"])
     assert.deepEqual(pro.swingArm.special, ["Titanium Grey", "Ocean Blue"])
     assert.deepEqual(pro.upholstery.standard, ["Black", "Saddle Brown", "Reddish Brown", "Mocha"])
     assert.deepEqual(pro.upholstery.special, [])
     assert.equal(pro.source.pdfPage, 51)
     assert.equal(pro.source.printedPage, 101)
    })
    
    test("SForce follows its own page, including Khaki upholstery and signature Titanium arms", () => {
     const sf = getCatalogFinishPalette("dhz-sforce")
     assert.deepEqual(sf.structure.standard, ["Piano Black", "Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red", "Titanium Grey"])
     assert.deepEqual(sf.swingArm.standard, ["Piano Black", "Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red", "Hermès Orange", "Apple Green", "Ocean Blue"])
     assert.deepEqual(sf.swingArm.special, ["Titanium Grey"])
     assert.deepEqual(sf.upholstery.standard, ["Black", "Saddle Brown", "Reddish Brown", "Khaki", "Mocha"])
     assert.notEqual(sf.source.asset, getCatalogFinishPalette("dhz-hammerforce-pro").source.asset)
     assert.equal(sf.source.pdfPage, 29)
    })
    
    test("unknown palettes and names are preserved as text rather than assigned another material", () => {
     for (const name of [undefined, null, "", "Cable Motion", "Preto", "dhz-hammerforce"]) assert.equal(getCatalogFinishPalette(name), undefined)
     const options = ["Piano Black", "Titanium Grey", "Amarelo", "Preto", "Ocean Blue"]
     assert.deepEqual(catalogFinishGroups("dhz-hammerforce-pro", "swingArm", options), {
      standard: ["Piano Black"], special: ["Titanium Grey", "Ocean Blue"], other: ["Amarelo", "Preto"],
     })
     assert.deepEqual(catalogFinishGroups(undefined, "upholstery", options), { standard: [], special: [], other: options })
     assert.deepEqual(options, ["Piano Black", "Titanium Grey", "Amarelo", "Preto", "Ocean Blue"])
    })
    
    test("paint names do not enter upholstery and a shortened graphite label keeps its original text", () => {
     assert.deepEqual(catalogFinishGroups("dhz-hammerforce-pro", "upholstery", ["Black", "Saddle Brown", "Apple Green", "Grafite"]), {
      standard: ["Black", "Saddle Brown"], special: [], other: ["Apple Green", "Grafite"],
     })
     assert.deepEqual(catalogFinishGroups("dhz-hammerforce-pro", "structure", ["Graphite Black", "Light Grey"]), {
      standard: ["Graphite Black", "Light Grey"], special: [], other: [],
     })
    })

    export type CatalogFinishPalette = "dhz-hammerforce-pro" | "dhz-sforce"
    export type CatalogFinishPart = "structure" | "swingArm" | "upholstery"
    type FinishOptions = { readonly standard: readonly string[]; readonly special: readonly string[] }
    export type CatalogFinishDefinition = Record<CatalogFinishPart, FinishOptions> & {
     readonly source: { readonly title: string; readonly asset: string; readonly pdfPage: number; readonly printedPage?: number }
    }
    
    // Transcribed from the original manufacturer pages; provenance travels with each raster.
    const palettes: Record<CatalogFinishPalette, CatalogFinishDefinition> = {
     "dhz-hammerforce-pro": {
      source: { title: "HammerForce Pro", asset: "/catalog/dhz-hammerforce-pro-original-colors.jpeg", pdfPage: 51, printedPage: 101 },
      structure: { standard: ["Piano Black", "Matte Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red"], special: ["Titanium Grey"] },
      swingArm: { standard: ["Piano Black", "Matte Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red", "Hermès Orange", "Apple Green"], special: ["Titanium Grey", "Ocean Blue"] },
      upholstery: { standard: ["Black", "Saddle Brown", "Reddish Brown", "Mocha"], special: [] },
     },
     "dhz-sforce": {
      source: { title: "Hammer S-FORCE", asset: "/catalog/dhz-s-force-original-colors.jpeg", pdfPage: 29 },
      structure: { standard: ["Piano Black", "Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red", "Titanium Grey"], special: [] },
      swingArm: { standard: ["Piano Black", "Graphite Black", "Light Grey", "Performance Red", "Hermès Orange", "Apple Green", "Ocean Blue"], special: ["Titanium Grey"] },
      upholstery: { standard: ["Black", "Saddle Brown", "Reddish Brown", "Khaki", "Mocha"], special: [] },
     },
    }
    
    export function getCatalogFinishPalette(value?: string | null): CatalogFinishDefinition | undefined {
     return value && Object.hasOwn(palettes, value) ? palettes[value as CatalogFinishPalette] : undefined
    }
    
    function colorKey(value: string, part: CatalogFinishPart) {
     const key = value.normalize("NFD").replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, "").toLowerCase().replace(/[\s-]+/g, "")
     // The supplier uses both graphite labels for paint; this does not translate generic fabrics or colors.
     return part !== "upholstery" && key === "mattegraphiteblack" ? "graphiteblack" : key
    }
    
    export function catalogFinishGroups(reference: string | null | undefined, part: CatalogFinishPart, available?: readonly string[] | null) {
     const options = [...(available ?? [])]
     const palette = getCatalogFinishPalette(reference)
     if (!palette) return { standard: [], special: [], other: options }
     const standard = new Set(palette[part].standard.map(name => colorKey(name, part)))
     const special = new Set(palette[part].special.map(name => colorKey(name, part)))
     return {
      standard: options.filter(name => standard.has(colorKey(name, part))),
      special: options.filter(name => !standard.has(colorKey(name, part)) && special.has(colorKey(name, part))),
      other: options.filter(name => !standard.has(colorKey(name, part)) && !special.has(colorKey(name, part))),
     }
