    # Listagens compartilhadas e ordenação — Implementation Plan
    
    > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans task-by-task. Use dispatching-parallel-agents only for independent files/domains after shared interfaces are defined.
    
    **Goal:** Padronizar as listagens e ordenar o conjunto completo antes da paginação, com integração e publicação verificadas.
    
    **Architecture:** Componentes próprios e controle compartilhado da ordenação na URL. SQL com allowlists por endpoint e collation pt-BR; comparação tipada somente para coleções completas. Sem biblioteca nova e sem alteração de regras comerciais.
    
    **Tech Stack:** Rust/Axum/sqlx/PostgreSQL18; React/Next16.4.3/TypeScript; Node, Playwright e SQLx.
    
    **Spec:** [Inventário e decisões](../specs/2026-11-13-shared-record-lists.md).
    
    ## Global constraints
    
    - Não alterar permissões, dados comerciais, impostos, descontos ou sequência de documentos.
    - Preservar q/filtros/offset/limit e parâmetros de navegação não relacionados.
    - Nulos no fim, desempate único, texto pt-BR, dinheiro/data/número tipados.
    - Nenhuma ordenação local de registros parcialmente carregados.
    - Não modificar o checkout original, que contém trabalho independente em andamento.
    
    ## Review focus
    
    - Requisições antigas sem sort preservam o padrão, inclusive consumidores auxiliares dos Query compartilhados.
    - Filtros e sort sobrevivem a busca, paginação, detalhe/voltar e reset sem apagar seleção comercial.
    - SQL não usa campos arbitrários; ordenação por valores exibidos e não aliases textuais de dinheiro/data.
    - Estado vazio preserva estrutura e permissões; erros não são apresentados como ausência de cadastro.
    - Cabeçalhos e preços continuam legíveis no mobile, rolagem somente no container e teclado utilizável.
    
    ## 1. Fundação de ordenação e layout
    
    Files: criar `apps/api/src/domains/list_sort.rs`, migração de collation; expor em domains/mod.rs. Criar `apps/web/src/components/workspace/list-layout.tsx`, `table-sort-model.ts`, `use-table-sort.ts`, aprimorar `data-table.tsx` e workspace-ui.css conforme necessário.
    
    Interfaces backend: `SortField::text(name, expression)` e `SortField::typed(name, expression)` com constantes estáticas; `order_by(sort_by: Option<&str>, sort_order: Option<&str>, fields: &[SortField], default: &str, unique: &str) -> Result<String, DomainError>`. Retorna cláusula ORDER BY completa. Ausência de ambos preserva default; field informado sem direção usa asc; direção sem field, campo ou direção inválidos são recusados. Valores são sempre binds; apenas expressões allowlisted entram na cláusula.
    
    Interfaces frontend: `TableSort { by: string; order: 'asc'|'desc'; explicit: boolean }`; `readTableSort(params, allowed, initial)`, `nextTableSort(state, field)`, `sortTableRows<T>(rows, sort, accessors, key)` com valores string/number/bigint/Date/null e nulos por último. `useTableSort(allowed, initial, prefix?)` retorna `{sort, toggle, query}`; query usa sortBy/sortOrder canônicos quando explícitos, toggle preserva toda URL e offset. `SortableTableHeader` recebe `{field, sort, onSort, children, className}`.
    
    `EntityListPage` recebe `{title, description?, actions?, toolbar?, summary?, footer?, children, className?}`. `SearchToolbar` recebe `{onSubmit, onClear?, canClear?, pending?, children, className?}`, inclui Buscar/Limpar. `FilterField` contém label/children. `StatusBadge` recebe children/tone. `EmptyState` recebe filtered/title?/description?/action?. `ResponsiveTable` recebe label/children/className?. `CurrencyCell` preserva td nativo, children já formatados e nowrap/alinhamento à direita.

    # Listagens compartilhadas e ordenação por cabeçalho
    
    Implementa os dois pedidos de 12/11: ordenação das tabelas como no Explorer e padronização estrutural das listagens. A implementação e publicação já foram solicitadas explicitamente. O objetivo geral antigo permanece pausado; custos nacionais, importações e outros dados não fazem parte deste trabalho.
    
    ## Inventário antes da refatoração
    
    O repositório usa React/Next 16.4.3, componentes próprios e PostgreSQL 18. Não usa TanStack Table. `DataTable` apenas preserva a tabela nativa; existem `PageHeader`, `Pagination`, `Button`, `SearchInput` e `RequestError`. Os demais padrões de listagem se repetem em cada feature. `workspace-ui.css` já contém tokens de espaçamento, controles e `.workspace-list-scroll`.
    
    | Família / arquivo em features | Consulta e paginação | Migração |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | catalog/catalog-workspace | products, servidor, 10/25/50/100 | Cabeçalho, busca, filtros, vazio, tabela e ordenação global |
    | parties/party-workspace; staff/staff-workspace | parties/staff, servidor25 | Mesmo padrão, mantendo formulários e permissões |
    | records/reference/reference-workspace | 8 cadastros, servidor25 | Uma migração cobre depósitos, categorias, contas, formas de pagamento, grupos e tags |
    | price-lists/price-lists-workspace | price-lists, servidor25; detalhe completo | Título ausente, criar no cabeçalho; ordenação global da lista e local no detalhe somente de leitura |
    | sales/proposals; sales/orders | proposals/orders, servidor25 | Cabeçalho, card, limpar, status, dinheiro e ordenação global |
    | sales/sales-pipeline | opportunities, servidor25 | Preservar resumo e etapas; integrar lista e ações |
    | sales/sales-workspace | proposals/orders limit5 | Preservar painel; subseções com tabelas resumidas e ações |
    | sales/commercial-table | commercial/tables, array completo, recorte14 local | P0: ordenar todo o resultado filtrado antes do recorte; dinheiro sem quebra e rolagem contida |
    | commercial-settings/price-tables | tabelas publicada/prévia completas | P0: mesma geometria e valores sem quebra; ordenar localmente |
    | finance/receivables; purchasing/payables; purchasing/purchase-list | servidor25 | Busca, status, vazio, paginação e valores tipados |
    | inventory/stock-workspace | stock, servidor25 | Produto, saldo, reservado e disponível ordenados globalmente |
    | fiscal/outgoing-xml-imports | outgoing-imports, servidor25 | Ordenação antes da paginação |
    | fiscal/outgoing-nfes | carrega todas as páginas cursor e combina localmente | Ordenar a coleção completa, sem modificar a semântica dos cursores da API |
    | pos/point-of-sale; pos/cash-history | products15; sessions/sales20, servidor | Ordenação global nas tabelas paginadas |
    | pos/cash-closing | movimentos completos no detalhe | Ordenação local dos movimentos, valores e datas tipados |
    | company/account/account-panels | provedor externo, páginas10 | Auditar e padronizar apresentação; sem cabeçalho ordenável enquanto o provedor não oferecer ordenação global |
    
    Não são listagens de registros reordenáveis: documentos para impressão, linhas de proposta/pedido/NF-e com sequência comercial, recibo, prévia de importação CSV, itens selecionados do simulador, editor indexado de itens de lista de preços e matriz de parâmetros por UF. Não mudar a sequência desses dados. Produção, logística, comissões, folha, auditoria e várias telas administrativas usam cartões ou histórico sem cabeçalhos de tabela; registrar essa forma no inventário, reutilizar componentes adequados sem convertê-las artificialmente em tabelas.
    
    Nenhuma tela prioritária de cadastro tem um PageHeader externo autenticado. Seus títulos h2 estão nos componentes. Propostas e listas de preços não têm título visível. Substituir esses blocos pelo cabeçalho compartilhado; não duplicar títulos. Estados de acesso negado ficam nos componentes de acesso.
    
    ## Decisões
    
    - Reutilizar os componentes próprios. Uma biblioteca adicional não resolve o contrato de paginação e duplicaria a estrutura existente.
    - `EntityListPage` reúne cabeçalho/ação, card, toolbar, resumo, tabela e paginação por slots; o domínio continua responsável por dados, permissões e regras. `SearchToolbar`, `FilterField`, `StatusBadge`, `EmptyState`, `ResponsiveTable`, `CurrencyCell` e `SortableTableHeader` concentram os padrões ausentes. Reutilizar Button e PageHeader.
    - Cabeçalhos nativos th/button, aria-sort, ↑/↓ em espaço reservado, foco e teclado nativos. Primeira seleção explícita é asc; segunda é desc. Manter a ordenação inicial de cada tela.
    - Estado na URL `sortBy`/`sortOrder`; preservar parâmetros não relacionados, filtros, offset, limite, destino e seleção de equipamentos. Navegação sem recarga completa. Busca/filtro mantém o comportamento atual de voltar à primeira página, preservando a ordenação.
    - Ordenação do servidor usa expressões estáticas por endpoint, nunca nomes recebidos na SQL. Texto usa collation ICU pt-BR, sem diferenças de caixa/acentos e com números naturais. Valores monetários, números e datas usam tipos do banco. Nulos no fim em ambas as direções e desempate por chave única.
    - Listas completas usam comparador tipado compartilhado com Intl.Collator pt-BR e useMemo, antes de qualquer slice. Nenhuma ordenação local de uma página parcial.
    - Ordenar situação pelo texto apresentado ao usuário, não pela grafia interna do enum. Preservar os filtros e o isolamento por empresa.
    - Tabela de preços: largura mínima legível, nomes/SKU em hierarquia própria, valores alinhados à direita e indivisíveis; rolagem somente em ResponsiveTable. Ações e avisos secundários não comprimem preços.
    - O vazio mantém o cabeçalho e a geometria da lista. Distinguir ausência de cadastro, filtros sem resultado e erro. Criação contextual depende da permissão existente.
    
    ## Verificação
    
    375/768/1024/1440px, teclado, setas/aria-sort, ausência de overflow na página, dinheiro sem quebra, pesquisa/filtros/offset/limite e Voltar/Avançar/reload. Integração PostgreSQL com mais de uma página, 160 produtos, acentos, nulos, empate, datas e valores 2/10/100; campo/direção inválidos e tentativas de injeção recusados. Os testes existentes de layout que contradizem o pedido novo devem ser atualizados preservando as verificações de negócio.
    
    Fonte técnica para collation: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/collation.html. Confirmar ICU no banco de testes e de produção antes da migração. A publicação deve executar migrações antes da ativação e manter as verificações existentes.

    name: executing-plans
    description: Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available
    ---
    
    # Executing Plans
    
    Execute the plan yourself, task by task, in this session: no implementer
    subagent per task, no reviewer per task. One fresh-context review of the
    whole branch at the end.
    
    **Why inline:** Subagent-driven development pays for a fresh implementer
    and a fresh reviewer on every task, each re-reading the codebase from zero.
    Inline execution pays for one context (yours) plus one reviewer at the end.
    What it gives up is a fresh context per task and a second pair of eyes per
    task. This skill keeps what those two things bought, by other means: the
    brief is the spec, the ledger is your memory, TDD is the per-task gate, and
    the final reviewer is the second pair of eyes.
    
    **Core principle:** The plan already did the thinking. Execute it exactly,
    prove each step with a test you watched fail and then pass, and leave a
    record that survives your own forgetting.
    
    **Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
    ledger and the tool results carry the record.
    
    **Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner
    between tasks. They chose inline execution to spend less, not to answer
    "should I continue?" after every task. Execute all tasks from the plan
    without stopping.
    
    **Rulings, not stalls.** Conflicts, ambiguities, plan defects — decide them.
    The spec is the binding authority, the plan is its argument, and your
    judgment settles what neither answers. Record every decision in the ledger
    as `Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`, and keep
    going. Deviating from the plan without a ledgered ruling is a decision made
    in secret.
    
    Four things stop you, and only these: an irreversible or destructive
    operation; a security-sensitive action; a side effect outside this worktree
    that norms say you ask about first (a merge, a push to a shared branch, a
    publish); and a plan so broken that every path forward is a guess. For
    those, stop and ask.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    - You have a plan from superpowers:writing-plans and your human partner
      chose inline execution at the handoff.
    - Your harness has no subagent tool (see the per-platform references in
      `../using-superpowers/references/`). Never fabricate a dispatch; run
      the plan here.
    - Tasks are mostly independent — the same precondition as
      superpowers:subagent-driven-development.
    
    A fully specified plan makes inline execution transcription plus testing:
    it runs well on a mid-tier session model, and the one place the most
    capable model earns its cost is the final review, which this skill
    dispatches separately. Tell your human partner so when they choose inline.
    
    Prefer superpowers:subagent-driven-development when your human partner
    wants a review gate on every task, or when the plan is long enough that
    its later tasks would run on a compacted context. Inline execution over a
    long plan still works — the ledger is what makes it recoverable — but the
    last tasks get the least of you.
    
    ## The Process
    
    ```dot
    digraph process {
        rankdir=TB;
    
        subgraph cluster_per_task {
            label="Per Task";
            "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief" [shape=box];
            "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output" [shape=box];
            "Step output matches plan's Expected?" [shape=diamond];
            "Plan wrong? Rule and ledger. Code wrong? systematic-debugging" [shape=box];
            "Commit as the plan's commit steps say" [shape=box];
            "Completion contract met?" [shape=diamond];
            "task-done: run tests, ledger the result; mark todo complete" [shape=box];
        }
    
        "Setup: worktree, workspace + ledger, read plan + spec, pre-flight scan" [shape=box];
        "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
        "Final whole-branch review (fresh reviewer if you have one)" [shape=box];
        "Re-grade, then: Critical/Important → ONE fix pass, each fix RED→GREEN + green suite; Minor → ledger" [shape=box];
        "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace" [shape=box];
        "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];
    
        "Setup: worktree, workspace + ledger, read plan + spec, pre-flight scan" -> "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief";
        "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief" -> "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output";
        "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output" -> "Step output matches plan's Expected?";
        "Step output matches plan's Expected?" -> "Plan wrong? Rule and ledger. Code wrong? systematic-debugging" [label="no"];
        "Plan wrong? Rule and ledger. Code wrong? systematic-debugging" -> "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output";
        "Step output matches plan's Expected?" -> "Commit as the plan's commit steps say" [label="yes, last step"];
        "Commit as the plan's commit steps say" -> "Completion contract met?";
        "Completion contract met?" -> "Work the steps in order: TDD, run every verification, read every output" [label="no - finish the task"];
        "Completion contract met?" -> "task-done: run tests, ledger the result; mark todo complete" [label="yes"];
        "task-done: run tests, ledger the result; mark todo complete" -> "More tasks remain?";
        "More tasks remain?" -> "task-start: brief + BASE; read the brief" [label="yes"];

        "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
    }
    ```
    
    ## Setup
    
    Ensure the work happens in an isolated workspace: use
    superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one.
    Never start implementation on a main/master branch without your human
    partner's explicit consent.
    
    Conversation memory does not survive compaction. An inline executor that
    loses its place re-implements tasks whose commits already exist — the same
    failure as a controller re-dispatching them, paid for in your own context.
    Track progress in a ledger file, not only in todos. Harness todos are a
    live view; the ledger is the record.
    
    The workspace and ledger are shared with superpowers:subagent-driven-development
    — same directory, same format — so a plan can change executors mid-flight
    and the new one resumes from the same ledger.
    
    - Each plan owns a workspace: at skill start, run
      `../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-workspace PLAN_FILE` — it
      prints the plan's git-ignored directory
      (`<repo-root>/.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/`), home to every
      artifact for THIS plan: ledger, briefs, review packages. Another plan's
      directory is never yours to read or write.
    - Check for this plan's ledger at `<workspace>/progress.md`. If its first
      line names your plan file, tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are
      DONE — do not redo them; resume at the first task without one. Their
      commits exist in git even when your context no longer remembers making
      them: after compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own
      recollection. A ledger whose first line names a different plan file is
      another plan's progress: leave it and start your own, fresh.
    - Create the ledger with its identity as the first line:
      `# SDD ledger — plan: <plan file path>`.
    - `git clean -fdx` will destroy the workspace (it's git-ignored scratch);
      if that happens, recover from `git log`.
    
    Read the plan once, note its context and Global Constraints, and create a
    todo per task. If the plan names a Spec, read that too: the spec is the
    authority the plan argues from, and conflicts inside the plan resolve
    against it. A plan with no reachable spec gets a ledger note saying so —
    rulings made without one are provisional.
    
    **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** load superpowers:test-driven-development now,
    before Task 1. It governs every step of every task below; a plan whose
    steps already say "write the failing test first" does not exempt you
    from reading it.
    
    Before Task 1, scan the plan for conflicts between tasks. The plan's

    ---
    name: subagent-driven-development
    description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
    ---
    
    # Subagent-Driven Development
    
    Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.
    
    **Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
    
    **Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration
    
    **Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
    ledger and the tool results carry the record.
    
    **Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are the four named below, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.
    
    **Rulings, not stalls.** A running plan does not wait on a human. Conflicts,
    ambiguities, plan defects, a cap you would have asked to exceed — decide
    them. The spec is the binding authority, the plan is its argument, and your
    judgment settles what neither answers. Record every decision in the ledger as
    `Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`, and keep
    going. A wrong ruling costs rework your human partner can see and undo; a
    session parked on a question costs their whole day and buys nothing.
    
    Four things stop you, and only these: an irreversible or destructive
    operation; a security-sensitive action; a side effect outside this worktree
    that norms say you ask about first (a merge, a push to a shared branch, a
    publish); and a plan so broken that every path forward is a guess. For those,
    stop and ask.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    ```dot
    digraph when_to_use {
        "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
        "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
        "Partner chose inline, or no subagent tool?" [shape=diamond];
        "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
        "executing-plans" [shape=box];
        "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];
    
        "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
        "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
        "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Partner chose inline, or no subagent tool?" [label="yes"];
        "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
        "Partner chose inline, or no subagent tool?" -> "executing-plans" [label="yes"];
        "Partner chose inline, or no subagent tool?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="no"];
    }
    ```
    
    **vs. Executing Plans (inline):**
    - Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution) instead of one context doing every task
    - Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality) instead of only at the end
    - Costs a fresh context per task and per review; inline costs one context plus one final reviewer
    - Both run in this session, share the same plan workspace and ledger, and never pause between tasks
    
    ## The Process
    
    ```dot
    digraph process {
        rankdir=TB;
    
        subgraph cluster_per_task {
            label="Per Task";
            "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
            "Implementer asks questions?" [shape=diamond];
            "Answer questions, provide context" [shape=box];
            "Implementer implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [shape=box];
            "Generate review package, dispatch task reviewer (./task-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
            "Spec ✅ and quality approved?" [shape=diamond];
            "Fix loop: read references/fix-loop.md before every round" [shape=box];
            "Append completion to ledger, mark todo complete" [shape=box];
        }
    
        "Setup: worktree, ledger check, read plan, pre-flight review" [shape=box];
        "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
        "Final review and finish: read references/final-review.md" [shape=box];
        "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace" [shape=box];
        "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];
    
        "Setup: worktree, ledger check, read plan, pre-flight review" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" -> "Implementer asks questions?";
        "Implementer asks questions?" -> "Answer questions, provide context" [label="yes"];
        "Answer questions, provide context" -> "Implementer implements, tests, commits, self-reviews";
        "Implementer asks questions?" -> "Implementer implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [label="no"];
        "Implementer implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Generate review package, dispatch task reviewer (./task-reviewer-prompt.md)";
        "Generate review package, dispatch task reviewer (./task-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec ✅ and quality approved?";
        "Spec ✅ and quality approved?" -> "Append completion to ledger, mark todo complete" [label="yes"];
        "Spec ✅ and quality approved?" -> "Fix loop: read references/fix-loop.md before every round" [label="no"];
        "Fix loop: read references/fix-loop.md before every round" -> "Append completion to ledger, mark todo complete" [label="addressed, or parked at the cap"];
        "Append completion to ledger, mark todo complete" -> "More tasks remain?";
        "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
        "More tasks remain?" -> "Final review and finish: read references/final-review.md" [label="no"];
        "Final review and finish: read references/final-review.md" -> "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace";
        "Final review clean: delete this plan's workspace" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
    }
    ```
    
    ## Setup
    
    Ensure the work happens in an isolated workspace: use
    superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one.
    Never start implementation on a main/master branch without your human
    partner's explicit consent.
    
    Conversation memory does not survive compaction. In real sessions,
    controllers that lost their place have re-dispatched entire completed task
    sequences — the single most expensive failure observed. Track progress in
    a ledger file, not only in todos.
    
    - Each plan owns a workspace: at skill start, run this skill's
      `bash scripts/sdd-workspace PLAN_FILE` — it prints the plan's git-ignored
      directory (under `<repo-root>/.superpowers/sdd/`), home to
      every artifact for THIS plan: ledger, briefs, reports, review packages.
      Another plan's directory is never yours to read or write.
    - Check for this plan's ledger at `<workspace>/progress.md`. If one exists,
      read [references/resuming.md](references/resuming.md) before anything
      else: it says whose ledger it is and where to resume.
    - Create the ledger with its identity as the first line:
      `# SDD ledger — plan: <plan file path>`.
    - The ledger is your recovery map: the commits it names exist in git even
      when your context no longer remembers creating them. After compaction,
      trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
    - `git clean -fdx` will destroy the workspace (it's git-ignored scratch); if
      that happens, recover from `git log`.
    
    Read the plan once, note its context and Global Constraints, and create a
    todo per task. If the plan names a Spec, read that too: the spec is the
    authority the plan argues from, and conflicts inside the plan resolve
    against it. A plan with no reachable spec gets a ledger note saying so —
    rulings made without one are provisional.
    
    Before dispatching Task 1, read [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md)
    and run the conflict scan it describes. Its table and rulings go in the
    ledger.
    
    ## Model Selection
    
    Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.
    
    **Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.
    
    **Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.
    
    **Architecture and design tasks**: use the most capable available model.
    The final whole-branch review is one of these — dispatch it on the most
    capable available model, not the session default.

    # The Pre-flight Scan
    
    Part of superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Run it once, before
    dispatching Task 1.
    
    Before dispatching Task 1, scan the plan once for conflicts, writing down
    what you checked as you check it:
    
    - tasks that contradict each other or the plan's Global Constraints
    - anything the plan explicitly mandates that the review rubric treats as a
      defect (a test that asserts nothing, verbatim duplication of a logic block)
    
    The scan's output is a table, not a verdict. One row for every pair of tasks
    that share a file or an interface: the two tasks, what one produces against
    what the other consumes, and what you found. One row for every task: whether
    its own text agrees with itself — the tests it specifies against the code it
    specifies, the files it creates against the files it later touches. "The scan
    is clean" without those rows is not a scan you ran.
    
    Write the table to the ledger. Rule on everything you find before execution
    begins — each finding against the plan text that mandates it — and record
    each ruling in the ledger. If the scan is clean, proceed without comment.
    Rule on each conflict it surfaces — the spec is the binding authority, the
    plan is its argument — record the ruling beside its row, and dispatch
    Task 1. The review loop remains the net for conflicts that only emerge from
    implementation.

                  <td className="hidden text-right tabular-nums lg:table-cell">{amount(item.freeDiscountPriceWithIpiCents)}</td>
                  <td className="hidden text-right tabular-nums lg:table-cell">{discount(item.maxOwnDiscountBps)}</td>
                  <td className="hidden text-right font-medium tabular-nums lg:table-cell">{amount(item.minOwnPriceWithIpiCents)}</td>
                  <td className="hidden lg:table-cell"><div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-1">{actions}</div></td>
                </tr>
              })}</tbody>
            </DataTable>

        </>}
      </main>
    }
    "use client"
    
    import { useState } from "react"
    import { PageHeader } from "@/components/page-header"
    import { DataTable } from "@/components/workspace/data-table"
    import Link from "next/link"
    import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
    import { RequestError } from "@/components/feedback/session-recovery"
    import { useCommand, useResource } from "@/hooks/use-operation"
    import { useNavigationGuard } from "@/components/shell/navigation-guard"
    
    type Item = { productId: string; sku: string; name: string; priceWithoutIpiCents: number; ipiBps: number; priceWithIpiCents: number }
    type Preview = { tenantId: string; line: string; revision: number; digest: string; items: Item[] }
    type Current = { tenantId: string; line: string; data: { version: number; publishedAt: string; items: Item[] } | null }
    const money = (cents: number) => (cents / 100).toLocaleString("pt-BR", { style: "currency", currency: "BRL" })
    
    export function PriceTables({ initialLine = "imported" }: { initialLine?: "imported" | "national" }) {
      const [line, setLine] = useState<"imported" | "national">(initialLine)
      const [locked, setLocked] = useState(false)
      return <main className="mx-auto min-w-0 max-w-5xl space-y-3 px-4 pb-12 pt-4 [--workspace-control-height:2.25rem]">
        <PageHeader eyebrow="Vendas / Tabelas de preços" title="Nova tabela de preços" description="Escolha a linha, confira os preços calculados e publique uma nova versão." />
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-3"><Link href="/vendas/simulador" className="text-primary underline">Simular negociação</Link><Link href="/preferencias/comercial" className="text-primary underline">Parâmetros comerciais</Link><Link href="/preferencias/despesas-fixas" className="text-primary underline">Despesas fixas</Link></div>
        <label className="grid max-w-xs gap-1">Linha comercial<select disabled={locked} className="min-h-10 rounded-lg border bg-background px-2" value={line} onChange={e => setLine(e.target.value as typeof line)}><option value="imported">Importada</option><option value="national">Nacional</option></select></label>
        <Publication key={line} line={line} onLocked={setLocked} />
      </main>
    }
    
    function Publication({ line, onLocked }: { line: "imported" | "national"; onLocked: (value: boolean) => void }) {
      const current = useResource<Current>(`/api/erp/price-tables/${line}`)
      const command = useCommand()
      const [preview, setPreview] = useState<Preview | null>(null)
      const [preparing, setPreparing] = useState(false)
      const [error, setError] = useState("")
      const [notice, setNotice] = useState("")
      useNavigationGuard(command.busy || command.uncertain ? "A publicação ainda não foi confirmada. Sair?" : null)
      async function prepare() {
        if (!current.value || preparing || command.busy || command.uncertain) return
        onLocked(true); setPreparing(true); setPreview(null); setError(""); setNotice(""); command.reset()
        try {
          const response = await fetch(`/api/erp/price-tables/${line}/preview`, { cache: "no-store" })
          const result = await response.json()
          if (!response.ok) throw Error(result.title || "Não foi possível preparar a tabela.")
          if (result.tenantId !== current.value.tenantId || result.line !== line || response.headers.get("etag") !== `"${result.revision}"` || !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(result.digest) || !Array.isArray(result.items) || !result.items.length) throw Error("Prévia incompleta. Recarregue antes de publicar.")
          setPreview(result)
        } catch (reason) { setError(reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : "Prévia indisponível.") }
        finally { setPreparing(false); onLocked(false) }
      }
      async function publish() {
        if (!preview || !current.value || command.busy) return
        onLocked(true)
        const result = await command.send<{ tenantId: string; line: string; status: string; version: number }>(`/api/erp/price-tables/${line}/publish`, current.value.tenantId, { digest: preview.digest }, `"${preview.revision}"`)
        if (result?.tenantId === current.value.tenantId && result.line === line && result.status === "published") {
          setNotice(`Versão ${result.version} publicada.`); setPreview(null); current.reload(); onLocked(false)
        } else if (result) { setError("Resposta divergente. Confira a versão publicada."); onLocked(false) }
      }
      return <div className="min-w-0 space-y-3">
        <p>Publicar cria uma versão da tabela com os custos dos produtos ativos e os parâmetros salvos. Produtos e pedidos existentes mantêm os preços cadastrados.</p>
        <Button variant="outline" disabled={!current.value || preparing || command.busy || command.uncertain} onClick={prepare}>{preparing ? "Preparando…" : "Preparar prévia"}</Button>
        {preview && <section className="form-section min-w-0 space-y-2"><h2 className="font-semibold">Conferência antes de publicar</h2><p>{preview.items.length} produtos · revisão {preview.revision}</p><Prices items={preview.items} /><Button disabled={command.busy || command.stale} onClick={publish}>{command.uncertain ? "Repetir confirmação" : "Confirmar publicação"}</Button></section>}
        {notice && <p role="status">{notice}</p>}{(error || command.error) && <p role="alert">{error || command.error}</p>}
        {command.stale && <p>Os dados mudaram. Prepare nova prévia e confira os valores.</p>}
        <section className="form-section min-w-0 space-y-2"><h2 className="font-semibold">Versão publicada</h2>{current.loading ? <p role="status">Carregando…</p> : current.error ? <p role="alert"><RequestError message={current.error} status={current.status} /></p> : current.value?.data ? <><p>Versão {current.value.data.version} · {new Date(current.value.data.publishedAt).toLocaleString("pt-BR")}</p><Prices items={current.value.data.items} /></> : <p>Nenhuma versão publicada nesta linha.</p>}</section>
      </div>
    }
    
    function Prices({ items }: { items: Item[] }) {
      return <div className="min-w-0 rounded-lg border"><DataTable aria-label="Produtos da tabela de preços" className="table-fixed [&_td]:px-2 [&_th]:px-2"><thead><tr><th scope="col" className="w-[54%] lg:w-[40%]">Equipamento</th><th scope="col" className="hidden text-right lg:table-cell lg:w-[22%]">Sem IPI</th><th scope="col" className="hidden text-right lg:table-cell lg:w-[10%]">IPI</th><th scope="col" className="w-[46%] text-right lg:w-[28%]">Com IPI</th></tr></thead><tbody>{items.map(item => <tr key={item.productId}>
        <th scope="row" className="text-left align-top font-normal [overflow-wrap:anywhere]"><span className="font-medium">{item.name}</span><p className="mt-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground">{item.sku}</p><p className="mt-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground lg:hidden">IPI <span>{(item.ipiBps / 100).toLocaleString("pt-BR")}%</span></p></th>
        <td className="hidden text-right tabular-nums [overflow-wrap:anywhere] lg:table-cell">{money(item.priceWithoutIpiCents)}</td><td className="hidden text-right lg:table-cell">{(item.ipiBps / 100).toLocaleString("pt-BR")}%</td>
        <td className="text-right align-top tabular-nums [overflow-wrap:anywhere]"><span className="font-semibold">{money(item.priceWithIpiCents)}</span><dl className="mt-2 text-xs lg:hidden"><dt className="text-muted-foreground">Sem IPI</dt><dd>{money(item.priceWithoutIpiCents)}</dd></dl></td>
      </tr>)}</tbody></DataTable></div>
    }
    
    ✓ • 679ms

    export type CommercialSelection = { productId: string; quantity: number }
    export type CommercialTableQuery = { line: "imported" | "national"; q: string; offset: number; destinationState: string; taxpayer: boolean; items: CommercialSelection[] }
    type TableLocation = Pick<CommercialTableQuery, "line" | "q" | "offset"> & Partial<Pick<CommercialTableQuery, "destinationState" | "taxpayer" | "items">>
    export const commercialTablePageSize = 14
    const states = new Set("AC AL AP AM BA CE DF ES GO MA MT MS MG PA PB PR PE PI RJ RN RS RO RR SC SP SE TO".split(" "))
    const uuid = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i
    
    export function readCommercialItems(value: string | null | undefined): CommercialSelection[] {
      if (!value || value.length > 4500) return []
      const entries = value.split(",")
      if (entries.length > 100) return []
      const seen = new Set<string>()
      const items: CommercialSelection[] = []
      for (const entry of entries) {
        const [id, quantity, extra] = entry.split(":")
        const productId = id.toLowerCase()
        if (!uuid.test(id) || extra !== undefined || !/^\d{1,7}$/.test(quantity || "") || Number(quantity) < 1 || Number(quantity) > 1_000_000 || seen.has(productId)) return []
        seen.add(productId)
        items.push({ productId, quantity: Number(quantity) })
      }
      return items
    }
    
    export function readCommercialTableQuery(params: Pick<URLSearchParams, "get">): CommercialTableQuery {
      const raw = params.get("offset") || "0"
      const offset = /^\d{1,6}$/.test(raw) ? Number(raw) : 0
      const destination = (params.get("destinationState") || "").toUpperCase()
      return { line: params.get("linha") === "national" ? "national" : "imported", q: (params.get("q") || "").trim().slice(0, 160), offset: Math.floor(offset / commercialTablePageSize) * commercialTablePageSize, destinationState: states.has(destination) ? destination : "", taxpayer: params.get("taxpayer") === "true", items: readCommercialItems(params.get("itens")) }
    }
    
    export function commercialTableHref(query: TableLocation) {
      const params = new URLSearchParams()
      if (query.line === "national") params.set("linha", query.line)
      if (query.q) params.set("q", query.q)
      if (query.offset) params.set("offset", String(query.offset))
      if (query.destinationState) params.set("destinationState", query.destinationState)
      if (query.taxpayer) params.set("taxpayer", "true")
      if (query.items?.length) params.set("itens", query.items.map(item => `${item.productId}:${item.quantity}`).join(","))
      return `/vendas/tabela-precos${params.size ? `?${params}` : ""}`
    }
    
    export function commercialSimulationHref(query: CommercialTableQuery, product?: string) {
      const params = new URLSearchParams({ linha: query.line })
      if (product) params.set("produto", product)
      else if (query.items.length) params.set("itens", query.items.map(item => `${item.productId}:${item.quantity}`).join(","))
      if (query.destinationState) params.set("destinationState", query.destinationState)
      params.set("taxpayer", String(query.taxpayer))
      params.set("returnTo", commercialTableHref(query))
      return `/vendas/simulador?${params}`
    }
    
    export function commercialTableReturn(value: string | undefined, line: string) {
      const fallback = commercialTableHref({ line: line === "national" ? "national" : "imported", q: "", offset: 0 })
      if (!value?.startsWith("/vendas/tabela-precos")) return fallback
      try {
        const url = new URL(value, "https://erp.local")
        if (url.origin !== "https://erp.local" || url.pathname !== "/vendas/tabela-precos") return fallback
        return commercialTableHref(readCommercialTableQuery(url.searchParams))
      } catch { return fallback }
    }

    export type TableSort = { by: string; order: "asc" | "desc"; explicit: boolean }
    export type TableSortInitial = Pick<TableSort, "by" | "order">
    export type TableSortValue = string | number | bigint | Date | null | undefined
    
    function sortKeys(prefix: string) {
      return prefix ? [`${prefix}SortBy`, `${prefix}SortOrder`] as const : ["sortBy", "sortOrder"] as const
    }
    
    /** Invalid browser state falls back to the screen's original ordering. */
    export function readTableSort(params: Pick<URLSearchParams, "get">, allowed: readonly string[], initial: TableSortInitial, prefix = ""): TableSort {
      const [byKey, orderKey] = sortKeys(prefix)
      const by = params.get(byKey)
      const order = params.get(orderKey)
      if (!by || !allowed.includes(by) || (order !== null && order !== "asc" && order !== "desc")) return { ...initial, explicit: false }
      return { by, order: order ?? "asc", explicit: true }
    }
    
    export function nextTableSort(state: TableSort, field: string): TableSort {
      return { by: field, order: state.explicit && state.by === field && state.order === "asc" ? "desc" : "asc", explicit: true }
    }
    
    /** API requests always use canonical keys even when a dashboard scopes its URL keys. */
    export function tableSortQuery(sort: TableSort): URLSearchParams {
      return new URLSearchParams(sort.explicit ? { sortBy: sort.by, sortOrder: sort.order } : {})
    }
    
    /** Change only sorting, keeping filters, offsets, duplicate parameters and fragments. */
    export function tableSortHref(href: string, sort: TableSort, prefix = ""): string {
      const fragmentIndex = href.indexOf("#")
      const fragment = fragmentIndex < 0 ? "" : href.slice(fragmentIndex)
      const address = fragmentIndex < 0 ? href : href.slice(0, fragmentIndex)
      const queryIndex = address.indexOf("?")
      const path = queryIndex < 0 ? address : address.slice(0, queryIndex)
      const params = new URLSearchParams(queryIndex < 0 ? "" : address.slice(queryIndex + 1))
      const [byKey, orderKey] = sortKeys(prefix)
      if (sort.explicit) {
        params.set(byKey, sort.by)
        params.set(orderKey, sort.order)
      } else {
        params.delete(byKey)
        params.delete(orderKey)
      }
      const query = params.toString()
      return path + (query ? `?${query}` : "") + fragment
    }
    
    const textOrder = new Intl.Collator("pt-BR", { sensitivity: "base", numeric: true })
    
    function normalized(value: TableSortValue): string | number | bigint | null {
      if (value == null) return null
      const result = value instanceof Date ? value.getTime() : value
      return typeof result === "number" && !Number.isFinite(result) ? null : result
    }
    
    function compare(left: string | number | bigint, right: string | number | bigint): number {
      if (typeof left === "string" && typeof right === "string") return textOrder.compare(left, right)
      return left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0
    }
    
    /** Only use for complete collections; paginated server results must sort upstream. */
    export function sortTableRows<T>(rows: readonly T[], sort: TableSort, accessors: Readonly<Record<string, (row: T) => TableSortValue>>, getKey: (row: T) => string | number | bigint): T[] {
      const accessor = accessors[sort.by]
      if (!accessor) return [...rows]
      return [...rows].sort((left, right) => {
        const a = normalized(accessor(left))
        const b = normalized(accessor(right))
        if (a === null && b !== null) return 1
        if (a !== null && b === null) return -1
        const result = a === null || b === null ? 0 : compare(a, b)
        if (result) return sort.order === "desc" ? -result : result
        // Keep tie-breaking deterministic in both directions, including collator-equivalent IDs.
        const keyA = getKey(left)
        const keyB = getKey(right)
        return keyA < keyB ? -1 : keyA > keyB ? 1 : 0
      })
    }

    }
    
    /** Data, permissions, errors and pagination stay with the feature. */
    export function EntityListPage({ title, description, actions, toolbar, summary, footer, children, className }: EntityListPageProps) {
      return (
        <section className={cn("workspace-entity-list", className)}>
          <PageHeader title={title} description={description} actions={actions} />
          <div className="workspace-list-card">
            {toolbar && <div className="workspace-list-toolbar">{toolbar}</div>}
            {summary != null && <div className="workspace-list-summary">{summary}</div>}
            {children}
            {footer && <div className="workspace-list-footer">{footer}</div>}
          </div>
        </section>
      )
    }
    
    export function SearchToolbar({ onSubmit, onClear, canClear = false, pending = false, children, className }: { onSubmit: FormEventHandler<HTMLFormElement>; onClear?: () => void; canClear?: boolean; pending?: boolean; children: ReactNode; className?: string }) {
      return (
        <form onSubmit={onSubmit} role="search" aria-busy={pending || undefined} className={cn("workspace-search-toolbar", className)}>
          {children}
          <div className="workspace-search-actions">
            <Button type="submit" disabled={pending}>Buscar</Button>
            {onClear && <Button type="button" variant="outline" disabled={pending || !canClear} onClick={onClear}>Limpar</Button>}
          </div>
        </form>
      )
    }
    
    /** A wrapping label associates existing SearchInput/select controls without generated IDs. */
    export function FilterField({ label, children, className }: { label: string; children: ReactNode; className?: string }) {
      return <label className={cn("workspace-filter-field", className)}><span>{label}</span>{children}</label>
    }
    
    export type StatusTone = "neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info"
    
    export function StatusBadge({ children, tone = "neutral" }: { children: ReactNode; tone?: StatusTone }) {
      return <span className="workspace-status-badge" data-tone={tone}>{children}</span>
    }
    
    export function EmptyState({ filtered, title, description, action }: { filtered: boolean; title?: string; description?: string; action?: ReactNode }) {
      return (
        <div className="workspace-list-empty">
          <p className="font-medium text-foreground">{title ?? (filtered ? "Nenhum resultado encontrado" : "Nenhum registro cadastrado")}</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{description ?? (filtered ? "Revise a pesquisa ou limpe os filtros para ver os registros." : "Os registros cadastrados aparecerão aqui.")}</p>
          {action && <div className="workspace-list-empty-action">{action}</div>}
        </div>
      )
    }
    
    export function ResponsiveTable({ label, children, className }: { label: string; children: ReactNode; className?: string }) {
      return <div role="region" aria-label={label} tabIndex={0} className={cn("workspace-list-scroll workspace-responsive-table", className)}>{children}</div>
    }
    
    /** Accepts an already formatted value; monetary parsing belongs to the domain. */
    export function CurrencyCell({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<"td">) {
      return <td {...props} className={cn("workspace-currency-cell", className)} />
    }
    
    export function CurrencyValue({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<"span">) {
      return <span {...props} className={cn("workspace-currency-value", className)} />
    }

    use super::DomainError;
    
    /// SQL expressions are defined by each endpoint, never supplied by the caller.
    pub struct SortField {
        name: &'static str,
        expression: &'static str,
        text: bool,
    }
    
    impl SortField {
        pub const fn text(name: &'static str, expression: &'static str) -> Self {
            Self {
                name,
                expression,
                text: true,
            }
        }
    
        pub const fn typed(name: &'static str, expression: &'static str) -> Self {
            Self {
                name,
                expression,
                text: false,
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn order_by(
        sort_by: Option<&str>,
        sort_order: Option<&str>,
        fields: &[SortField],
        default: &str,
        unique: &str,
    ) -> Result<String, DomainError> {
        let Some(name) = sort_by else {
            return if sort_order.is_none() {
                Ok(format!("ORDER BY {default}"))
            } else {
                Err(DomainError::Invalid("Informe o campo da ordenação"))
            };
        };
        let direction = match sort_order.unwrap_or("asc") {
            "asc" => "ASC",
            "desc" => "DESC",
            _ => return Err(DomainError::Invalid("Direção de ordenação inválida")),
        };
        let field = fields
            .iter()
            .find(|field| field.name == name)
            .ok_or(DomainError::Invalid("Campo de ordenação inválido"))?;
        let expression = if field.text {
            format!("({}) COLLATE public.erp_pt_br_natural", field.expression)
        } else {
            field.expression.to_owned()
        };
        Ok(format!(
            "ORDER BY {expression} {direction} NULLS LAST, {unique} ASC"
        ))
    }

    "use client"
    
    import { usePathname, useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
    import { nextTableSort, readTableSort, tableSortHref, tableSortQuery, type TableSortInitial } from "./table-sort-model"
    
    export function useTableSort(allowed: readonly string[], initial: TableSortInitial, prefix = "") {
      const params = useSearchParams()
      const pathname = usePathname()
      const router = useRouter()
      const sort = readTableSort(params, allowed, initial, prefix)
      function toggle(field: string) {
        if (!allowed.includes(field)) return
        const href = pathname + (params.size ? `?${params}` : "") + window.location.hash
        router.push(tableSortHref(href, nextTableSort(sort, field), prefix), { scroll: false })
      }
      return { sort, toggle, query: tableSortQuery(sort) }
    }

    async function bounded(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, maximum: number) {
      const reader = stream?.getReader()
      const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []
      let size = 0
      if (reader) for (;;) {
        const { done, value } = await reader.read()
        if (done) break
        size += value.byteLength
        if (size > maximum) { await reader.cancel(); throw new RangeError("Document exceeds limit") }
        chunks.push(value)
      }
      return Buffer.concat(chunks)
    }

    "use client"
    
    import { useCallback, useMemo } from "react"
    import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
    import { nextTableSort, readTableSort, tableSortHref, tableSortQuery, type TableSortInitial } from "./table-sort-model"
    
    export function useTableSort(allowed: readonly string[], initial: TableSortInitial, prefix = "") {
      const params = useSearchParams()
      const router = useRouter()
      const { by, order, explicit } = readTableSort(params, allowed, initial, prefix)
      const sort = useMemo(() => ({ by, order, explicit }), [by, order, explicit])
      const query = useMemo(() => tableSortQuery(sort), [sort])
      const allowedSignature = JSON.stringify(allowed)
      const initialBy = initial.by, initialOrder = initial.order
      const toggle = useCallback((field: string) => {
        const fields: string[] = JSON.parse(allowedSignature)
        if (!fields.includes(field)) return
        const latest = readTableSort(new URLSearchParams(window.location.search), fields, { by: initialBy, order: initialOrder }, prefix)
        const href = window.location.pathname + window.location.search + window.location.hash
        router.push(tableSortHref(href, nextTableSort(latest, field), prefix), { scroll: false })
      }, [allowedSignature, initialBy, initialOrder, prefix, router])
      return { sort, toggle, query }
    }

    ---
    name: receiving-code-review
    description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
    ---
    
    # Code Review Reception
    
    ## Overview
    
    Code review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.
    
    **Core principle:** Verify before implementing. Ask before assuming. Technical correctness over social comfort.
    
    ## The Response Pattern
    
    ```
    WHEN receiving code review feedback:
    
    1. READ: Complete feedback without reacting
    2. UNDERSTAND: Restate requirement in own words (or ask)
    3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality
    4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?
    5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback
    6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each
    ```
    
    ## Forbidden Responses
    
    **NEVER:**
    - "You're absolutely right!" (explicit instruction-file violation)
    - "Great point!" / "Excellent feedback!" (performative)
    - "Let me implement that now" (before verification)
    
    **INSTEAD:**
    - Restate the technical requirement
    - Ask clarifying questions
    - Push back with technical reasoning if wrong
    - Just start working (actions > words)
    
    ## Handling Unclear Feedback
    
    ```
    IF any item is unclear:
      STOP - do not implement anything yet
      ASK for clarification on unclear items
    
    WHY: Items may be related. Partial understanding = wrong implementation.
    ```
    
    **Example:**
    ```
    your human partner: "Fix 1-6"
    You understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.
    
    ❌ WRONG: Implement 1,2,3,6 now, ask about 4,5 later
    ✅ RIGHT: "I understand items 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before proceeding."
    ```
    
    ## Source-Specific Handling
    
    ### From your human partner
    - **Trusted** - implement after understanding
    - **Still ask** if scope unclear
    - **No performative agreement**
    - **Skip to action** or technical acknowledgment
    
    ### From External Reviewers
    ```
    BEFORE implementing:
      1. Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase?
      2. Check: Breaks existing functionality?
      3. Check: Reason for current implementation?
      4. Check: Works on all platforms/versions?
      5. Check: Does reviewer understand full context?
    
    IF suggestion seems wrong:
      Push back with technical reasoning
    
    IF can't easily verify:
      Say so: "I can't verify this without [X]. Should I [investigate/ask/proceed]?"

    export const pipelineStages = { new: "Novo", contacted: "Contato feito", proposed: "Proposta enviada", negotiation: "Negociação", won: "Ganho", lost: "Perdido" }
    export type PipelineStage = keyof typeof pipelineStages
    export type PipelineQuery = { q: string; stage: PipelineStage | ""; offset: number }
    export const pipelinePageSize = 25
    
    export function readPipelineQuery(params: Pick<URLSearchParams, "get">): PipelineQuery {
      const q = Array.from((params.get("q") || "").replace(/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/g, " ").trim()).slice(0, 160).join("")
      const stage = params.get("stage") || ""
      const rawOffset = params.get("offset") || "0"
      const offset = /^\d{1,6}$/.test(rawOffset) && Number(rawOffset) <= 100000 ? Math.floor(Number(rawOffset) / pipelinePageSize) * pipelinePageSize : 0
      return { q, stage: Object.hasOwn(pipelineStages, stage) ? stage as PipelineStage : "", offset }
    }

        const unitInput = await page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Unidade", exact: true }).boundingBox()

    const listRoute = /^\/(?:cadastros\/[^/]+|estoque\/depositos|vendas\/(?:pedidos|propostas|funil)|compras\/pedidos|financeiro\/(?:contas-pagar|contas-receber)|servicos\/ordens)(?=\/|$)/
    
    /** Carry a list's URL through its records without changing unrelated navigation. */
    export function listNavigationHref(href: string, pathname: string, search: string) {
      const list = pathname.match(listRoute)?.[0]
      if (!list || !href.startsWith("/") || href.startsWith("//")) return href
      try {
        const target = new URL(href, "https://erp.local")
        const params = new URLSearchParams(search)
        const previous = params.get("returnTo")
        const source = pathname === list && search ? list + "?" + search : previous
        if (!source || !source.startsWith(list + "?")) return href
        const origin = new URL(source, "https://erp.local")
        if (origin.origin !== target.origin || origin.pathname !== list) return href
        if (target.pathname === list && !target.search) return list + origin.search + target.hash
        if (target.pathname.startsWith(list + "/") && !target.searchParams.has("returnTo")) {
          target.searchParams.set("returnTo", list + origin.search)
          return target.pathname + target.search + target.hash
        }
      } catch { return href }
      return href
    }

    export function useAllowNextUnload() {
      return useContext(NavigationGuardContext).allowNextUnload
    }
    
    export function useListNavigationHref() {
      const pathname = usePathname()
      const search = useSearchParams()
      return (href: string) => listNavigationHref(href, pathname, search.toString())
    }
    
    export function GuardedLink({ onNavigate, ...props }: ComponentProps<typeof NextLink>) {
      const confirmNavigation = useConfirmNavigation()
      const listHref = useListNavigationHref()
      const href = typeof props.href === "string" ? listHref(props.href) : props.href
      return <NextLink {...props} href={href} onNavigate={event => {
        if (!confirmNavigation()) { event.preventDefault(); return }
        onNavigate?.(event)
      }} />
    }

    $ $workflowCopiesRoot=(Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.github/workflows').Path
        $workflowSources=@(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $workflowCopiesRoot -File | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.yml','.yaml' })
        $workflowEncoding=[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
        $workflowCopies=foreach($workflowSource in $workflowSources) {
          $workflowTarget=Join-Path $workflowCopiesRoot ($workflowSource.BaseName+'.md')
          if(Test-Path -LiteralPath $workflowTarget){ throw ('Já existe: '+$workflowTarget) }
          $workflowOriginalHash=(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $workflowSource.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          $workflowRaw=[IO.File]::ReadAllText($workflowSource.FullName)
          $workflowTickRuns=@([regex]::Matches($workflowRaw,([string][char]96+'+')) | ForEach-Object { $_.Length })
          $workflowFenceLength=3
          if($workflowTickRuns.Count){$workflowFenceLength=[math]::Max(3,1+($workflowTickRuns | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum)}
          $workflowFence=[string]::new([char]96,$workflowFenceLength)
          $workflowPrefix='# '+$workflowSource.Name+"`n`n"+'Origem: ['+$workflowSource.Name+']('+$workflowSource.Name+").`n`n"+$workflowFence+"yaml`n"
          $workflowSeparator=if($workflowRaw.EndsWith("`n")){''}else{"`n"}
          $workflowMarkdown=$workflowPrefix+$workflowRaw+$workflowSeparator+$workflowFence+"`n"
          [IO.File]::WriteAllText($workflowTarget,$workflowMarkdown,$workflowEncoding)
          $workflowSaved=[IO.File]::ReadAllText($workflowTarget)
          if($workflowSaved.Substring($workflowPrefix.Length,$workflowRaw.Length) -cne $workflowRaw){throw ('Cópia divergente: '+$workflowTarget)}
          if((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $workflowSource.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $workflowOriginalHash){throw ('Original alterado: '+$workflowSource.Name)}
          [pscustomobject]@{Original=$workflowSource.Name;Copia=[IO.Path]::GetFileName($workflowTarget);Conteudo='Conferido'}
        }
        $workflowCopies | Format-Table -AutoSize
        Write-Output ('TOTAL='+$workflowCopies.Count)

    const a="11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111", b="22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222", c="33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333", d="44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444"
    const node = (id,name,parentId=null,sortOrder=0,status="active")=>({id,name,parentId,sortOrder,status})
    
    test("registry URLs bound pagination, reject invalid filters and keep each list's own roles",()=>{
     assert.deepEqual(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams("q= Casa &status=active&role=supplier&offset=49"),"party"),{q:"Casa",status:"active",role:"supplier",offset:25})
     assert.equal(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams("role=supplier"),"staff").role,"")
     assert.equal(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams("role=seller"),"staff").role,"seller")
     for(const offset of ["-25","Infinity","1e4","100001","999999999999","25abc"]) assert.equal(parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams({offset}),"reference").offset,0)
     const query=parseRegistryQuery(new URLSearchParams({q:"x".repeat(200),status:"invalid",role:"employee",offset:"100000"}),"reference")
     assert.equal(query.q.length,160); assert.equal(query.status,""); assert.equal(query.role,""); assert.equal(query.offset,100000)
     assert.equal(registryQueryString({q:"Casa & filial",status:"archived",role:"customer",offset:25}),"q=Casa+%26+filial&status=archived&role=customer&offset=25")
     assert.equal(registryQueryString({q:"",status:"",role:"",offset:0}),"")
    })
    
    test("category paths retain sibling order and prevent self/descendant parenting",()=>{
     const options=referenceHierarchy([node(c,"Série B",a,2),node(a,"Premium",null,1),node(b,"Core",null,0),node(d,"Série A",a,1)])
     assert.deepEqual(options.map(x=>x.path),["Core","Premium","Premium / Série A","Premium / Série B"])
     assert.equal(options.find(x=>x.id===d).depth,1)
     assert.deepEqual(availableParents(options,a).map(x=>x.id),[b])
     assert.deepEqual(availableParents(options,d).map(x=>x.id),[b,a,c])
    })
    
    test("invalid hierarchies fail visibly instead of losing or silently reparenting records",()=>{
     for(const nodes of [[node(a,"A",b)], [node(a,"A",b),node(b,"B",a)], [node(a,"A"),node(a,"Again")], [node(a,"A",a)]]) assert.throws(()=>referenceHierarchy(nodes))

    name: CI
    
    on:
      pull_request:
      workflow_dispatch:
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
    
    jobs:
      changes:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 2
        outputs:
          web: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.web }}
          api: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.api }}
          fiscal: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.fiscal }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              fetch-depth: 0
          - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts/ci -p 'test_*.py'
          - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts/deploy -p 'test_*.py'
          - id: scope
            env:
              BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || format('{0}^', github.sha) }}
            run: python3 -B scripts/ci/pr-gate.py plan
    
      web:
        needs: changes
        if: needs.changes.outputs.web == 'true'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
            with:
              version: 11.11.0
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
              cache: pnpm
              cache-dependency-path: pnpm-lock.yaml
          - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
          - run: pnpm --filter web lint
          - run: node --import ./tests/helpers/register-typescript.mjs --test tests/*-model.node.mjs
            working-directory: apps/web
    
      api:
        needs: changes
        if: needs.changes.outputs.api == 'true'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 20
        services:
          postgres:
            image: postgres:18-alpine
            env:
              POSTGRES_DB: erp_next_test
              POSTGRES_USER: postgres
              POSTGRES_PASSWORD: erp_next_ci_only
            ports:
              - 5432:5432
            options: >-
              --health-cmd "pg_isready -U postgres -d erp_next_test"
              --health-interval 2s
              --health-timeout 3s
              --health-retries 20
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:erp_next_ci_only@127.0.0.1:5432/erp_next_test
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.99.1
            with:
              components: rustfmt
          - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
            with:
              shared-key: pr-api
          - run: cargo fmt --all --check
          - run: cargo test --workspace --locked -- --test-threads=2
    
      fiscal:
        needs: changes
        if: needs.changes.outputs.fiscal == 'true'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 24
              cache: npm
              cache-dependency-path: apps/fiscal-engine/package-lock.json
          - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - run: npm test
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-engine
          - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
            with:
              version: 0.12.24
          - run: uv sync --frozen --extra dev --python 3.12
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-mcp
          - run: uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest tests/test_fiscal_schema.py tests/test_simplified_danfe.py tests/test_nfe_assinatura.py
            working-directory: apps/fiscal-mcp
    
      gate:
        needs: [changes, web, api, fiscal]
        if: always()
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 2
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Validate selected checks and record explicit skips
            env:
              SOURCE_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
              VALIDATION_JOBS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
            run: python3 -B scripts/ci/pr-gate.py gate artifacts/mlops/ci-attestation.json
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            if: always()
            with:
              name: erp-mlops-ci-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
              path: artifacts/mlops/ci-attestation.json
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 14

## Assistant

O [`ci.yml`](C:/Users/nicol/source/erp-next-main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) valida as alterações de cada PR. O [`ci-full.yml`](C:/Users/nicol/source/erp-next-main/.github/workflows/ci-full.yml) faz uma regressão mais abrangente.

| Aspecto | `ci.yml` | `ci-full.yml` |
|---|---|---|
| Execução | Automaticamente nas PRs ou manualmente | Manualmente ou semanalmente |
| Escopo | Seleciona os módulos afetados | Verifica o projeto inteiro |
| Frontend | Lint e testes de modelo | Também gera contratos, compila e testa no navegador |
| Rust | Formatação e testes | Também executa Clippy e verifica contratos |
| Outras verificações | Testes dos módulos selecionados | Arquitetura, compatibilidade da API, consumidores e sessões |

**Nenhum dos dois publica o sistema.** O deploy fica no `production-release.yml`.

Eu manteria os dois:

- **`ci.yml`** dá retorno mais rápido em cada PR, verificando o que foi afetado.
- **`ci-full.yml`** procura regressões entre módulos, com build, contratos e testes de navegador.

Ter dois arquivos não é obrigatório, mas essa separação faz sentido no ERP. O completo pode continuar semanal e manual, como está hoje.
